findings.title: ilink_bd_assault carries a second, drifting copy of iLinkman and IEEE1394_bd (about 3,500 lines) instead of building from modules/ilink
findings.problem: Every file under ilink_bd_assault/src/{IEEE1394_bd,iLinkman} is a near copy of modules/ilink: iLink_intr/TxRx/DMA/PHY differ only in the include path, iLink.c only in the chained BD_iLink_start call, sbp2_driver.c by 57 diff lines (it lacks sbp2FreeDevNr), scsi.c is the older SDK one (no READ(16), 12-byte CDB). ORIGIN.txt:18-20 says 'A change to one belongs in both', and the #1024 and October 22 fixes were applied twice; the copies already drift.
findings.fix: Build ilink_bd_assault.irx from modules/ilink/iLinkman/src and modules/ilink/IEEE1394_bd/src with one define (for example ILINK_BD_ASSAULT) that selects the static GetConsoleIDs, the chained _start/BD_iLink_start and no IRX_ID in IEEE1394_bd main.c, the malloc/free single definition, and skips bd->path for the older include/bdm.h; keep only Makefile, include/bdm.h, src/imports.lst and src/exports.tab here, then delete the copied trees and point the dual-copy tests at one source.
findings.justification: Adds roughly 30-40 lines of #ifdef in modules/ilink to remove about 3,800 duplicated lines; it ends the double maintenance that ORIGIN.txt:18-20 documents (the #1024, October 22 and November 2 changes were each written twice). The ifdefs must keep the deliberate differences: no device-number change for this copy (README.md:102-104), the cdvdman-free GetConsoleIDs and the chained _start. Whether the newer READ(16) path is wanted under POPSTARTER is untested.
findings.benefit: ~3,800 source lines removed (3,440 lines of cited bdmassault sources excluding the kept Makefile, plus iLink_internal.h 327 and iLink_CROM.h 72, minus ~40 ifdef lines); every future i.LINK fix made once. No menu ELF change claimed. INFERRED.
findings.evidence: Python difflib and diff -w between each bdmassault file and modules/ilink: iLink_intr.c, iLink_TxRx.c, iLink_DMA.c, iLink_PHY.c only include-path and one comment differ; iLink.c differs at :74,:160-163 (BD_iLink_start chain); iLink_internal.c at GetConsoleIDs :57-64, dmac_enable vs sceEnableDMAChannel, malloc ifdef :170-191; iLink_crom.c older endian handling; sbp2_driver.c diff 57 lines incl. missing sbp2FreeDevNr (modules/ilink sbp2_driver.c:403-427); scsi.c 141 diff lines (no READ_16/READ_CAPACITY_16). include/bdm.h lacks the path field that modules/ilink scsi.c sets. INFERRED part: the pinned PS2DEVPINNED container used by flavours.yml:363-398 must accept the shared source (e.g. sceEnableDMAChannel names); console testing required.

findings.title: Five per-component import/export files inside ilink_bd_assault are never used by its Makefile
findings.problem: The Makefile sets IOP_SRC_DIR := src/, so imports.o/exports.o come from src/imports.lst and src/exports.tab with src/irx_imports.h; no .c file includes irx_imports.h. The sub-tree copies are leftovers: IEEE1394_bd/src/imports.lst lacks I_PollEventFlag that sbp2_driver.c:392 calls, and iLinkman/src/imports.lst:1-4 still imports cdvdman sceCdRI/sceCdRM, which README.md says would abort loading under POPSTARTER.
findings.fix: Delete the five files (independently of finding 1).
findings.benefit: 244 lines and 5 stray files removed (73+35+30+74+32); no binary change. Removes a misleading cdvdman import list. INFERRED (standard PS2SDK Makefile.iopglobal rules, not in repo).
findings.evidence: Makefile:9,13-14 IOP_OBJS = exports.o ... imports.o, IOP_SRC_DIR := src/; custom rules :31-36 only compile .c. git grep '#include' over ilink_bd_assault/src: no source includes irx_imports.h. Grep cdvdman: only iLinkman/src/imports.lst:1-4 imports it. Grep test_ilink*.py for imports.lst/exports.tab/irx_imports: no hits. PollEventFlag absent from IEEE1394_bd/src/imports.lst but present in src/imports.lst:64.

findings.title: BgmPlayer: single-instance class reached only through two thread trampolines and five one-line forwarding wrappers
findings.problem: BgmPlayer has exactly one instance, the file-static gBgm (bgm.cpp:56), and no code outside bgm.cpp names the class (include/bgmplayer.h is included only by bgm.cpp:14). Every outside use goes through the C-style sound.h functions, which only forward (bgm.cpp:905-928), and the thread bodies need two static trampolines (bgm.cpp:58-66) because they are member functions. The 768 KB ring already had to stay outside the class (bgm.cpp:72), and the running flags (bgm.cpp:73) are plain globals shared with sound.cpp through soundint.h:12.
findings.fix: Make the BgmPlayer members file-static variables in bgm.cpp and the member functions static functions, name the public ones directly bgmStart/bgmStop/bgmQuiesce/isBgmPlaying/bgmDiscretionaryIoAllowed, pass the thread functions to CreateThread directly, and delete include/bgmplayer.h.
findings.benefit: ~55 lines removed (50-line header replaced by ~15 static declarations, 9 trampoline lines, ~20 forwarding lines). No ELF change expected beyond a few bytes of call indirection (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: grep BgmPlayer|bgmplayer.h over the repo: code hits only in include/bgmplayer.h and src/core/bgm.cpp; other hits are docs/CPP-CONVERSION-PLAN.md:388-396 (the conversion that introduced it) and .github/scripts/test_audio_threads.py / test_bgm_source.py, which locate functions by the text 'BgmPlayer::waitForRoom(' etc. and would need their anchors updated. Callers of the sound.h API: sound.cpp:50, textures.cpp:933 (gBgmInRead). Confidence Med because the class form follows the repo's own C++ conversion plan.

findings.title: Unused pieces in both SBP-2 drivers: DeinitIEEE1394, the get_max_lun hook, the always-LOGIN mode parameter, stray include and comments
findings.problem: DeinitIEEE1394 has no caller (only its prototype) and is the only reader that needs iLinkIntrCBThreadID global; sbp2_get_max_lun always returns 0 and scsi_warmup only M_DEBUGs it; ieee1394_SendManagementORB is only called with SBP2_LOGIN_REQUEST and rejects anything else; usbhdfsd-common.h supplies nothing used; a commented-out declaration and IRX_ID remain.
findings.fix: Delete DeinitIEEE1394 and its prototype and make iLinkIntrCBThreadID a local; delete sbp2_get_max_lun, the get_max_lun member and its call; drop the mode parameter (always LOGIN) and its guard; drop the usbhdfsd-common.h include and the commented lines. Adjust the tests that extract these functions by signature (test_ilink_sbp2_completion.py, test_ilink_bd_reset.py, test_ilink_bd_assault_reset.py, test_ilink_scsi_geometry.py).
findings.benefit: ~25 lines per copy, ~50 total; DeinitIEEE1394 and sbp2_get_max_lun are non-static or referenced, so a few dozen bytes per IRX (INFERRED, not measured).
findings.evidence: git grep DeinitIEEE1394: definitions sbp2_driver.c:775 (bdmassault) and :802 (ilink), prototypes sbp2_disk.h:180 (both), no caller, not in any exports.tab. ieee1394_SendManagementORB callers: sbp2_driver.c:250 only, with SBP2_LOGIN_REQUEST (tests also pass LOGIN). get_max_lun: set at sbp2_driver.c:87, called only at scsi.c:170 (result only logged), same in modules/ilink scsi.c:215-216. sbp2_driver.c uses no USBMASS_/bd_fragment symbol.

findings.title: scsi_read and scsi_write are the same loop in both IEEE1394_bd copies
findings.problem: scsi_read and scsi_write differ only in the const qualifier and the write flag passed to scsi_cmd_rw_sector; the 25-line chunking/retry loop is written twice in each copy.
findings.fix: Keep one static scsi_rw(bd, sector, buffer, count, write) with the loop and make scsi_read/scsi_write one-line calls (or point the block_device read/write at thin wrappers).
findings.benefit: ~20 lines per copy, ~40 total; roughly 100-150 bytes of IRX code per copy (INFERRED: one fewer copy of a small loop).
findings.evidence: Read bdmassault scsi.c:238-263 vs :265-290 side by side: identical apart from 'const' and the 0/1 argument; modules/ilink scsi.c:304 and :332 same pattern (diff with bdmassault shows only the debug macro lines differ).

findings.title: cheatman parser: parse_line wrapper re-tests is_cheat_code, make_code has a redundant zero branch, term_str callback has one caller
findings.problem: parse_buf already calls is_cheat_code (:346) and enters the parser branch for code lines and empty lines; parse_line (:187-200) runs is_cheat_code again only to return a zero code for the empty-line case, plus a per-line LOG. make_code pre-zeroes address/value and then has a failure branch that zeroes again (:149-153). term_str (:227-240) is a generic callback walker with a NULL check whose only caller passes is_cmt_str, which re-runs strlen at every character.
findings.fix: In parse_buf, call make_code directly when is_cheat_code(line) is true and skip the line otherwise; delete parse_line. In make_code delete the sscanf failure branch: its only caller passes lines holding exactly CODE_DIGITS hex digits, so both fields always parse. Replace term_str+is_cmt_str with one inline scan that cuts the line at the first '#' or '//'.
findings.benefit: ~30 lines removed; a few hundred bytes of .text at most (INFERRED; static functions, likely inlined already).
findings.evidence: All five functions are static in cheatman.cpp; grep term_str|is_cmt_str|parse_line|make_code in src: only cheatman.cpp. term_str called only at :342; parse_line only at :354. is_cheat_code returns 0 for an empty string (i==0 != CODE_DIGITS), so the zero code from parse_line for non-code lines is the only thing it adds. Note: the per-line LOG at :193 goes away with parse_line.

findings.title: OSDHistory: unused date getters, no-op DEBUG_PRINTF calls, commented-out loop and three stray includes of OSDHistory.h
findings.problem: osdHistoryGetYear/Month/Date have no use anywhere. findings.fix: Delete the three getters, the DEBUG_PRINTF define and its calls, and the commented-out loop; set size once after the switch (or pick only the icon pointer in it); drop the OSDHistory.h include from sysvmc.cpp, sysneutrino.cpp and sysdisc.cpp.

findings.evidence: grep osdHistoryGet(Year|Month|Date) whole repo: only OSDHistory.h:83-85 and a docs mention. grep DEBUG_PRINTF in src/: only OSDHistory.cpp:33 (define) and its 8 calls; other hits are in .github/scripts tests and IOP modules with their own defines. grep MAX_HISTORY_ENTRIES|HistoryEntry|osdHistorySetDate in src/: only OSDHistory.cpp. grep AddHistoryRecord in src/: system.cpp:1350,1378 only. sysvmc.cpp:41, sysneutrino.cpp:42, sysdisc.cpp:43 are bare includes.

findings.title: POPSTARTER i.LINK driver registers the full iLinkman export table that nothing imports
findings.problem: The combined module links IEEE1394_bd statically to iLinkman, yet still exports 22 iLinkman entry points and calls RegisterLibraryEntries. Under POPSTARTER the only other driver is bdm_assault (usbd.irx.ilink), so nothing imports them; iLinkAddCROMUnit/DeleteCROMUnit, GetNodeCapabilities, SetNodeCapabilities, DisableSBus and GetLocalNodeEUI64 are reachable only through this table and stay in a memory-card IRX.
findings.fix: Reduce src/exports.tab to the mandatory _start/_exit/_retonly slots (or drop the library registration) and let the export-only functions be removed; verify on a console that POPSTARTER loads the module without the iLinkman library.
findings.benefit: Export-only functions are ~70 lines of C (cited ranges); a few hundred bytes of the 27,769-byte usbhdfsd.irx.ilink (INFERRED, not measured).
findings.evidence: sbp2_driver.c calls only iLinkEnableSBus, SetTrCallbackHandler, GetGenerationNumber, GetLocalNodeID, GetNodeCount, TrAlloc, TrFree, TrWrite, GetNodeMaxSpeed, GetNodeTrSpeed, FindUnit, ReadCROM (read in full). PROVENANCE.md: usbd.irx.ilink is bdm_assault.irx (byte-identical to usbexfat). INFERRED: that POPSTARTER/bdm_assault never import iLinkman, and that the export removal frees bytes (dropping unreferenced functions needs --gc-sections, not confirmed for this Makefile build). README.md item 4 notes iopfixup needs exports.o first, so keep a minimal table.

findings.problem: USE_CUSTOM_ILINKMAN_MALLOC_AND_FREE is defined nowhere, so the iLinkman malloc/free copy never compiles; the combined module uses the identical pair in sbp2_driver.c:782-801 (the #ifdef exists only to avoid duplicate symbols).

findings.title: scsiCommandBudget re-implements sbp2ElapsedUs, and the TEST UNIT READY try count duplicates the 30 s budget
findings.problem: scsi.c:36-41 repeats sbp2ElapsedUs's GetSystemTime/64-bit subtract/SysClock2USec sequence from the same module. The warm-up is bounded twice: SCSI_READY_TRIES 300 polls at 100 ms each cannot end before about 30 s, which is SCSI_READY_BUDGET_US, the elapsed bound checked in the same condition.
findings.fix: Make sbp2ElapsedUs non-static (declare it in scsi.h) and call it from scsiCommandBudget; drop SCSI_READY_TRIES and the tries counter, keeping the 30 s elapsed-time budget (it allows at most one more poll), and update the turCalls <= 300 checks in test_ilink_bd_reset.py and test_ilink_bd_assault_reset.py plus the scsi.c extraction in those tests so they supply the shared helper.
findings.benefit: ~10 lines per copy, ~20 total; small code-size saving (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Compared scsi.c:30-41 with sbp2_driver.c:145-154: same statements. scsi.c:186 checks '++tries >= SCSI_READY_TRIES || !scsiCommandBudget(scsi)', with DelayThread(SCSI_READY_RETRY_US = 100 ms) per iteration and budget 30 s. Tests (test_ilink_bd_assault_reset.py) compile scsi.c with sbp2ElapsedUs 'when present', so the shared helper must be provided to them.

findings.title: Upstream BDM leftovers: always-true MBR 'valid' counter, unused GPT GUID and attribute macros, unneeded includes
findings.problem: In partitions_sanity_check_mbr 'valid' is incremented on every loop pass and the loop either returns early or ends with valid == 4, so 'valid == 4' is always true; MS_BASIC_DATA_PARTITION_GUID and the GPT_PART_ATTR_PLATFORM_REQUIRED/LEGACY_BOOTABLE/TYPE_* and GPT_BDP_ATTR_* macros are referenced nowhere; part_driver.c includes mbr_types.h, gpt_types.h, errno.h and string.h without using them.
findings.fix: Return active > 0 and delete the valid counter; delete the unused GUID and macros; drop the four unused includes from part_driver.c. Upstream ps2sdk code: optional, or offer upstream.
findings.benefit: ~15 lines; no binary change (static const arrays and macros are not emitted when unused). INFERRED.
findings.evidence: git grep MS_BASIC_DATA_PARTITION_GUID, GPT_BDP_, GPT_PART_ATTR_ over the repo: only gpt_types.h definitions, plus GPT_PART_ATTR_IGNORE used at part_driver_gpt.c:153 (kept). part_driver.c uses only part_driver.h, stdio (via M_ macros) and bdm.h symbols. part_driver_mbr.c:19-30 read: valid++ unconditional at :29.

findings.title: load_cheats: read_text_file's maxsize option is never used and the parse tail duplicates load_cheats_buf
findings.problem: read_text_file's only caller passes maxsize 0 (:476), so the size-limit branch (:411-415) is dead. load_cheats (:467-489) repeats load_cheats_buf's ensureCheatTable/parse_buf/mode-return sequence (:495-507).
findings.fix: Drop the maxsize parameter and its branch. In load_cheats_buf call ensureCheatTable before the NULL test, so a NULL buffer still clears the table; then make load_cheats read the file, call load_cheats_buf(buf), free the buffer and return that result. Do not simply read first and clear later: a failed read must still leave an empty table, or set_cheats_list (host.cpp:156) can flatten the previous game's cheats on a launch that continues past the error.
findings.benefit: ~12 lines removed; no measurable ELF change (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: grep read_text_file in src: cheatman.cpp:388,393,476 only. load_cheats called at supportbase.cpp:1811, load_cheats_buf at supportbase.cpp:1779; both return values are used the same way (>=0 then sbCheatsSelect). Order change (table allocated after the read instead of before) does not change results: a failed read returns -1 either way.

Nothing in bgm.cpp calls a pad.h function, and the only timer-like call, SetAlarm, is a kernel.h syscall that opl.h:5 already brings in (INFERRED for timer.h).

findings.title: GPT driver re-checks a sector size that bdm_try_mount already guarantees to be 512
findings.problem: part_connect_gpt is reached only through g_gpt_fs.connect_bd, which bdm_try_mount calls only after refusing every device whose sectorSize != 512, so entriesPerSector is always 4 and the entriesPerSector <= 0 branch (added in commit 5fe47865, not SDK code) cannot run.
findings.fix: Delete the check (lines 69-74).
findings.benefit: 6 lines; a few instructions in bdm.irx (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: part_driver.c:140 is the only assignment of part_connect_gpt (g_gpt_fs.connect_bd); fs connect_bd is only called at bdm.c:184, after the sectorSize != 512 return at :169-180. Partition pseudo devices copy bd->sectorSize (part_driver_gpt.c:171), so they also pass the gate only at 512. git blame: lines 69-74 from 5fe47865 (2026-10-27).

findings.problem: No C/C++ source uses CHEAT_VERSION, CR or SPACE from this header; NUL and LF (:46-47) are the only character constants the cheat code uses. CHEAT_VERSION's only other mention is a text anchor in .github/scripts/test_cheat_capacity.py:24.

findings.title: parse_buf computes each cheat's Select-mode default that cheatConfigLoadSelections always recomputes
findings.problem: parse_buf sets enabled = (gCheatMode == 0) || cheatConfigIsMasterCode(name) for every cheat. In Select mode (load returns 1) both load paths call sbCheatsSelect (supportbase.cpp:1785,1840), whose cheatConfigLoadSelections first resets every entry to cheatConfigIsMasterCode(name) (cheatconfig.cpp:72-73). The parser's master-code test is therefore overwritten every time, and it is the only reason cheatman.cpp includes cheatconfig.h.
findings.fix: Set enabled = 1 in parse_buf (Auto mode runs every cheat; Select mode is reset by cheatConfigLoadSelections), drop the cheatconfig.h include from cheatman.cpp, and drop or rewrite the text check in .github/scripts/test_neutrino_cheats.py:335 that requires the old line.
findings.benefit: ~3 lines and one header dependency removed; saves one name normalisation (one 129-byte stack buffer and a few strcmp) per parsed cheat (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read supportbase.cpp:1730-1840: sbCheatsSelect(cheatMode,...) calls cheatConfigLoadSelections when cheatMode==1, after both load_cheats_buf (:1779-1785) and load_cheats (:1811, :1840). load_cheats/load_cheats_buf have no other callers. grep cheatConfig in cheatman.cpp: only :27 (include) and :369. Med: relies on every future Select-mode path going through sbCheatsSelect.

findings.title: Boot logo animation frames LOGO1..LOGO6 and the single LOGO_PICTURE are decoded on every theme load but never drawn
findings.problem: The splash no longer animates: guisplash.cpp:73 draws only LOGO0_PICTURE (LOGO_PICTURE only when logoFrameCount is 0, which cannot happen because logo0 is always embedded and loaded with texLoadInternal). Yet themes.cpp:1684 and 1691-1697 decode LOGO_PICTURE and all seven LOGO0..LOGO6 frames on every theme load and keep them until the theme is freed. findings.title: GSHandler delay-slot emulation: B_taken zero-extends backward branch offsets and B_com1 masks the REGIMM field with 0x3F
findings.problem: When a trapped GS access is in a branch delay slot, GSHandler computes the resume PC itself. B_taken takes the offset with and 0xFFFF then sll 2, so a negative offset is zero-extended: a taken backward branch resumes at EPC+4+~0x3FFxx (about 256 KB ahead) instead of the loop head. B_com1 masks the REGIMM rt field with 0x3F, which also takes bit 21 (low bit of rs), so BLTZ/BGEZ/... on an odd register (v1, a1, a3, t1, s1, sp, ra...) indexes past the 32-word BD_t2 table and jumps to whatever word follows it. Either way the game jumps into arbitrary code.
findings.fix: In B_taken replace the li/and/sll triple with a sign-extending pair (shift the instruction left 16, then arithmetic shift right 14). In B_com1 change the mask from 0x3F to 0x1F (its own comment already says range 0x00-0x1F).
findings.benefit: Fixes a crash/freeze whenever a trapped GS access sits in a backward-branch delay slot (GSM: CSR polling loops with the ld in a beql slot; IGR menu tracker: GS register stores in loops) or an odd-rs REGIMM slot (INFERRED frequency); net -1 instruction
findings.evidence: Read gsm_engine.S:1030-1255 (BD path: BD2 from Cause bit 30, BD_t1/BD_t2 dispatch, B_taken, B_com1), 99-127 (BD_t2 = 32 words, last item of .data), 1266-1312 (BPC 0x60280000 = DRE+DWE for GSM, reads of CSR page trapped via TRAP_MASK 0x1FFFEF0F in gsm_defines.h:17; 0x20280000 = DWE for TRACK_ONLY). Reachability: main.c:127-140 EnableGSM when per-game GSM is on; main.c:147-151 EnableGSTracker for every game when In-Game Menu is on (IGR_MENU is a base define, ps2.yaml:609); gsm_api.c:155-174 installs GSHandler at 0x80000100. git blame: both lines date from a3f22727 (2015), 62052d1a1 (2021) only reindented (git show). grep over all of src/ for these lines: only this file. Code defect is READ; how often real games hit it is INFERRED. Upstream-derived (Open PS2 Loader GSM).

findings.title: Atlas node tree held in nested raii::UniquePtr makes GCC unroll the recursive destructor into ~14 KB of .text
findings.problem: Atlas::Node owns its children as raii::UniquePtr<Node>, so destroying the tree is a recursive chain of inline templates (unique_ptr dtor -> DestroyFree -> ~Node -> two unique_ptr dtors). At -O2 GCC inlines that recursion several levels deep: nm of the shipped ELF shows Atlas::~Atlas at 0x1958 (6,488 B) and std::unique_ptr<Atlas::Node, raii::DestroyFree>::~unique_ptr at 0x1d10 (7,440 B) plus a 168 B DestroyFree part, i.e. 14,096 of atlas.o's 15,448 text bytes for freeing a binary tree that upstream OPL freed with a ten-line recursive function.
findings.fix: Stop the recursive inlining: either give Node plain Node* children and free the tree with one small static recursive (or iterative) free function, as upstream OPL's atlas.c did, or keep UniquePtr and declare Node's destructor out of line with __attribute__((noinline)). Confirm with nm that Atlas::~Atlas and the unique_ptr<Atlas::Node> destructor drop to a few hundred bytes.
findings.justification: The fix replaces the template destructor chain with one explicit free routine (or one attribute); source size stays about the same while ~13.8 KB of loaded .text goes away.
findings.benefit: ~13.8 KB .text: MEASURED 6,488 + 7,440 + 168 = 14,096 B now (riptopl-nm-size-sorted.full.txt:132-133,153-154,3181); a non-inlined free is ~200-300 B (INFERRED). ELF is packed, so on-disk saving is smaller (INFERRED); RAM saving is the full amount.
findings.evidence: Read atlas.h:42-52 (Node with raii::UniquePtr leaf1/leaf2, root_) and atlas.cpp:42-60,105-139; raii.h:83-95 (DestroyFree calls p->~T() then free, UniquePtr = std::unique_ptr<T, DestroyFree>). evidence/RiptOPL/raw/riptopl-nm-size-sorted.full.txt:132-133 _ZNSt10unique_ptrIN5Atlas4NodeEN4raii11DestroyFreeEED1/D2Ev size 0x1d10 (same address), :153-154 _ZN5AtlasD1/D2Ev size 0x1958 (same address), :3181 DestroyFree::operator()<Atlas::Node>.part.0 0xa8; other Atlas methods total ~1.3 KB (placeIn 0x26c, create 0x13c, copyData 0xcc, place 0x88). riptopl-per-object.tsv:92 atlas.o text 15448. compile-link-flags.txt:55 riptopl -O2. BUILD-EVIDENCE.md:232 also lists Atlas::~Atlas() at 6,488 B.

findings.title: ArtIndex allocates hashes[4096] and pics[4096] (48 KB) per indexed directory regardless of its size and keeps them for the session
findings.problem: ArtIndex::build mallocs kMaxEntries*sizeof(unsigned int) = 16,384 bytes for hashes and kMaxEntries*sizeof(Pic) = 32,768 bytes for pics before the sweep and publishes those same buffers into the slot, never shrinking them to the n / picCount entries actually found. Slots are freed only when round-robin reuses them (release() via slotFor; invalidate() frees nothing), so with kSlots = 3 up to 147,456 bytes stay allocated for the whole run even when each ART folder holds a few hundred files. The index is live: artload.cpp:777 registers the art worker as owner and textures.cpp:1345,1357,1431 query it.
findings.fix: After the sweep succeeds, shrink hashes to n entries and pics to picCount entries with realloc (skip the shrink when the count is 0), before publishing them into the slot.
findings.justification: Two realloc calls are the smallest change that returns the unused tail of each array to the heap; the alternatives (a counting pre-pass or growable arrays) add more code. Concrete gain: about 46 KB per slot for a 200-file ART folder, which is >= 32 KB of EE RAM that is otherwise held for the session.
findings.benefit: INFERRED: per slot 49,152 B allocated vs 12*n B needed (n=200: 2,400 B), so ~46 KB freed per slot, up to ~140 KB with all three slots in use. sizeof(Pic)=8 from the two 4-byte members at artindexint.h:40-44.
findings.evidence: Read artindexint.h:26-92 (kSlots=3, kMaxEntries=4096, Pic {unsigned int hash; int name;}). Read artindex.cpp:180-289: malloc at :191 and :199 sized by kMaxEntries, no realloc of hashes/pics afterwards, buffers stored into slot at :281-286. Grep release(|invalidate(|free( in artindex.cpp: release() at :92-97 called only at :154 (slot reuse); invalidate() at :421 (comment at :153 says it deliberately does not free). findings.title: httpParseCatalog allocates 2048-row arrays (~890 KB) for every catalog and keeps them for the whole HTTP listing

The parse contract the host fixtures check does not change: the harness compiles the extracted function against libc, which has realloc.
findings.benefit: ~867 KB EE heap freed for a 100-row catalog and the refresh peak lowered by the same (INFERRED: (2048-100) x 445 B). Only while the HTTP source is in use, so rated 4, not 5.

findings.title: Ranet, RaBadge, RaHash and RaWatch are single-instance classes wrapped by a full layer of free forwarder functions

No ps2.yaml target, tools/build_configuration.py or tools/build_edition.py defines it, and deci2/drvtif/tifinet are in no embed_irx list (ps2.yaml:652, build_configuration.py:84-102), so the DECI2 declarations in extern_irx.h, every #ifdef __DECI2_DEBUG block and the five prebuilt blobs are never built or linked.
findings.fix: Delete the five extern_irx.h declarations, the __DECI2_DEBUG blocks in system.cpp, debug.cpp, opl.cpp, system.h and ee_core/src/iopmgr.c (keeping the TTY_UDP/TTY_PPC branches), CORE_IRX_DECI2 if nothing else remains, the DECI2 set in tools/syntax_sweep.py, and the five modules/debug blobs.
findings.benefit: ~110 source lines (sum of cited ranges) and 91,597 bytes of committed blobs (MEASURED: ls -l modules/debug, 73625+5985+5985+3301+3301); no shipped ELF change since no build compiles it (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: git grep -n -i deci2 tools/build_configuration.py tools/build_edition.py ps2.yaml .github/workflows tools/build.py tools/assets.py: no match. git grep DECI2_DEBUG: only Makefile, ee_core/Makefile, tools/syntax_sweep.py:23 (syntax check set), and the #ifdef sites listed. extern_irx.h names deci2_img/drvtif_irx/drvtif_ingame_irx/tifinet_irx/tifinet_ingame_irx are used only inside those #ifdef blocks (system.cpp:317,995-998; debug.cpp:27,32) and legacy Makefile rules. Brief open question 5 raised the same; this confirms it. Other readers own system.cpp/debug.cpp; listed here as the same problem.

findings.title: LinkImage applies the PS2RD .img cheat image before the game is loaded, so the patches never land
findings.problem: LinkImage is called from eecoreInit (main.c:116-117), i.e. on the first ee_core run, before LoadExecPS2 (main.c:181) restarts ee_core, which then wipes user memory (syshook.c:117, plus the kernel wipe from ModStorageEnd) and loads the game ELF (syshook.c:126). At LinkImage time the game is not in memory: the sanity gate reads OPL's leftover memory at Offset0 and fails, and any word it did write is wiped and overwritten by the game load. The $EnableImage option therefore never patches a game.
findings.fix: Delete the .img feature (LinkImage, config->gImage, LoadImage/GetImage/gImage, sbLoadImage and its call sites, the $EnableImage row and strings). If the owner wants to keep it, the apply has to move to sysLoadElf after LoadElf/apply_patches, with the words kept somewhere the wipe does not reach (ee_core has no room for the 4 KB, cheat_api.c:36-38).
findings.benefit: Removes an option that silently does nothing; ~100 lines across ee_core and the menu (INFERRED from the cited ranges plus prototypes/UI rows) and 4 KB of main-ELF .bss (static u32 gImage[MAX_IMAGEWORDS=1024] = 4096 bytes, INFERRED arithmetic).
findings.evidence: Read main.c:40-185 (eecoreInit calls EnableCheats/LinkImage, then main() calls LoadExecPS2; isInit path calls sysLoadElf), syshook.c:86-147 (WipeUserMemory(&_end, ModStorageStart), LoadElf, apply_patches, CleanExecPS2), system.cpp:1195 (kernel InitializeUserMemory set to ModStorageEnd), host.cpp:161-163 (gImage handed over), cheatman.cpp:111-125 (LoadImage), supportbase.cpp:1701-1718. git show 97421c9520: the call was added at eecoreInit with no in-game test noted. grep LinkImage/gImage over tests and .github: no test. INFERRED part: that .img targets are game addresses (format not documented in the repo); any target above 0x97000 is wiped or reloaded.

findings.title: One-line free forwarders duplicate EthSupport/FavSupport methods and netsupport (21 wrappers)
findings.problem: Every public EthSupport/FavSupport operation exists twice: as a class method and as a free function whose whole body is `return gXxxSupport.method(...)` (eth: ethIsNfs, ethShareChosen, ethIsSMBShareConnected, ethEnsureSMBShareConnected, ethRequestCheckedRefresh, ethRequestReconnect, ethResolveIsoFavourite; fav: favGetItemSourceMode, favGetFlags, favGetItemKind, favGetArtMode, favRemoveByIndex, addFavouriteItem, removeFavouriteByIdAndText, favGetItemDisplay, favGetItemStarred, favToggleByIndex). Four more eth functions only forward to netsupport (ethApplyConfig, ethGetModulesLoaded, ethGetNetConfig, ethGetDHCPStatus). gEthSupport/gFavSupport are already extern in the same headers.
findings.fix: Pick one API. Simplest: callers use gEthSupport.x()/gFavSupport.x() (and netApplyConfig/netGetModulesLoaded/netGetConfig/netGetDHCPStatus) directly; delete the 21 forwarders and their prototypes, moving the useful prototype comments onto the methods. Update the source-text tests that stub or scrape these names.
findings.benefit: ~21 forwarders x 4 lines + ~40 prototype/comment lines in the two headers = ~110 lines removed, ~50 call sites renamed (INFERRED from cited ranges). ELF effect small: forwarders are non-static, no section GC assumed (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read every forwarder body at the cited lines; grep -rn 'return gFavSupport\.' favsupport.cpp shows the 10 fav forwarders; grep of the eth names over src: callers in ui/guisettings.cpp, guigame.cpp, guifilemgr.cpp, menuitems.cpp, sources/vcdsupport.cpp, supportbase.cpp, achievements.cpp, ranet.cpp, nettime.cpp, lwnbdctl.cpp, platform/system.cpp, debug.cpp, udpfssupport.cpp, bdmsupport.cpp, appsupport.cpp. ethApplyConfig only caller: src/platform/debug.cpp:72 (debug overlay); ethGetDHCPStatus only caller: ranet.cpp:816 (RA). 21 .github/scripts/*.py files mention some of these names (stubs/scrapes) and must be updated.

findings.title: Stateless single-instance classes BdmBoot, BdmLauncher, NeutrinoLauncher with private headers and free forwarders
findings.problem: None of the three classes has a data member; each has exactly one global instance (gBdmBoot, gBdmLauncher, gNeutrinoLauncher) and each header is included only by its own .cpp. The public entry points are free functions that just forward to the instance, and BdmBoot even needs public static shims slotIdentity/elfOnSlot (bdmboot.h:22-24) so the file's own free function bootElfProbe can reach its private statics.
findings.fix: Delete the three headers and the globals; make the member functions file-static functions in their .cpp, and let bdmResolveBootDir/bdmResolveBootDirBootstrap/bdmLaunchCue/bdmLaunchVcd be the functions themselves instead of forwarders. Update the source-scraping tests that look up 'BdmLauncher::'/'NeutrinoLauncher::' names.
findings.benefit: ~100 lines removed (121 header lines, ~17 forwarder/global lines, minus comments worth keeping); no ELF change expected (INFERRED: no state, calls already resolve statically)
findings.evidence: git grep gBdmBoot|bdmboot.h|BdmBoot (excluding docs): only bdmboot.h and bdmboot.cpp. git grep gBdmLauncher|gNeutrinoLauncher|bdmlauncher.h|neutrinolauncher.h: only the headers and bdmlaunch.cpp. Read both launcher headers: no data members (NeutrinoLauncher has only static constexpr kMaxFrags). Tests that scrape the member names: test_issues_830_831.py, test_ember_disc_selection.py, test_mcemu_slots.py, test_netblock_oplcore.py, test_patch_zone_restore.py, test_pccf.py, test_retrogem_ember.py (git grep -ln BdmLauncher::|NeutrinoLauncher::|BdmBoot::).

findings.title: In-game DECI2 debug mode (__DECI2_DEBUG) is dead: no ps2build configuration defines it and its IRX blobs are never embedded
findings.problem: __DECI2_DEBUG is set only by the legacy make files (Makefile:340, ee_core/Makefile:44); tools/build_configuration.py (debug configs at :79-100) never adds it and ps2.yaml/tools never embed drvtif/tifinet/deci2. findings.title: vmc_groups.cpp: 97 count_ constants and the titleCount field can go if the arrays are NULL-terminated
findings.problem: Each of the 97 groups has a hand-written count_X = sizeof(titles_X)/sizeof(titles_X[0]) line (1344 is one of them) feeding a titleCount field. The pattern has already broken: the comments at 1153, 1158, 1172, 1180 record four copy-pasted numerators that overstated the count and walked past the array.

Only users of the struct: getGroupIdForTitleId (1452-1474) and tests/host/test_vmc_groups.cpp:12-34 (includes the .cpp). include/vmc_groups.h exposes only the function.

findings.title: deinit() is a line-for-line copy of deinitEx() with modeSelected2 = -1
findings.problem: deinit (1373-1456) repeats deinitEx (1279-1371) statement for statement, including its 36 comment lines. The only differences: deinit calls deinitAllSupport where deinitEx runs the same loop with a spared mode (with modeSelected2 = -1 the loop is exactly deinitAllSupport, 608-614), and deinitEx adds launchDiagMark(7)/(8), which are gated on gLaunchDiag (compiled to 0 without LAUNCH_DIAG, armed only by udp-block Neutrino launches). Both copies also carry a stale paragraph saying 'deinitAllSupport below' (1310-1318, wrong in deinitEx) and the deinitEx header comment (1254-1256) is separated from its function by the drain-ticks block.
findings.fix: Delete the body of deinit and make it call deinitEx(exception, modeSelected, -1). Keep one copy of the comments, drop the stale first 'JOIN the art worker' paragraph (the join is described again at cacheEnd), and move the deinitEx header comment next to its function. Adjust .github/scripts/test_menu_crash_catcher.py:63-64, which greps both bodies for menuWatchStop().
findings.benefit: ~80 source lines removed (84-line function becomes a 3-line forwarder); one copy of the teardown code leaves the ELF, a few hundred bytes (INFERRED, not measured); future teardown fixes land once instead of twice.
findings.evidence: Read opl.cpp:1254-1456 side by side: identical statements 1281-1349 vs 1375-1443; loop 1350-1355 with modeSelected2<0 gives spared=0 -> moduleCleanup(..., modeSelected), same as deinitAllSupport 608-614; then audioEnd..configEnd identical (1359-1368 vs 1446-1455). launchDiagMark/gLaunchDiag: include/launchdiag.h:52-76 (#define gLaunchDiag 0 and inline no-op when LAUNCH_DIAG is off; armed only by stage 1 in NeutrinoLauncher). Callers: deinit via host.cpp:77 from ~20 call sites (system.cpp:461,665, appsupport.cpp:1073 etc.), deinitEx via host.cpp:78 from Neutrino/POPSTARTER paths. Test test_menu_crash_catcher.py:63-64 asserts menuWatchStop() in both function bodies.

findings.title: sysneutrino.cpp: file read, write-with-restore and two 8 KB static buffer pairs duplicated in the udpfs ip sync and SMB/NFS preflight
findings.problem: sysSyncNeutrinoUdpfsToml and sysNeutrinoSmbPreflight each carry the same accumulate-read loop (403-409 vs 670-676) and the same O_TRUNC write plus restore-original-on-short-write block (446-465 vs 733-749), and each owns static toml[4096] plus updated[4116] / updated[4608]. Both run only on the GUI thread before teardown and never nest, so the second pair of buffers is never live at the same time as the first. sysWriteNeutrinoCheats (980-991) repeats the open/write/close/unlink-on-short-write that sysNeutrinoRAWrite (1068-1079) already implements.
findings.fix: Move the two buffers to file scope once (toml[4096], updated[4608]) and use them from both functions; replace the duplicated read loop and write-restore block with two small static helpers (read whole file into toml, write updated or restore toml). Take sysNeutrinoRAWrite out of the RETROACHIEVEMENTS block and call it from sysWriteNeutrinoCheats.
findings.justification: The helpers replace two copies each of the same 7-line read loop and 15-line write/restore block plus one 10-line write/unlink copy, so code shrinks, and sharing the buffers removes a whole duplicate 8 KB .bss pair.
findings.benefit: 8,212 B .bss (INFERRED: 4096+4116+4096+4608 = 16,916 B now vs 4096+4608 = 8,704 B shared) and about 25 lines.
findings.evidence: Read sysneutrino.cpp:382-468 and 637-752 side by side: the read loops and write/restore blocks differ only in log text and return codes. Callers: sysSyncNeutrinoUdpfsToml only from sysNeutrinoPreflight (sysneutrino.cpp:837, udpfs/udpfsbd/udpbd only); sysNeutrinoSmbPreflight from ethsupport (system.h:79 contract, smb/nfs leg) - disjoint devices, both pre-teardown, neither calls the other. sysNeutrinoRAWrite at 1068-1079 under #ifdef RETROACHIEVEMENTS (1021-1124).

findings.title: InGameScreenshot spends roughly 8-15 s in decorative busy-waits and writes its text file one byte per RPC
findings.problem: On the IGR thread, between the game's shutdown and IGR_Exit, the screenshot code waits only to animate the background colour: FastDelay(1) (a 768-pass nop loop) after every pixel in the three ConvertColors loops, delay(1) (16.7M-pass nop loop, util.c:170-179) after each 128 KB DMA slice and six more times, and two success blinks (BlinkColour, util.c:184-198) worth 10 more delay units. SaveTextFile then sends its ~700-byte report with one fioPutc (one fio RPC) per byte.
findings.fix: Delete FastDelay and its three calls with the per-pixel fade writes, the six standalone delay(1) calls and the success blinks at lines 61 and 787. Keep the per-slice delay(1) only if a hardware test shows the empirical slicing needs it. Replace the fioPutc loop with one fioWrite of the built string.
findings.benefit: INFERRED: delay(1) = 16.7M passes x 4-7 cycles at 294.9 MHz = 0.23-0.40 s; 16 fixed units = 3.6-6.4 s, 8 slices at 640x448x32 = 1.8-3.2 s; FastDelay 768 x 4-7 cycles x 286720 px = 3.0-5.2 s. ~700 RPCs become 1. ~24 lines removed.
findings.evidence: Read igs_api.c 1-790; delay() and BlinkColour() at util.c:170-198; DBGCOL_BLNK expands to BlinkColour (ee_core.h:91), BGCOLND to a GS_BGCOLOUR write (ee_core.h:90). Counted delay units: 171, 379, 556, 564, 673, 762 (6); line 61 BlinkColour(2) = delay(2)+4 = 6; line 787 BlinkColour(1) = 4; per-slice 303. Cycle counts per loop pass are INFERRED (eecore -Os, ps2.yaml:612); no hardware timing measured. Upstream-derived code (git log: Open PS2 Loader commits only). Compiled only in extras/extras_ds5 (tools/build_configuration.py:37-40); called at padhook.c:646-648 after oplIGRShutdown and the IOP reset, followed by IGR_Exit at padhook.c:659.

findings.title: bdmLoadBlockDeviceModules sleeps up to 4.2 s on the IO worker at boot, ahead of every page list and of deferredInit (splash end)
findings.problem: The first bdmInit queues bdmLoadBlockDeviceModules (1559) before each slot's IO_MENU_UPDATE_DEFFERED (opl.cpp 538-542), and deferredInit, which posts GUI_INIT_DONE, is queued after init() (opl.cpp 2116); the single FIFO IO worker runs them in order. The pass ends with one-shot DelayThread settles: 600 ms whenever USB is enabled (1465), 600 ms when MX4SIO is enabled but no card answers (1422), and a 12 x 250 ms poll when iLink is enabled but no iLink root appears (1480-1481). Every page list, and the splash fade (guisplash.cpp 191-210 waits on guiInitComplete), waits behind those sleeps.
findings.fix: Delete the iLink poll loop at 1480-1483 and keep its single bdmForceDeviceRefresh, as the MX4SIO branch does: bdmevent is armed before any transport loads (1513-1526), so a late iLink mount already bumps BdmGeneration, which docs/ILINK-DISCOVERY-PARITY-2026-10-18.md already relies on after the deadline. For the USB and MX4SIO settles, either drop the DelayThread and keep the probe plus refresh, or queue the one-shot settle tail as its own IO request after deferredInit so GUI_INIT_DONE and the first lists are not behind it.
findings.justification: Only the second USB/MX4SIO option adds anything (one function split out of bdmLoadBlockDeviceModules and one ioPutRequest). It removes a fixed 0.6-1.2 s from the boot critical path without changing the settle the comments at 1429-1461 defend; the iLink part is a pure deletion.
findings.benefit: Up to 3.0 s (iLink on, no device) + 0.6 s (MX4SIO on, no card) + 0.6 s (USB on) less wait before the first lists and the splash fade (INFERRED: sum of the DelayThread arguments; overlap with other boot work not measured); ~6 lines removed for the iLink loop
findings.evidence: Read bdmsupport.cpp 1260-1560. ioman.cpp 259-331: one worker, appendLocked links at the tail, putUnlessWaiting only skips an identical not-started request. opl.cpp 538-542: init() then ioPutRequest(IO_MENU_UPDATE_DEFFERED) per page; 1719 _loadConfig -> applyConfig -> initAllSupport (567 bdmEnumerateDevices -> bdmInitDevicesData -> initSupport per slot, bdmdevices.cpp 97); 2116 deferredInit queued after init(); 1757-1759 GUI_INIT_DONE; gui.cpp 195-196 sets initComplete_; guisplash.cpp 191-210 fade gated on guiInitComplete. git log -S ilinkProbeDone: 79f16d18 (deliberate upstream-parity restore; its doc states the 3 s cost). INFERRED: how much of the sleep overlaps main-thread boot work, and that mount events alone discover iLink on hardware.

findings.title: delay() is a CPU-burning NOP spin (~0.25 s per tick) that starves lower-priority threads, and lwnbdctl's '~5 s' pad retry is really ~20 minutes
findings.problem: delay(n) spins 0x01000000 x 4 nops per tick; the repo's own notes put a tick at about 0.25 s (opl.cpp:1269-1272, autolaunch.cpp:204, settingsio.cpp:1419). It runs on the main thread at priority 31, so while it spins the IO worker (32), the art worker (72) and BGM I/O (31) cannot run; guiWarning spins delay(count) for 2 to 25 ticks. lwnbdctl retries startPads 100 times with delay(50) and its comment calls that ~5 s; at 0.25 s per tick it is about 12 s per retry and ~20 minutes in total, the very freeze #307 tried to bound.
findings.fix: Make delay() sleep instead of spin: DelayThread(250000) per tick, which keeps the tick length every caller was tuned to. In lwnbdctl.cpp replace the two delay(50) retry waits with a 50 ms DelayThread so the 100-try bound is the ~5 s its comment states.
findings.benefit: Frees the CPU for the IO, art and BGM threads during every guiWarning and boot/autolaunch wait; bounds the NBD pad retry at ~5 s instead of ~20 min (INFERRED tick length from repo comments).
findings.evidence: Read util.cpp:941-950. grep -n 'delay(' over src include: guimodal.cpp:287 (guiWarning; callers pass 20 opl.cpp:1727, 6 opl.cpp:2129, 2 menuitems.cpp:299, 12/25 util.cpp:839-846), ioman.cpp:383, settingsio.cpp:1426, lwnbdctl.cpp:200,236, autolaunch.cpp:207,243,249; ee_core has its own delay (ee_core/src/util.c:170), not affected. Priorities: main 31 (opl.cpp:2064), IO 32 (ioman.cpp:250), BGM 0x1E/0x1F (bgm.cpp:40,684,696), art 72 (artload.cpp:31). Tick length INFERRED from opl.cpp:1269-1275, autolaunch.cpp:203-205, settingsio.cpp:1419; not measured. lwnbdctl.cpp:228-231 states ~5 s for 100 x delay(50). DelayThread is already used in 27 src files.

findings.title: IoQueue::blockOps polls the drain with delay(1), a ~0.25 s NOP spin, so drains finish late and every bound is in idle-CPU ticks (NBD bound ~4 min)
findings.problem: blockOps lowers the caller to priority 90 and waits with delay(1), a 0x01000000-iteration NOP spin (util.cpp:941-949; opl.cpp:1269-1271 says about a quarter second per tick). A drain that ends mid-spin is noticed only when the spin ends, so each launch, exit, NBD start and HDD rename/delete with work queued waits up to ~0.25 s more. The spin advances only while every higher-priority thread is blocked, so the timeout counts idle CPU, not time. lwnbdctl.cpp:78 still passes 1000 ticks (~4 min) as its bound; opl.cpp rescaled its own constants but NBD was missed.
findings.fix: In IoQueue::blockOps replace delay(1) with DelayThread(10 * 1000) and count the budget in those 10 ms steps. Restate the budgets in that unit: EXIT_IO_DRAIN_TICKS 4 -> 100, LAUNCH_IO_DRAIN_TICKS 40 -> 1000, and LWNBD_IO_DRAIN_TICKS to the bound it was meant to be. menusys.cpp:248 passes 0 and is unaffected.
findings.benefit: Drain completion seen within 10 ms instead of up to ~0.25 s per call (INFERRED: 16.7M-iteration spin, repo comment opl.cpp:1269-1271); the NBD bound drops from ~250 s (1000 x ~0.25 s, INFERRED) to a real wall-clock limit; no lines added.
findings.evidence: Read ioman.cpp:360-398 (blockOps: ChangeThreadPriority(90), while(hasPending()) delay(1)) and util.cpp:941-949 (delay = nested NOP spin, no sleep). Worker priority 32 at ioman.cpp:250, so it and any thread above 90 preempt the spin.
