findings.title: NIBBLE2CHAR emits 'k'..'p' for hex digits 10-15, so the SOS/Disaster Report IREMSND patch gets a wrong module ID
findings.problem: NIBBLE2CHAR(n) is 'a' + n for n > 9, giving 'k' for 10 instead of 'a'. SOS_SifLoadModuleHook formats the IREMSND module ID with it and iremsndpatch parses it with strtol(..., 16), which stops at the bad character: an ID such as 0x1A becomes 1, so the patch searches for the wrong module (ID 1 exists) or none.
findings.fix: Change the macro to 'a' + (n) - 10.
findings.benefit: Fixes the IREMSND patch for module IDs whose hex form contains a-f (6 of 16 low nibbles). No size change.
findings.evidence: Read patches.c:160 and 565-570; iremsndpatch/main.c:60-76 (argc check, strtol base 16, walks lc->image_info comparing m->id). Upstream-derived code. Only caller of the hook path: SOSPatch for SLUS_205.61 / SLPS_251.13 (patches.c:113-115, 581-596).

findings.title: PS1 favourites resolve and star by name, but addItem/removeByIdAndText require the stored id, so un-favouriting fails once the PS1 list reorders
findings.problem: VCD/CUE favourites ignore the stored id when resolving (700-728), lighting device-page stars (594-596) and All Games stars (1740), but the add-time duplicate check (1025) and removeByIdAndText (1071) require recs[i].id == id unless mode is APP (616-619). PS1 lists are qsorted (vcdsupport.cpp:737-738, cuesupport.cpp:1105-1106), so adding/removing a PS1 game or toggling autosort shifts the index. R3 on the lit star (menuitems.cpp:459-465, toggleByIndex 1770) then matches nothing, rewrites the file unchanged, returns 1 ('Removed'), and the star returns on the next rebuild; the next R3 appends a duplicate record.
findings.fix: Make favIdsMatchForMode kind-aware: ignore the id for FAV_KIND_VCD and FAV_KIND_CUE exactly as it already does for APP_MODE, and pass the kind from addItem and removeByIdAndText. favRecIsStarred can then call the same helper instead of its own favKindIsNameAddressed special case.
findings.benefit: Fixes un-favouriting of PS1 games after any PS1 list change and stops duplicate PS1 records in favourites.bin; net ~0 lines (one extra parameter, one special case folded in).
findings.evidence: Read favResolve 690-766: name-addressed branch never compares id. favFindVisibleSource 594: LIB_VIEW_PS1 matches by text only. favRecIsStarred 1740 skips id for name-addressed kinds. addItem 1025 and removeByIdAndText 1071 call favIdsMatchForMode(mode, recId, id) which is id-equality except APP_MODE. Callers: menuitems.cpp:446-465 store/remove with libListSourceId (libview.cpp:158-163), the PS1-list index; toggleByIndex 1770 passes the All Games row id. vcdsupport.cpp:730-738 comment says VCD ids follow a qsorted backing array and 'favourites resolve BY NAME'; cuesupport.cpp:1105-1106 qsorts too. hddsupport.cpp:3324 already handles 'Favourites can keep a source id from before a refresh' for ps1SaveDir.

findings.title: RA badge cache keeps 168 bytes per list row for the whole session although it is only read during the same list rebuild
findings.problem: refresh() mallocs count * RA_BADGE_TEXT (ISO_GAME_NAME_MAX 160 + 8 = 168 bytes) per device list and fills every row, mostly with empty strings, and keeps it until the next rebuild of that list. The only readers are raBadgeText at opl.cpp:800 (which immediately strdup's the text into the row) and cfgtitle.cpp:149 (uses it at once), both inside the same updateMenuFromGameList pass on the I/O thread, so the per-row strings are never needed afterwards and badged names exist twice.
findings.fix: Store one byte per row in the slot (badged or not) instead of the formatted string, and let text() format prefix/suffix plus the row name into one static RA_BADGE_TEXT buffer on demand; both callers already copy or consume the result before the next call.
findings.benefit: INFERRED: 168 B/row -> 1 B/row of EE heap held per list, e.g. a 500-row USB list 84,000 -> 500 bytes, 1,000 rows ~167 KB -> 1 KB; RA builds with telemetry and badges on only. Source size about equal (the snprintf moves into text()).
findings.evidence: Read rabadge.cpp:141-218 and rabadge.h:8-38. ISO_GAME_NAME_MAX = 160 at include/supportbase.h:7, RA_BADGE_TEXT at rabadge.cpp:48. grep raBadgeText/gRaBadge over src: callers only opl.cpp:800 (strdup at :802) and cfgtitle.cpp:149 (keepTitle, called from cfgTitleRefresh at opl.cpp:842 in the same updateMenuFromGameList); raBadgeRefresh only at opl.cpp:747. Renderer uses the row's raText/raBadged snapshot (gui.cpp:222-223, menusys.cpp:1773, themeelems.cpp:1130), never the cache. Allocation skipped when gRATelemetry or gRABadges is 0 (rabadge.cpp:163); telemetry default 0 (settings.cpp:65), badges default 1 (:68).

findings.title: cacheLoadImage retries every non-ERR_BAD_FILE failure, so an undecodable art file is re-read continuously while it is on screen
findings.problem: The transient branch fires for any result other than ERR_BAD_FILE, including deterministic format failures: ERR_SET_JMP (truncated/corrupt PNG, or any PNG over the 1024x1024 user limit), ERR_BAD_DEPTH (16-bit PNG), ERR_BAD_DIMENSION, and ERR_FILE_IO for a zero-byte file. The slot is cleared, the row re-requests on its next draw, and the 'settle gate' the comment relies on only exists for SIO2, so on USB/HDD/SMB the art worker re-opens and re-reads that file back to back (twice per try, since texLoadArtFile retries a bad .png as a JPG) for as long as the row or selected BG is shown, keeping cacheHasPendingArt() true.
findings.fix: Keep the retry lane only for real I/O and allocation failures: retry when the result is ERR_FILE_IO, ERR_READ_STRUCT or ERR_INFO_STRUCT, and park every other negative result exactly like ERR_BAD_FILE (it is re-asked after the next fail-epoch bump). Make the zero-byte case at textures.cpp:723-726 return a format error rather than ERR_FILE_IO so it parks too.
findings.benefit: Stops an unbounded read loop (one full file read, often two, per art-worker cycle) for every broken art file on screen; no lines added, one condition changed (INFERRED from the code path; no hardware count).
findings.evidence: artload.cpp:714-758: result<0 and !abortRequested -> if (result != ERR_BAD_FILE) { transientFail++; cacheClearItem(entry,0); release } with no backoff (grep transientFail|retryFrame|backoff over src/gfx: only artload.cpp:166,747). textures.h:195-207 error codes. textures.cpp:1035-1042 png_set_user_limits(1024,1024) then png_read_info (png_error -> setjmp at 1023-1031 -> ERR_SET_JMP), bitDepth>8 -> ERR_BAD_DEPTH; 1108-1111 ERR_BAD_DIMENSION; 723-726 empty file -> ERR_FILE_IO; 1328-1334 non-PNG .png falls to texLoadJpgFile which re-opens and stages the file again and returns the PNG result. texcache.cpp:245-351: cleared slot (UID 0, key empty) misses both the id path and the key reunion, so the next cacheGetTextureEx claims a slot and enqueues again; texcache.cpp:372-378 idle gate applies only when isSio2.

findings.title: cheat_entry_t.codes[] is sized in u32 words (510) but holds pairs: the 1.05 MB cheat table is twice what any consumer can use
findings.problem: MAX_CHEATLIST (510) is the word count of gCheatList (5 hook pairs + 250 code pairs), but cheat_entry_t uses it as the number of code_t PAIRS per cheat. No reader can use more than 255 pairs of one cheat: set_cheats_list caps the whole list at 510 words, igrRowFits needs n <= 250, set_cheats_list_live takes at most 5 hooks plus 250 codes. Half of every 4216-byte entry is unreachable.
findings.fix: Declare codes[MAX_CHEATLIST / 2] and bound the parser store (cheatman.cpp:373) and the four codes[] walks (524, 570, 623, 660) by that array size instead of MAX_CHEATLIST. Update the ~1.03 MB comments.
findings.benefit: sizeof(cheat_entry_t) 132+4080+4 = 4216 -> 132+2040+4 = 2176; x250 = 1,054,000 -> 544,000 bytes, 510,000 bytes less heap per cheats-on launch and a smaller single malloc that is less likely to fail (INFERRED arithmetic).
findings.evidence: Read cheatman.h:39-69, cheatman.cpp:312-385,448-680, ee_core/include/igrcheats.h:22-71 (IGR_CHEAT_SET_CODES 250). grep gCheats|codes[|MAX_CHEATLIST over the repo: the only codes[] readers are cheatman.cpp:524,570,593,614,623,660; guimodal.cpp and cheatconfig.cpp read only name/enabled; supportbase.cpp:1856 reads gCheatList (<= 255 pairs). Behaviour change only for a cheat with more than 255 codes, whose tail can already never reach ee_core.

findings.title: diaShowKeyb writes one byte past its pre[maxLen] VLA when strlen(text) == maxLen; File Manager rename passes FM_NAME - 1 with names up to 127 bytes
findings.problem: diaKeybTextWidth copies text[from..to) into scratch and writes scratch[to - from] = 0; diaShowKeyb passes the stack VLA pre[maxLen] with from=view(0) and to=n=len every frame, so len == maxLen writes pre[maxLen]. fmRenameEntry seeds name from a list entry (fmList keeps names up to 127 bytes, filemgr.cpp:208-210) and passes maxLen FM_NAME - 1 = 127, so renaming a file whose name is 127 bytes long overwrites one stack byte per frame while the keyboard is open. Every other caller passes the buffer size.
findings.fix: Pass sizeof(name) (FM_NAME) instead of FM_NAME - 1 at guifilemgr.cpp:523 and :539, matching every other diaShowKeyb caller and fmNameOk's 1..FM_NAME-1 limit (filemgr.cpp:151).
findings.benefit: Closes a reachable one-byte stack overwrite in the main thread (consequence depends on what lies above the VLA in the frame: INFERRED); no size change.
findings.evidence: Read diaeditors.cpp:104-109 (memcpy + scratch[to-from]=0), :130 len=strlen(text), :138 caret=len, :215 char pre[maxLen], :216 n=len, :224 and :238 diaKeybTextWidth(shown, view, n, pre). Callers (grep diaShowKeyb): dia.cpp:946 tmp[32]/32, gui.cpp:176 tmp[maxLength]/maxLength, menusys.cpp:2252 empty/CONFIG_KEY_VALUE_LEN, guigame.cpp:110/153 handler args from dia.cpp:941 (tmp,32), guifilemgr.cpp:523/539 name[FM_NAME]/FM_NAME-1. FM_NAME 128 at include/filemgr.h:8; fmList keeps strlen < 128 (filemgr.cpp:208-210); rename reached from diaFileActions FMA_RENAME (guifilemgr.cpp:602-603).

findings.title: lwnbdctl.cpp: NBD start/stop 'bounded' waits treat delay() ticks as milliseconds (IO drain ~4 min, pad retries up to ~20 min)
findings.problem: delay() spins 0x01000000 x 4 nops per tick, ~0.25 s (util.cpp:941-950; the repo records this at opl.cpp:1269-1277). ioBlockOpsTimed spends one delay(1) per tick (ioman.cpp:380-386), so LWNBD_IO_DRAIN_TICKS = 1000, meant to fail a stuck request quickly, spins the GUI thread for ~250 s behind the frozen 'Starting NBD' screen. Both pad-restart loops wait delay(50) (~12.5 s) per failed startPads(), up to 100 times (~20 min), where the comment at 228-231 promises ~5 s. LWNBD_ART_DRAIN_TICKS = 500 next to it is milliseconds (artload.cpp:426-449), so the two *_TICKS constants differ in unit by ~250x.
findings.fix: Set LWNBD_IO_DRAIN_TICKS to about 4 (~1 s, the same value opl.cpp:1276 already uses for EXIT_IO_DRAIN_TICKS) and note the unit. In both pad loops replace delay(50) with DelayThread(50000) so 100 tries are the documented ~5 s (move the delaythread.h include out of the __OPLDIAG block), or keep delay() and use delay(1) with 20 tries.
findings.benefit: On NBD start/stop failure paths the screen freezes ~1 s / ~5 s as documented instead of ~250 s / up to ~20 min. Timing INFERRED: 16.8M loop iterations per tick at 294.9 MHz is ~0.25 s, the figure opl.cpp:1269-1272 and artload.cpp:426-427 state.
findings.evidence: Read lwnbdctl.cpp:77-78,141-154,192-203,228-239; ioman.cpp:360-398 (blockOps: while hasPending, delay(1), timeoutTicks--) and 467-476; util.cpp:941-950; opl.cpp:1269-1277 (same units trap already fixed there: EXIT 4, LAUNCH 40 ticks); artload.cpp:426-454 and hddsupport.cpp:308-312 (art waits are DelayThread(1000) per tick = ms); pad.cpp:1155-1200 (startPads returns 0 when no port opens, e.g. after a half-done IOP reset as the 228-231 comment anticipates). Caller: menusys.cpp:2380-2382 MENU_NBD on the GUI thread. The tick duration is computed, not measured on hardware.

findings.title: vmc_groups: 1046 per-title pointers cost 4184 B of .data; fixed-width char arrays make them unnecessary
findings.problem: Each of the 97 groups is a static const char *titles_*[] array (first at line 14, last at 1346), so every title costs a 4-byte pointer in .data on top of its 12-byte string: vmc_groups.o has 4184 B of .data = 1046 x 4. Every ID is 11 characters (once SSCES_540.95 at 614 is fixed, finding 6), so the pointers carry no information.
findings.fix: Declare each group as static const char titles_*[][12] with the same initialiser lists and make MemoryCardGroup.titleIds a const char (*)[12]; the count expressions, the strcmp lookup and the host test keep working. A mechanical edit of 97 declarations and one struct field.
findings.benefit: ~4 KB of ELF and RAM (MEASURED 4184 B .data in riptopl-per-object.tsv; strings move from .rodata.str into the arrays at the same 12 B, minus ~144 B of string merging lost for 12 repeated IDs, INFERRED).
findings.evidence: evidence/RiptOPL/raw/riptopl-per-object.tsv: vmc_groups.o text 224, rodata 1164 (allMemoryCardGroups, nm size 0x48c = 97 x 12), data 4184. grep -cE over indented string lines of vmc_groups.cpp: 1046 titles. tests/host/test_vmc_groups.cpp:22-28 reads g.titleIds[j] into a const char *, which an array row decays to. The 12-character SSCES_540.95 would not fit a [12] row, so finding 6 comes first.

findings.title: Glyph cache pages of 256 entries (9 KB each) make CJK text cost ~0.7 MB of mostly empty cache per font
findings.problem: The cache is paged by codepoint/256, and each page is malloc'd whole: 256 x 36-byte entries = 9,216 B. CJK ideographs are spread over U+4E00-9FFF, so a few hundred distinct characters touch dozens of pages, each almost empty. Pages are freed only when the font is flushed. Counting the codepoints in lng/fork/Japanese, SChinese and TChinese.yml gives 74, 76 and 81 distinct pages: 666-729 KB per font once those strings have been drawn, for 578-746 used entries.
findings.fix: Lower GLYPH_CACHE_PAGE_SIZE to 32. The code already uses only the constant (/ and %). Optionally also narrow the entry's int fields to short.
findings.benefit: INFERRED from the lang files: at 32 entries a page is 1,152 B, so 239-340 pages = 269-382 KB instead of 666-729 KB per CJK font (~350-400 KB saved per font in the worst case). Latin fonts save ~10-18 KB each. The pointer array grows to at most 8 KB.
findings.evidence: Read fontsystem.h:22 (GLYPH_CACHE_PAGE_SIZE 256) and 43-59 (entry: 7 ints + 2 pointers = 36 B on the 32-bit EE), and fntsys.cpp:187-221 (page malloc of 256 entries) and 593-602. grep GLYPH_CACHE_PAGE_SIZE: used only at fntsys.cpp:155, 209, 214, 594, 595. A Python count of distinct (codepoint // N) over lng/fork/*.yml: Japanese 74 pages at 256, 239 at 32; SChinese 76 / 305; TChinese 81 / 340; Korean 43 / 194. That assumes every string of the language is drawn before a flush, so it is an upper bound.

findings.title: NIBBLE2CHAR emits 'k'..'p' for 10..15, so the SOS/Disaster Report hook can patch the wrong IOP module
findings.problem: NIBBLE2CHAR returns 'a' + n for n >= 10, i.e. 'k'..'p' instead of 'a'..'f'. SOS_SifLoadModuleHook uses it to pass IREMSND's IOP module ID as two hex digits (patches.c:565-570), and iremsndpatch parses the argument with strtol(argv[1], NULL, 16) (main.c:65). For an ID like 0x2A the argument is "2k", strtol returns 2, and iremsndpatch writes its JAL/JMP words at fixed offsets into module 2's text (main.c:87-108). With a high nibble of A-F the parse gives 0 and the fix is silently skipped.
findings.fix: Change the second branch of NIBBLE2CHAR to 'a' + (n) - 10.
findings.benefit: Fixes IOP code corruption (crash or hang) in Disaster Report and Zettai Zetsumei Toshi whenever IREMSND's module ID has a low nibble of A-F; one character, no size change (INFERRED)
findings.evidence: Read patches.c:160 (macro) and :509-579 (only user); grep -rn NIBBLE2CHAR over the repo: only patches.c:160,565,566. Read modules/iopcore/patches/iremsndpatch/main.c fully: strtol base 16 at :65, module lookup by id at :70-76, fixed-offset writes at :87-108. patch_list entries SLUS_205.61 / SLES_513.01 / SLPS_251.13 (patches.c:113-115) reach SOSPatch; the PAL hook is commented out (patches.c:592-594), so the NTSC-U and NTSC-J titles are affected. INFERRED part: IOP module IDs are small sequential numbers, so which nibble IREMSND gets depends on how many modules the device mode loads.

findings.title: fmCopy / fmCopyThenDelete clean up an FM_ERR_EXISTS failure by deleting the file or folder that was already at the target
findings.problem: A failed copy is undone with fmDeleteTree(dst) whatever the error. FM_ERR_EXISTS means the target's create was refused because something is already there (O_EXCL open 332-338, mkdir 400-401), i.e. fmTarget's fmExists (156-172, one try) wrongly said 'not there'; the cleanup then removes that pre-existing file or folder tree, the case O_EXCL was added to stop. The file's own header (11-12) says the first card access after a card is detected answers 'changed card', and for a file the opendir fallback cannot succeed. Trigger: copy a file, swap the memory card in that slot (listing not refreshed), paste where the new card has the same name: open fails once, O_EXCL fails, fmExists now says yes, remove(dst) deletes the card's file.
findings.fix: In fmCopy and fmCopyThenDelete, skip the fmDeleteTree(dst) cleanup when fmErr is FM_ERR_EXISTS; keep it for every other error.
findings.justification: One condition in two places. It is the smallest change that stops a refused create from deleting the user's existing file or save folder; an FM_ERR_EXISTS can only arise where this call made nothing at that path (a nested one needs two source names the target treats as one, where keeping the partial copy is the safe side).
findings.benefit: Closes a memory-card data-loss path (an existing save file or folder deleted on paste). No size change.
findings.evidence: Read filemgr.cpp 156-172 (fmExists: one open with fmDevPath, then opendir on the raw path), 315-372 (fmCopyFile: O_EXCL retries x4 on mc, then fmFail(fmExists(dst) ? FM_ERR_EXISTS : FM_ERR_WRITE)), 390-413, 424-433 (fmTarget), 453-466 (fmCopy cleanup), 468-477 (fmRemove), 564-585. Caller: guifilemgr.cpp fmPaste 428-485 runs fmCopy/fmMove on the GUI thread with mc paths in mc0:/ form (fmScanDrives 204). The changed-card behaviour on the first access is the code's own statement at filemgr.cpp:11-12 (INFERRED that it applies after a swap in an open listing); whether mcman honours O_EXCL was not checked (if not, the same false negative overwrites instead).

findings.title: Every config entry is a fixed 308-byte node (48-byte key + 256-byte value) regardless of content
findings.problem: allocConfigItem mallocs sizeof(config_value_t) = 48 + 256 + 4 = 308 bytes (plus malloc header) for every key, although typical keys are under 30 bytes and most values are a few digits. The five global sets (settings, last, apps, network, game) stay loaded for the whole menu session; include/config.h defines 137 CONFIG_OPL_* and 47 CONFIG_ITEM_* key names, so the resident sets hold on the order of 150-250 nodes.
findings.fix: Allocate each node with its key and value at their real lengths (one malloc: header + key + NUL + value + NUL) and reallocate the node only when setStr stores a longer value. Callers that keep a getStr() pointer across a setStr of the same key must be checked first, since such a pointer would then dangle.
findings.benefit: INFERRED: ~200 resident nodes x ~280 unused bytes = ~55 KB EE heap returned; per-game sets loaded at launch shrink the same way. Not measured.
findings.evidence: Read configset.h:13-20 (key[CONFIG_KEY_NAME_LEN], val[CONFIG_KEY_VALUE_LEN], next), config.h:265-269 (48 and 256), config.cpp:229-241 (malloc(sizeof(config_value_t)) per entry), 363-386 (setStr overwrites val in place), 389-399 (getStr returns a pointer into val). git grep -c on include/config.h: 137 '#define CONFIG_OPL_* "' and 47 '#define CONFIG_ITEM_* "'. Theme config is freed after load (themes.cpp:1814), so it is not counted. Entry counts per set were not measured.

findings.title: HDD exact archive and generic sweep share one TAR_KIND_ART slot: mixed Favourites/Apps lists reload the whole index per cover
findings.problem: cacheResolveArtArchive picks the HDD archive per row (mode 1) for HDD-origin Favourites/Apps rows and the generic sweep (mode 0) for others. artTarLoadImageExact calls tarLoadFile, which drops a generic index. artTarLoadImage calls tarFindPrefix, which drops any exact index (s_isExact) and runs tarLoadFromAnyDevice from gDevices[0]. So in a list that alternates HDD and USB/SMB/MMCE games, each change of source frees the index, opens device archives again and re-reads the whole sidecar (64 bytes per member) or rescans the tar, all on the art worker.
findings.fix: Give the HDD exact archive its own kind slot (one more TarKind with ART's entry size and cache name, used only by artTarLoadImageExact) so both indexes stay resident. Then delete the s_isExact close-and-reload branches in tarLoadFromAnyDevice, tarFind and tarFindPrefix.
findings.justification: The extra slot is the cause-level fix: the reloads exist only because two archives share one slot. Cost is the second index's RAM (64 bytes per member, held only when an HDD archive exists). It removes about as many lines of s_isExact handling as it adds.
findings.benefit: Removes a full index reload plus up to 12 device open() probes per HDD/non-HDD alternation (INFERRED; a 3000-member pack is a 192 KB sidecar read; artload.cpp:44 notes a missed open can cost ~4.3 s)
findings.evidence: Read tar.cpp:389-458 and 467-574: tarLoadFile early-returns only when s_isExact and the same path, else tarCloseInternal; tarFind/tarFindPrefix call tarCloseInternal when s_isExact, then tarLoadFromAnyDevice sweeps from gDevices[0] (s_dev cleared). texcache.cpp:180-207: HDD support and FAV/APP rows whose source is HDD_MODE return hddGetArtArchivePath (hddsupport.cpp:3212-3221, "<prefix>ART/art.tar"), others return 0. artload.cpp:659-666 dispatches per request. The cost per reload is INFERRED from the code path (sidecar read in tarReadCache, opens in tarLoadFromAnyDevice). Not measured on hardware.

findings.title: readFileBuffer hands lang.cpp a pointer into its own buffer for an empty line; the buffer is freed and the pointer is later passed to free()
findings.problem: With allocResult set, readFileBuffer only mallocs a copy when lineSize is non-zero; an empty line (or a lone CR) returns 1 with *outBuf = lastPtr, an address inside fileBuffer->buffer. lngLoadFromFile (the only allocResult=1 caller) stores it in newL[], calls closeFileBuffer (frees the buffer), then reads it in lngFormatFits and frees it at lang.cpp:183 or in lngFreeFromFile (language switch, and lngEnd in deinitEx before every launch). One blank line in a lang_*.lng is a use-after-free plus an invalid free of an interior pointer: newlib heap corruption. The copy's malloc is also unchecked (memcpy to NULL on OOM).
findings.fix: In readFileBuffer drop the lineSize test so every returned line is a heap copy when allocResult is set, and return 0 if that malloc fails.
findings.justification: The added NULL check stops a NULL memcpy on allocation failure; dropping the lineSize test removes code. Together they close a heap corruption reachable from a user-supplied language file.
findings.benefit: Fixes heap corruption (invalid free at language switch or game-launch teardown) triggered by any blank line in a .lng file; net about +1 line.
findings.evidence:
Traced readFileBuffer for input 'a

b
': 2nd call finds posLF==lastPtr, lineSize=0, skips the malloc at 631 and returns buffer+2. grep openFileBuffer( over src: allocResult=1 only at lang.cpp:163 (config.cpp:1190,1377,1402,1578 pass 0). lang.cpp:170 stores the pointer, :173 closeFileBuffer frees buffer (util.cpp:694), :178 lngFormatFits reads it, :183 frees it on mismatch; lngFreeFromFile (lang.cpp:42-53) frees the first nValidEntries entries; lngEnd (lang.cpp:459-461) runs from deinitEx (opl.cpp:1363). lang_compiler.py:158 writes one line per string, so an empty translation is an empty line; custom .lng files are loaded from devices (lngAddLanguages).

findings.title: findDuplicate shares the first COV cache whatever slot count the later element needs: synthesized Coverflow/Grid/PSBBN views can get a 2-slot cache
findings.problem: initMutableImage links any earlier element's cache with the same suffix (findDuplicate) and only creates its own cache when none was linked, so the FIRST COV element's slot count wins. A GameImage with pattern=COV gets count 1 floored to 2. For a disk theme without views=, thmViewSynthesize appends the template presenter after the theme's last main block, so a Coverflow (wants 20), PSBBN flow or Grid (wants 2 x cells, up to 48) built after such a GameImage shares its 2-slot cache. The eviction scan never takes an entry used this frame, so only 2 covers of the carousel/grid ever load; the rest stay on the default picture.
findings.fix: In findDuplicate, share a cache only when its count() is at least the slot count the new element asked for (pass cacheCount in from initMutableImage); otherwise let the element create its own cache as it already does when nothing matches.
findings.justification: Adds one parameter and one condition. The cache has no resize, so refusing an undersized share is the smallest change that gives presenters the slots their own code computes (grid.cpp:663-671, coverflow COVER_CACHE_SLOTS); the cost is at most a duplicate decode of the selected cover in the small GameImage cache.
findings.benefit: Fixes permanently missing covers (all but 2) in synthesized Coverflow/Grid/PSBBN views of disk themes that declare a GameImage pattern=COV before the presenter. Theme population affected is INFERRED.
findings.evidence: Read findDuplicate (themeelems.cpp:633-677) and initMutableImage (808-909): count from _count, floor 2 at 852-853, link before cacheInitCache at 884-891. themes.cpp:700-702 GameImage passes count 1; themes.cpp:1480-1491 synthesizes undeclared views for disk themes; themeviews.cpp:393,404-413 presenter types exclude GameImage, 495 copies it unchanged, 513-528 appends presenter after last block. coverflow.cpp:356 asks COVER_CACHE_SLOTS (20, themeint.h:76); grid.cpp:666-671 asks 2*cells. texcache.cpp:396-407 skips entries with lastUsed == guiFrameId. grep cacheResize/cacheGrow/count_ = : only texcache.cpp:59 (init), no resize. Built-in cfgs (misc/*.cfg) have no COV GameImage before a presenter, so only disk themes hit it (INFERRED).

findings.title: vmcsaves: names read from a VMC image are not validated before vsWriteFolder joins them into a path, so an export can write outside SAVES/
findings.problem: vsLoadVmc copies the save name (453) and every file name (469) straight from the card's directory entries, and vsWriteFolder joins them into parent + save + '/' + file (727, 739) and opens that with O_CREAT|O_TRUNC (740). vsLoadPsu checks the same names with vsNameOk (796, 822) and vsWritePsu checks the save name (867), but the VMC-to-folder export (vmcSavesExport, guigame.cpp:442) checks nothing. A crafted VMC whose save holds a file named like '../../../X' makes the export create or truncate X outside the save folder on a device whose path layer resolves '..'.
findings.fix: Check the names where they enter, as vsLoadPsu does: in vsLoadVmc fail with VMCSAVES_ERR_NAME when vsNameOk(s->name) or vsNameOk(f->name) is false. The save-name check in vsWritePsu (867-868) then covers every source (folder and PSU sources are already checked) and can be deleted.
findings.justification: Adds two checks with an existing helper: they close a path traversal from untrusted VMC images (shared save cards) into the rest of the drive, and the now-redundant check in vsWritePsu goes, so the net change is about one line.
findings.benefit: Closes an overwrite-outside-the-folder path on VMC export (HDD/SMB/NFS); net about +1 line (INFERRED: +3 in vsLoadVmc, -2 in vsWritePsu).
findings.evidence: Read vmcsaves.cpp 440-491 (vsLoadVmc, no name check), 720-751 (vsWriteFolder joins s->name and f->name), 766-770 (vsNameOk), 780-843 (vsLoadPsu checks at 796 and 822), 860-868 (vsWritePsu: comment says a card name like ../x never leaves the folder). Caller guigame.cpp:442 vmcSavesExport(card, vmcSavesCard[pick].name, folder) with folder = <card dir>SAVES/ built at guigame.cpp:420. USB/MX4SIO go through FatFs with FF_FS_RPATH 0 (modules/bdm/bdmfs_fatfs/fatfs/include/ffconf.h:156), which rejects '..', so the exposed devices are pfs (HDD), SMB and NFS: INFERRED that those resolve '..' (pfs keeps '..' directory entries; its source is not in this repo).

findings.title: Xerabora cache keeps a fixed 1024-entry achievement_entry_t array (232 KB) for the rest of the session
findings.problem: achievementsParseXerabora mallocs XERA_LIST_MAX (1024) entries of achievement_entry_t for every parse and keeps the block as xeraList; nothing frees it (achievementsForget only marks it stale). A game set is typically tens of entries and a library a few hundred, so most of the 237,568-byte block is held unused for the whole menu session, and each refetch briefly holds the old list, the new one and the 512 KB document together.
findings.fix: After the parse loop, shrink the list to count entries with realloc (keep the original block if realloc fails or count is 0).
findings.justification: Two added lines return roughly 200 KB of EE heap that is otherwise pinned for the session after the browser is first opened in Xerabora mode; no new state or option.
findings.benefit: INFERRED: sizeof(achievement_entry_t) = 5 ints (20) + 33+57+101+20 chars = 231, padded 232; 1024 x 232 = 237,568 B held; a 100-entry set needs 23,200 B, so ~210 KB freed (RA editions only).
findings.evidence: Read achievements.cpp:144-146 (XERA_DOC_MAX 512 KB, XERA_LIST_MAX 1024), :356 malloc, :383-385 free old + keep new, :427-436 512 KB doc per fetch, :656-660 achievementsForget only sets flags. grep -n xeraList over src: only achievements.cpp (no other free). Struct at achievements.h:17-21. Compiled only with RETROACHIEVEMENTS (file wrapped in #ifdef at :4).

findings.title: ArtIndex::build allocates 4096-entry hash and picture tables plus a 16 KB name buffer per directory and never trims them
findings.problem: Every indexed directory gets hashes = 4096 x 4 B = 16 KB and pics = 4096 x 8 B = 32 KB at full kMaxEntries size, and names starts at 16 KB; the slot keeps these exact sizes until the round-robin rebuilds that slot (invalidate() only marks slots unusable). A 200-entry POPS or ART folder needs about 7 KB but holds 64 KB; a 2000-picture ART folder needs ~72 KB but holds ~112 KB. With three slots that is roughly 120-170 KB of EE heap held for nothing.
findings.fix: After the sort and before publishing (lines 275-286), shrink each buffer to what the sweep used: realloc hashes to n entries, pics to picCount entries and names to namesUsed bytes, keeping the original pointer when realloc returns NULL or the count is zero.
findings.justification: Adds three or four realloc lines; the concrete problem is 40-57 KB of heap per held directory slot that no code ever reads, and shrinking in place is the smallest change that returns it.
findings.benefit: ~40-57 KB heap per valid slot, ~120-170 KB with three slots (INFERRED: 16 KB + 32 KB fixed tables and 16 KB name floor vs 12 B per entry + name bytes actually used).
findings.evidence: Read artindex.cpp:147-290 (malloc(kMaxEntries*sizeof(unsigned int)) at 191, malloc(kMaxEntries*sizeof(Pic)) at 199, namesSize = 16*1024 at 200, growth only by doubling at 230-239, published unchanged at 281-286), release() at 92-102 called only from build() line 154, invalidate() at 421-435 frees nothing. artindexint.h:29-38 kSlots=3, kMaxEntries=4096, kNamesMax=128 KB; Pic is two 4-byte fields (40-44). Directory sizes are examples, not measured.

findings.title: Undecodable art files are retried back-to-back forever: decode failures are reported as transient to the art cache
findings.problem: A present art file that cannot be decoded returns ERR_SET_JMP (corrupt PNG, PNG over 1024 px via png_set_user_limits, neither PNG nor JPG), ERR_BAD_DIMENSION (e.g. an 800x600 RGBA PNG over maxSize) or ERR_BAD_DEPTH (16-bit PNG). texDiscoverArt passes these up unchanged and artload.cpp:746 treats every result other than ERR_BAD_FILE as transient: it clears the slot, and texcache re-claims it on the next frame (only SIO2 devices have an idle gate). So the art worker reloads the same file in a loop for as long as the game is on screen, each cycle a full open and read (two of each for a .png name, finding 2).
findings.fix: Treat decode failures of a file that was read completely as absent: in texDiscoverArt return ERR_BAD_FILE for ERR_SET_JMP, ERR_BAD_DIMENSION and ERR_BAD_DEPTH (or let artload.cpp:746 retry only ERR_FILE_IO and the libpng-struct OOM codes). So a mid-read network error on the streaming reader stays transient, have texReadFileFunction mark its reader when read() fails and make the setjmp handler return ERR_FILE_IO in that case.
findings.justification: Adds a flag in tex_file_reader_t and one mapping (about 4 lines). It fixes a real endless reload loop that occupies the art worker and the device bus (shared with BGM on USB, with the pad on MMCE/MX4SIO). It is the smallest change that keeps the issue #388 rule that only real I/O failures retry.
findings.benefit: Ends an indefinite reload loop per broken art file on screen. INFERRED: a 2 MB 1280x720 PNG background read twice per cycle on USB at about 1 MB/s is about 4 s of device time per cycle, repeated while selected, delaying every other cover behind it.
findings.evidence: Read textures.cpp texLoadAll 880-1115 (setjmp handler returns ERR_SET_JMP, user limits 1035, ERR_BAD_DEPTH 1041-1042/1101-1105, ERR_BAD_DIMENSION 1108-1111), texReadFileFunction 477-483 (read failure -> png_error -> ERR_SET_JMP), texLoadArtFile 1328-1334, texFindArt 1360, texDiscoverArt 1404-1408. Callers: BdmSource::image bdmsupport.cpp:2092-2097, ethsupport.cpp:1566-1571, udpfssupport.cpp:1213-1218, hddsupport.cpp:2958, mmcesupport.cpp:662, appsupport.cpp:1381 return the result unchanged to artload.cpp:670. artload.cpp:746-751 clears on result != ERR_BAD_FILE; texcache.cpp:24-42 cacheClearItem wipes key; texcache.cpp:305-339 then finds no key, 372-378 gates only isSio2, 422-470 enqueues a new request. grep transientFail: only the counter at artload.cpp:747 and its getter, no retry cap.

findings.title: tarInvalidate(TAR_KIND_ART) frees the art index from the GUI/IO thread while the art worker is using it
findings.problem: The ART index (s_index/s_count/s_cap/s_dev) has no lock. All lookups, parses and reads run on the art worker (priority 72, artload.cpp:659-666), but applyConfig(...,0) from many settings pages and the Artwork toggle call tarInvalidate on the GUI thread (31), which preempts the worker at every wake. If it lands while the worker is blocked in a header read inside tarParseFile, the partial index is freed, parsing continues from mid-archive, and tarWriteCache stores that truncated index with the full tar size, so every later boot accepts it. s_dev is also cleared, so every tarRead fails for the session. If it lands inside artTarDecode, tarRead reads entry->offset and rawSize from freed memory.
findings.fix: Do not free from the foreign thread: tarInvalidate only sets a per-kind volatile flag; tarFind, tarFindPrefix, tarLoadFile and tarLoadFromAnyDevice (all called on the art worker) check it at entry, clear it, call tarCloseInternal and clear s_inactive. Nothing else changes.
findings.justification: Adds one flag and a 3-line check. It removes a real use-after-free and a corrupt sidecar that persists across boots. A semaphore like the THM one would make the GUI thread wait out multi-second device reads, so the deferred flag is the smallest safe change.
findings.benefit: Removes a use-after-free and a truncated art_cache.bin that hides covers until the archive changes size (paths READ; the race timing is INFERRED; needs gEnableArtTar on)
findings.evidence: grep tarInvalidate over src: settingsio.cpp:2480 (applyConfig with skipDeviceRefresh==0; called from guisettings.cpp:404,1044,1297,2408,2550,2859,2984,3093 on the GUI thread and settingsio.cpp:1970/opl.cpp:1735 at boot) and guisettings.cpp:1804. ART lookups and reads only from artload.cpp:89-136, run by cacheArtWorkerThread (artload.cpp:765-813, ART_THREAD_PRIORITY 72 at :31). grep cacheHoldArtStarts/cacheShutdownArtLoads: only the launch paths in opl.cpp:1299-1308,1393-1402, so nothing pauses the worker around applyConfig. tarReadCache validates only magic, version and tarSize (tar.cpp:137-142), so a short entryCount is accepted. THM has its own lock (tar.cpp:623-655); ART has none.

findings.title: Hold-L3 view switch runs a full thmLoad (cfg, font files, up to 47 PNG probes, two art drains) synchronously on the GUI thread
findings.problem: menuHandleInputMain (GUI thread, screen input dispatch) calls thmCycleView on a 500 ms L3 hold; it reloads the whole theme through setGuiValueLocked -> thmLoad between frames, so no frame is drawn until it returns. For a disk theme that re-reads conf_theme.cfg, every font file (thmLoadFonts, whole TTF reads) and probes/decodes up to 47 icon PNGs from the theme device (SMB, USB, MMCE), plus up to 3 x 500 ms art drains (DelayThread(1000) loops, artload.cpp:442-452); the built-in theme decodes about 100 embedded PNGs. Only the element layout differs between views.
findings.fix: Run the hold-L3 switch through guiHandleDeferedIO(..., IO_CUSTOM_SIMPLEACTION, worker, 0) like the other blocking actions (menusys.cpp:983, guisettings.cpp:953), so the IO worker does the load while the GUI keeps drawing a busy message; thmLoad already publishes under the GUI lock for IO-thread loads (themes.cpp:1828-1844).
findings.justification: Adds a two-line void wrapper and one call. Problem: a frozen frame for the whole reload on every hold-L3 (seconds for a disk theme on a network share, INFERRED). Reusing the existing deferred-IO wait is the smallest change that keeps the UI responsive without restructuring thmLoad.
findings.benefit: Removes a frozen frame on each view switch: INFERRED hundreds of ms (built-in theme, ~100 PNG decodes) to seconds (disk theme over SMB: cfg + fonts + up to 47 file probes); not measured on hardware
findings.evidence: Call path: guiscreens.cpp:19/97 dispatch -> menuHandleInputMain (menusys.cpp:2780) -> menuHandleViewHold -> thmCycleView (menusys.cpp:2776) -> thmSetViewLocked (themes.cpp:2203) -> setGuiValueLocked(..., 1) (2146) -> thmLoad (2035). thmLoad comment themes.cpp:1831-1832 says the view switch runs between frames. Texture loads counted from textures.h enum: LOAD0-7 (8), BDM_ICON..START_ICON (23), INDEX2_0..INDEX4_3 (9), UDPFS (1), L3..FAV_MARK (4), L1/R1 (2) = 47 thmLoadResource calls, each one texDiscoverLoad .png probe (textures.cpp:1411-1437); built-in adds ELF_FORMAT..VMODE_PAL (44) and 9 logos. Drain waits: artload.cpp:426-455 (ticks are 1 ms DelayThread). guiHandleDeferedIO: guiwait.cpp:149-153. Duration not measured.

findings.title: hiddenLists reserves 512 name slots for each of 15 modes: 40,920 bytes of .bss for lists that are usually empty
findings.problem: hidden_list_t embeds names[HIDDEN_MAX] pointers and ps1[HIDDEN_MAX] flags (gamemanage.cpp:33-39) and hiddenLists has one per MODE_COUNT (15) mode (41): MEASURED 40,920 bytes of .bss. APP, FAV and HTTP can never hold a list (hiddenPrefix 60-62), and a device's hidden list is normally a handful of names.
findings.fix: Replace the two fixed arrays with one heap array of {name, ps1} entries per list, grown with realloc in hiddenAppend and freed in hiddenClear; keep HIDDEN_MAX as the cap and keep prefix/loaded/count static.
findings.justification: About 38 KB of EE RAM is reserved for the whole run by a feature that is usually unused; a growable array is about 6 extra lines.
findings.benefit: MEASURED 40,920 B .bss (BUILD-EVIDENCE.md:113) -> about 2.6 KB (15 x 176 B) plus heap per hidden game; ~38 KB RAM saved.
findings.evidence: evidence/RiptOPL/BUILD-EVIDENCE.md:113 lists hiddenLists 40,920 b and :125 gamemanage.o .bss 40,924. Arithmetic: 160 + 4 + 4 + 512*4 + 512 = 2,728 B x 15 = 40,920. MODE_COUNT = 15 from include/iosupport.h:10-28. Only names/ps1/count are touched: hiddenClear 70-75, hiddenAppend 77-88, hiddenFind 126-132, hiddenSave 156-174, hiddenSet 176-220, all in this file.

findings.title: Custom Settings Path is ignored at boot whenever the boot folder still holds a settings file
findings.problem: config.path is read only inside tryAlternateDevice, and _loadConfig and miniInit call that only when the boot home has no master file. Choosing a Custom Settings Path writes the settings only to the new folder and leaves the old settings_riptopl.cfg beside the ELF as it was. The next boot loads that stale file (custom path empty) and never reads config.path, so every change saved since appears lost, and the next save goes back to the boot folder.
findings.fix: Check the redirect before trusting the boot home: move the readConfigPathRedirect / prepareCustomSettingsPath block out of tryAlternateDevice into the first read in _loadConfig and miniInit, and fall back to the boot home when the redirect target has no master.
findings.justification: The setting is documented as a folder to read and save settings in instead of the default, but it fails for every user who saved settings before choosing a path. Moving the existing check costs one small open() of config.path per boot and adds no new mechanism.
findings.benefit: Fixes a settings-revert bug for Custom Settings Path users who already had settings in the boot folder; costs one extra small file open per boot (INFERRED)
findings.evidence: Read settingsio.cpp:1546-1563 (first configReadMulti; tryAlternateDevice only when !(result & CONFIG_OPL)), 938-984 (the only readConfigPathRedirect call), 2367-2402 (explicit save: configSetMove(customSettingsTarget) then configWriteChecked; the boot-home master is neither rewritten nor removed), opl.cpp:1885-1895 (miniInit has the same shape). config.cpp:345-355 rename() only changes the filename; grep remove/unlink in config.cpp: none. grep readConfigPathRedirect: settingsio.cpp:296 (definition) and :964 only. The user flow was traced in code, not run on hardware.

findings.title: R3 handlers keep pointers into gFavSupport's array and the menu row across blocking card I/O while the higher-priority IO worker can free both
findings.problem: itemExecFav runs on the GUI thread (prio 31) after endFrame drops the GUI lock (gui.cpp:368-374). toggleByIndex writes r->starred through r = &array_[i] after addItem/removeByIdAndText card I/O (1769-1774); removeByIndex reuses the array text after I/O (1086-1095); recentRecord copies fav->text (menuitems.cpp:93-95) only after favReadFile (1492-1507); itemExecFav writes it->favourited after I/O (menuitems.cpp:418-423). While the GUI waits on the card RPC, the prio-30 IO worker can run a queued FAV rebuild: clearMenuGameList frees the rows (opl.cpp:712) and update() calls clear(), freeing array_ and texts (1183, 789-800). Every other list rebuild queues one (opl.cpp:908-909).
findings.fix: In toggleByIndex and removeByIndex copy mode, id, kind, starred and the text into locals before the I/O, and afterwards touch array_ only if validIndex(favIndex) still holds and that entry's text equals the copy. In itemExecFav re-read curMenu->current after the call instead of writing through the old it, and in itemRecordRecent pass a local copy of fav->text.
findings.justification: Closes a write to freed heap reachable from a button press (for example R3 on All Games while the apps scan it arms at 1630-1632, a boot device scan or a hotplug list lands). Local copies and one re-check (~8 lines) are the smallest fix; no new lock is needed.
findings.benefit: Removes a use-after-free write that can corrupt the EE heap or star the wrong row; about +8 lines (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read gui.cpp:114-132 (startFrame locks, endFrame unlocks) and 335-379 (dispatchInput after endFrame); menusys.cpp:2842-2844 calls item->fav directly. opl.cpp:690-741: IO-thread updateMenuFromGameList calls clearMenuGameList (guiLock only inside, 460-476) then gsOf->update; FavSource::update 1181-1186 calls gFavSupport.clear() which frees texts and array_ (789-800). artMode note 910-918 states IO worker prio 30 outranks GUI prio 31. INFERRED part: the timing window (a FAV rebuild must be queued while the GUI thread is blocked in the R3 file I/O).

findings.title: bdmUpdateDeviceData fast reappearance path republishes the old list for whatever volume now holds the slot
findings.problem: A confirmed disconnect (bdmdevices 437-449) hides the page but keeps root/driver/type, and the rescan it triggers keeps the old list because sbReadList retains it when the device is gone (supportbase 707-714). Any later mount in that slot is treated as 'reappeared intact' (286-309): page shown, return 0, so needsUpdate stops at 1817 before the CD/DVD mtime and ul.cfg checks. Swap stick A for stick B and B's tab shows A's games and art until a manual refresh. The path also skips the publish gates at 373-390: a page of a disabled transport is re-shown on every generation bump and hidden again on the next poll (bdmsupport 1725-1734), and BDM=Off is not honoured.
findings.fix: In the fast path, return without showing the page when bdmTransportEnabled(type)==0 or the explicit BDM-Off gate applies. Then let BdmSource::needsUpdate still run its cheap CD/DVD mtime and ul.cfg size comparison for a restored page (for example a distinct return value that skips the connect sound and folder creation). A stall on the same volume costs two stats, and a different volume gets a normal rebuild.
findings.justification: Adds about 8 lines. It fixes a wrong game list (and launches of titles that are not on the inserted device) without bringing back the full rescan on every transient stall, which is what the fast path was added to avoid. Reusing the existing mtime/size checks is the smallest change that can tell two volumes apart.
findings.benefit: Correct list after a device swap; no tab flash or FAV rebuild per hotplug for a disabled transport (INFERRED from the traced call chain).
findings.evidence: Read bdmdevices.cpp:209-456, bdmsupport.cpp:1698-1878 (needsUpdate), 1880-1921 (update), 899-943 (event handler only bumps BdmGeneration), supportbase.cpp:534-725 (sbReadList keeps list and fsize on total read failure), opl.cpp:690-742 and 1006-1056 (gen bump queues IO_MENU_UPDATE_DEFFERED). Grep for bdmDeviceRoot[0] =, bdmDriver[0] =, bdmULSizePrev = -2 over src: identity is never cleared on removal (only bdmsupport.cpp:1624, 2008, 2037 set -2). INFERRED: that bdm gives the freed massN slot to the next device that mounts.

findings.title: Four virtual host:: service interfaces have one implementation each, and most members are pure forwarders
findings.problem: UiServices, AppServices, LibraryServices and LaunchServices are abstract classes with exactly one product implementation each (OplUi, OplApp, OplLibrary, OplLaunch in host.cpp); OplUi/OplApp/OplLibrary only forward to existing free functions. The only substitute is a no-op UiServices in tests/host/host_env.h, and hostmap.py exists just to rewrite host:: calls back into the old function names so source-scraping tests still work. The cost is 4 vtables plus RTTI and ~45 forwarder thunks in the shipped ELF and an indirect call per use.
findings.fix: Replace the classes with a plain header of free-function prototypes (the decoupling the header was written for only needs declarations, not virtual dispatch) and call guiMsgBox/libViewActive/... directly; keep OplLaunch's real logic as free functions. Tests substitute by linking their own definitions, as host_env.h already does for ziso_init/ziso_read_sector. Then delete hostmap.py and its imports.
findings.benefit: MEASURED: the 79 host-layer symbols (vtables, typeinfo, forwarders, accessors) total 1863 B in riptopl-nm-size-sorted.full.txt; about 1.3 KB of that is vtable/RTTI/forwarder overhead (INFERRED, OplLaunch logic ~0.5 KB stays). ~150 lines (host.cpp forwarders, class boilerplate, hostmap.py).
findings.evidence: Read host.h, host.cpp, hostmap.py, tests/host/host_env.h. Regex scan over src,tests,ee_core: 'Services\s*&' only in host.cpp:289-292 and host_env.h:63 (no other implementation). Per-method call counts collected (e.g. msgBox 71, warning 52, listViewActive 29). nm (evidence/RiptOPL/raw/riptopl-nm-size-sorted.full.txt): _ZTV OplUi 0x5c, OplApp 0x54, OplLibrary 0x30, OplLaunch 0x28, typeinfo names/objects, 45 OplUi/OplApp/OplLibrary text thunks totalling 796 B; all host-layer symbols 1863 B. Call-site rewrite touches ~560 occurrences across 74 files, hence effort L.

findings.title: pad.h and sound.h sfx* functions are pure forwarders to a single static PadManager / SoundEffects instance
findings.problem: Sixteen pad.h functions (pad.cpp:1244-1322) and four sfx* functions (sfx.cpp:421-439) only call the same-named method on one file-static object (gPads, gSfx); no other instance or caller of the classes exists. unloadPads goes through two forwarders (unloadPads -> PadManager::unload -> unloadEx(0)). The build already inlines the members into the wrappers: the linker map lists the out-of-line PadManager copies as discarded, so the layer is source weight only.
findings.fix: Keep one API: either make the methods the pad.h/sound.h functions over file-static state (the shape before the class conversion), or let the few callers use the object directly. At minimum delete PadManager::unload and call unloadEx(0) from unloadPads.
findings.benefit: ~100 source lines (wrappers ~105, public class declarations ~35, offset by moving state to file statics); no ELF change, MEASURED: riptopl-discarded-firstparty.txt shows the out-of-line PadManager members already removed by --gc-sections
findings.evidence: Read pad.cpp:1240-1322, sfx.cpp:417-439, padmanager.h, soundeffects.h. Grep PadManager|SoundEffects over the repo: only pad.cpp, sfx.cpp, the two headers, docs/CPP-CONVERSION-PLAN.md:389 (states the free functions 'forward to it') and five .github/scripts source-text tests (test_pad_repeat_clock.py etc., which would need their extraction patterns updated). evidence/RiptOPL/raw/riptopl-discarded-firstparty.txt lists 20 .text._ZN10PadManager* sections of pad.o as discarded (1,564 bytes, BUILD-EVIDENCE.md:231).

findings.title: Include blocks of autolaunch.cpp and lwnbdctl.cpp are copied from opl.cpp; most headers and their comments do not apply
findings.problem: Both files carry the ~60-line opl.cpp include list verbatim (dupes-blocks.tsv: autolaunch.cpp:9-65 == lwnbdctl.cpp:10-66, also matching opl.cpp, appscan.cpp, settingsio.cpp, menuitems.cpp). autolaunch.cpp uses only oplint/opl/ioman/config/util/supportbase/bdmsupport/hddsupport/menusys and fileXio_rpc; lwnbdctl.cpp uses oplint/oplog/opl/ioman/gui/lang/texcache/pad/system/util/extern_irx/ethsupport/sound. The per-include comments are wrong for these files: lwnbdctl.cpp says fileXio is 'used by BDM autolaunch' and both justify sys/stat.h by an mkdir neither file calls; libds34bt/usb, tar.h, rabadge.h, cheatman.h, xparam.h etc. are unused.
findings.fix: Delete the unused includes and their comments from autolaunch.cpp and lwnbdctl.cpp, keeping only the headers listed above; let the compiler confirm. Apply the same trim to the other split-out copies when their units are touched.
findings.benefit: ~95 source lines removed from the two files (60+61 lines down to ~13+14); faster compiles; no ELF change (INFERRED: headers only).
findings.evidence: Read both files fully and appscan.cpp:1-85. Located each used symbol's declaration with Grep over include/: miniInit/gExportName/deinitAllSupport oplint.h:12-18, AUTOLAUNCH_MASS0_RETRIES oplint.h:10, LOG ioman.h:77, LOG_INIT oplog.h, menuGameRequiresParentalLock menusys.h:201, isValidIsoName supportbase.h:45, bdmReadDriverName/bdmResolveLBA_UDMA/bdmLaunchGame bdmsupport.h, hddLaunchGame hddsupport.h:171, eth* ethsupport.h:22-24, sysIsPccfOwned/sysShutdownDev9/sysLoadModuleBuffer system.h, cache*Timed texcache.h:235-236, startPads/unloadPads pad.h, audio*/sfxInit/bgmStart sound.h, guiMsgBox/guiRenderTextScreen/guiExecDeferredOps gui.h, lwnbdsvr_irx/ps2atad_irx extern_irx.h. findings.title: GSM 'fix' toggles are compile-time constants written at runtime; the engine tests them on every trapped GS write

findings.benefit: ~55 source lines; INFERRED ~45 instructions (~180 bytes) of ee_core ram84 text: 6 handlers x ~6 dead instructions + 5 sites x 3 flag-test instructions; one lb+beql less per trapped GS write
findings.evidence: Grep GSMFlags|_fix over ee_core: C writers only gsm_api.c:109-119 (constants, FIELD_fix/gs576P from args); asm readers gsm_engine.S:596,624,678,697,715,937 and gsm_engine_adv.S:307,345,369,390,415 (lb + beql). findings.title: checkMC always opens four directories even when the first answers the question

findings.title: Concrete mc0:/mc1: boot handling in preferredMcSlot, tryMissingConfigPathRecovery and the tryAlternateDevice legacy fallback is unreachable
findings.problem: tryAlternateDevice returns at 1012-1019 for every concrete MC boot, so tryMissingConfigPathRecovery (only caller 1023) and the legacy block at 1044-1081 never see gBootDir starting mc0:/mc1:; nothing in between rewrites gBootDir. preferredMcSlot's other caller, mcConfigPathRedirect, is only reached under gBootHomeDeferred (311, 360), which is set only for smb/udpfs boots (1398-1400). So preferredMcSlot always returns sysCheckMC(), the mc1-first swap is dead, and the concreteMcHome branch and the sameConcreteMcSlot(gBootDir, concreteMcHome) branch never run.

findings.title: PS2-logo probe (open, CheckPS2Logo, close) copied five times; udpfsLaunchOplCore opens the ISO twice and launch() builds partname twice
findings.problem: The block 'if (gPS2Logo) { fd = open(partname); if (fd >= 0) { EnablePS2Logo = CheckPS2Logo(fd, 0); close(fd); } }' appears five times. In udpfsLaunchOplCore the ISO is opened once for its size (941-947) and then reopened for the logo (948-954), although CheckPS2Logo seeks to 0 itself (util.cpp:796); on UDPFS each open/close is a server round trip. UdpfsSource::launch calls sbCreatePath for the same partname at 1125 and again at 1150.
findings.fix: In udpfsLaunchOplCore run CheckPS2Logo on the fd opened for the size before closing it. In launch() build partname once before the logo check and drop the second sbCreatePath. Optionally add one helper next to CheckPS2Logo (int ps2LogoForFile(const char *path): returns 0 when gPS2Logo is off, else opens, checks, closes) and call it from the other four sites.
findings.justification: The helper replaces five identical 7-line blocks with one-line calls; an 8-line helper leaves about 20 lines net removed, and the udpfs merge saves one network open/close per OPL-core launch.
findings.benefit: ~20-25 lines net (INFERRED: 5 x 7-line blocks -> 5 calls + ~8-line helper, plus 5 lines in udpfsLaunchOplCore); one fewer UDPFS open/close round trip per OPL-core launch.
findings.evidence: Grep 'EnablePS2Logo = CheckPS2Logo(fd, 0)' over src: udpfssupport.cpp:951,1128, ethsupport.cpp:1246,1482, mmcesupport.cpp:1506 (all the same open/check/close shape, read), plus bdmlaunch.cpp:847 which reuses an existing fd. util.cpp:784-797 read: CheckPS2Logo does lseek(fd,0,SEEK_SET) before reading, so sharing the size fd is safe.

findings.title: Remember-last-played block copy-pasted in nine launch paths across the game sources

findings.title: Write-only font-system state: GSCLUT fields, glyph shy, and fntCacheFlushPage clearing pages that are freed next
findings.problem: GSCLUT is used only for FontSystem::clut_; its PSM, ClutPSM and VramClut are written in prepareCLUT and never read (newAtlas sets the surface's ClutPSM itself and reads only clut_.Clut). The glyph field shy is written at 631 and never read. fntCacheFlushPage clears every entry of a page that cacheFlush frees on the very next line, its only call site.
findings.fix: Replace GSCLUT clut_ with a plain u32 *clut_ and delete the GSCLUT typedef; delete the shy field and its store; delete fntCacheFlushPage and its call.
findings.benefit: ~22 lines removed (8-line typedef, 3 stores, shy, 11-line function and call), INFERRED; a few bytes of .bss and code.

findings.title: config.cpp: configSetMove duplicates configInit; configMove and configBuildLegacyOplPath are one-line forwarders

findings.title: bdmDeviceIsATA/bdmGetATADeviceId re-implement the identity and by-type lookup helpers

findings.title: menuRenderMain and menuRenderInfo are the same five-branch dispatcher and re-call the family getter

findings.title: hddUpdateGameListCache detects only partition-name changes, so games.bin keeps stale start_sector/name/size and the next boot launches from it
findings.problem: The rewrite test only asks whether every cached partition_name still exists and whether the counts match. A game reinstalled under the same partition label (new start_sector/size) or retitled in its HDL header leaves games.bin untouched. At the next boot update() publishes the cache without any APA scan (forceUpdate is 0), and the native launch writes the stale game->start_sector into cdvdman's lba_start. The game then fails to boot until the user refreshes. The log labels are also swapped: a cached game missing from the scan is logged as "game added".
findings.fix: Replace the nested partition-name loops with one test: rewrite when the counts differ or memcmp of the two arrays differs. Both arrays are byte-deterministic because hddGetHDLGamelist memsets the records and walks the APA table in a fixed order.
findings.benefit: Fixes a stale-LBA boot failure on the opt-in HDD game list cache. Removes about 18 lines and the O(n*m) strncmp loop (INFERRED from 3155-3176).
findings.evidence: Read hddsupport.cpp 1458-1465 (forceUpdate=0 at init), 1860-1882 (cache published with no scan on the first update, forceUpdate=1 after), 3097-3198 and 2779 (lba_start from game->start_sector). Read platform/hdd.cpp 165-249: records are memset and filled in APA dirent order, start_sector comes from private_5. gHDDGameListCache defaults to 0 (core/settings.cpp:91), so the feature is opt-in. INFERRED part: that PC install tools reuse the same partition label when the same game is reinstalled. The Neutrino leg resolves by partition name, so only the native core is hit.

findings.title: texLoadArtFile opens and reads a .png art file twice when its bytes are not a PNG (JPG-in-.png, corrupt PNG)
findings.problem: For a .png name, texLoad -> texLoadAll opens the file and (on mmce/mass) stages it whole, then libpng fails on the signature and the buffer is freed. texLoadArtFile then calls texLoadJpgFile, which opens the same path again (another FAT directory walk, which the comments at 533-546 measure in seconds on big ART folders) and reads the whole file again just to test for a JPG. This happens on every load of a JPG saved as .png (a case the comment at 1144-1146 says is supported) and on every failed PNG, doubling the cost of finding 1's retries.
findings.fix: In texLoadArtFile read the non-tar file into RAM once (the open + texStageExternalFileIntoMemory that texLoadJpgFile already does) and decode it with texLoadArtFromMemory, which already tries PNG and then JPG from one buffer. Delete texLoadJpgFile and the extension branch. This moves HDD/SMB PNG art from the 4 KB streaming reader to one staged read, as .jpg art already does.
findings.benefit: One open and one read per art file instead of two for JPG-named-.png and broken files; about 15 lines removed (texLoadJpgFile 22 lines and the extension branch, replaced by about 8). INFERRED.
findings.evidence: Read texLoadArtFile 1309-1335: for dot NULL or .png it calls texLoad (1329), and every result except >=0/ERR_BAD_FILE/ERR_FILE_IO/ERR_LOAD_ABORTED falls to texLoadJpgFile (1334). texLoad 1118-1129 -> texLoadAll staged arm 927-983 (open, texStageExternalFileIntoMemory, close) or streaming arm 984-1005; libpng signature failure longjmps to 1023-1031 (ERR_SET_JMP). texLoadJpgFile 1269-1288 opens again (1278) and stages again (1281). texLoadArtFromMemory 1299-1305 already does PNG-then-JPG on one buffer. grep texLoadJpgFile over the repo: only the definition (1269) and the call at 1334; .github/scripts/test_ripps2_art_port.py names texLoadJpgMemory only.

findings.title: favPrepareSave re-reads and re-parses the primary file that favReadFile just validated on every favourite/recent save
findings.problem: All three writers (addItem, removeByIdAndText, recentRecord) call favReadFile with editable and refuse to write unless it authorises the write; favWriteFile then runs favPrepareSave, which loads and parses the same primary (and staged) file again and recomputes the same decision (primary complete wins; else staged complete and primary missing or recoverable; else both missing). The only extra work it does is copying a complete .new back over a torn primary. recentRecord runs on every game launch, so each launch pays an extra open/read/parse of the primary before the two write+readback cycles.
findings.fix: Let favReadFile report which copy was authoritative (primary, staged, or none) and pass that to favWriteFile; restore the primary from the staged image only in the staged case and drop favImageValid and the primary re-read in favPrepareSave.
findings.benefit: ~15 lines removed and one fewer whole-file read (open, 2 lseek, read, tail read, close, about 6 IOP RPCs) of the memory-card file per favourite toggle and per launch (INFERRED from favLoadImage 344-373)
findings.evidence: Read favReadFile 395-423 and favPrepareSave 528-545: identical three-way decision on complete/missing/recoverable. Callers of favWriteFile: addItem 1050 (after favReadFile 1012), removeByIdAndText 1074 (after 1059), recentRecord 1516 (after 1492); grep favWriteFile shows no other caller. INFERRED: no other thread changes the config path or file between the two reads inside one call (the comment at 526-527 argues for re-reading across config-path changes and PC edits, which cannot happen inside a single save). Storage path: needs hardware testing.

Grep rmDrawOverlayPixmap( over src: the three calls here plus coverflow.cpp:341, grid.cpp:324, psbbnflow.cpp:169 (those use their own geometry and colour, not included). themeelems.cpp:860-863 shows Background elements never load an overlay, so bgPicture==defaultTexture in the overlay branch of drawStaticImage.

findings.title: Element init chain carries parameters that are unused or always passed the same constant
findings.problem: initMutableText ignores themePath and theme, and both callers pass alias=NULL, DISPLAY_ALWAYS, SIZING_NONE. findDuplicate's overlayTexture is discarded with (void) and the function is exported in themeint.h though only this file calls it. initMutableImage's defaultTexture/overlayTexture, initGameImage's texture/overlay, initStaticImage's imageName, initBackground's texture and initItemsList's decorator are NULL at every call site; each is only a seed for a configGetStr.

findings.title: The mc0:/mc1: path prefix test is written out in six places (suIsMc, fmIsMcPath, fmIsMc, menuwatch writeReport, settingsio twice)
findings.problem: The same expression (strncmp(p, "mc", 2) == 0 && (p[2] == '0' || p[2] == '1') && p[3] == ':') appears as three identical static one-line functions (selfupdate.cpp:117, guifilemgr.cpp:69, filemgr.cpp:82), inline in menuwatch.cpp:284, and twice more in settingsio.cpp (bootHomeIsConcreteMc on gBootDir, and inside sameConcreteMcSlot). No shared helper exists in include/.
findings.fix: Keep one static inline isMcPath() in a header the files already include (include/opl.h) and delete suIsMc, fmIsMcPath, fmIsMc and bootHomeIsConcreteMc, calling the shared one instead; use it in menuwatch.cpp:284 and for the first operand in sameConcreteMcSlot.
findings.justification: The helper replaces six copies of the same test already in the tree, so it removes code overall (four function bodies and two inline expressions become one four-line inline).
findings.benefit: ~10 source lines net (INFERRED: 4 static helpers of 4-5 lines plus 2 inline expressions replaced by one 4-line inline); no ELF change, the compiler already inlines these static one-liners.
findings.evidence: Grep over src/RiptOPL for "[2] == '0' || x[2] == '1'": selfupdate.cpp:119, menuwatch.cpp:284, guifilemgr.cpp:71, filemgr.cpp:84, settingsio.cpp:694 and :703, nothing else. findings.title: Modal screens render the whole menu (guiShow) and then paint an opaque black rect over it every frame
findings.problem: RebootIopPrompt::draw, guiWarning, RemoveSettingsPrompt::draw, CheatScreen::draw (and guiRenderTextScreen) call guiShow() and then cover the full screen with gColBlack (alpha 0x80, solid: renderman.cpp:122), so the menu render is invisible wasted frame time. guiConfirmVideoMode already dropped this exact call for that reason (guisettings.cpp:3457-3462), and the comments at guimodal.cpp:308 and 398 still cite guiConfirmVideoMode as having guiShow as backdrop, which is no longer true.
findings.fix: Delete the guiShow() call (and its stale 'same reason as guiConfirmVideoMode' comment) in the four guimodal.cpp draws and in guiRenderTextScreen.
findings.benefit: One full menu-screen render per frame saved on every opaque modal and status screen (INFERRED from the repo's own note at guisettings.cpp:3457-3461 that this render cost visible frame time); ~8 lines removed.
findings.evidence: Read guimodal.cpp:224-238,272-288,304-320,394-433 and guiwait.cpp:200-230: each calls guiShow() then rmDrawRect(0,0,W,H,gColBlack). gColBlack = RGBA(0,0,0,0x80) 'solid black' at renderman.cpp:122. guisettings.cpp:3457-3462 documents removing guiShow before the same opaque backdrop as 'pure frame time'. Only MessageBoxScreen (gColDarker when ui_ set) is translucent and it does not call guiShow.

findings.title: cacheAbortMmceImageLoadsTimed called right before cacheCancelPendingImageLoadsTimed at six sites is redundant and can lengthen the drain
findings.problem: Cancel is a strict superset of Abort: it flags the in-flight request whatever its bus, frees the whole queue, and waits for queued==0 && active==0. Abort first frees only SIO2 requests, RE-PUSHES the rest and wakes the worker, then waits for an SIO2 read; once it sleeps the worker can pop a re-pushed non-SIO2 request and start a new device read that the following Cancel must then wait out. The pair costs up to 2x the timeout instead of 1x.
findings.fix: At the six paired sites delete the cacheAbortMmceImageLoadsTimed call and keep only cacheCancelPendingImageLoadsTimed (fold guiwait's abortOk into cancelOk). Keep Abort where it is used alone (mmcesupport, bdmlaunch, bdmsupport, menusys, themes.cpp:1415).
findings.benefit: ~8 call-site lines removed; worst-case drain halved (500-2000 ms less when an SIO2 read is in flight); one detach/re-push pass and a possible extra device read avoided (INFERRED from the code paths)
findings.evidence: Read artload.cpp:428-508 (both functions). Grep cacheAbortMmceImageLoadsTimed|cacheCancelPendingImageLoads over src: paired calls at lwnbdctl.cpp:141-142, guiwait.cpp:67-68, themes.cpp:1820-1821, appsupport.cpp:789-790, hddsupport.cpp:2178-2179 and 2267-2268 (all read); Abort alone at mmcesupport.cpp:1204,1257,1326,1851, bdmlaunch.cpp:104,198, bdmsupport.cpp:2404, menusys.cpp:920, themes.cpp:1415. Worker priority 72 (artload.cpp:31) is below the GUI (31), so it runs when the caller sleeps in Abort's DelayThread loop (artload.cpp:499-505).

findings.title: bgmStart/bgmStop block the GUI thread: up to 500 ms prebuffer wait in start(), 200 ms minimum alarm slice in stop()
findings.problem: start() runs on the GUI thread and spins DelayThread(5 ms) up to 100 times until 48 chunks are decoded, so no frame is drawn for up to 500 ms at main-loop entry, on Audio settings accept and after a theme change. stop() waits in SetAlarm/SleepThread slices of 3200 HSYNC (~200 ms); the I/O thread has priority 31 like the GUI thread (opl.cpp:2064, bgm.cpp:696), so it cannot exit before the first sleep and every stop costs at least ~200 ms. A theme change does stop then start: roughly 0.2-0.7 s of frozen screen.
findings.fix: Move the prebuffer wait to the top of threadMain (the playback thread waits for the cushion before its first queueChunk; discretionaryIoAllowed already holds art I/O until the ring is primed) and drop the else-branch at 810-816, since the playback thread already exits on the I/O thread's terminate signal. In stop(), poll with DelayThread(10 ms) over the same 3.2 s budget and delete bgmShutdownDelayCallback.
findings.benefit: Removes up to ~500 ms (start) and ~190 ms (stop) of GUI-thread stall per call (INFERRED: 100 x 5 ms loop bound; 3200 HSYNC slice vs a 10 ms poll); about 6 lines removed (callback, else-branch).
findings.evidence: Read bgm.cpp:741-881. Callers via grep bgmStart|bgmStop: gui.cpp:333 (mainLoop entry, GUI thread), guisettings.cpp:1958 (guiSetAudioSettingsState), 2742/2767 (theme apply), selfupdate.cpp:424, sound.cpp:51 (audioEnd at launch), lwnbdctl.cpp:250. Thread priorities: GUI 31 at opl.cpp:2064, BGM io thread BGM_THREAD_BASE_PRIO+1 = 31 at bgm.cpp:40,696, playback 30. Durations are derived from the loop constants, not measured on hardware.

findings.title: RA notice timer uses an absolute clock() deadline, the wrap-unsafe form the class header warns against
findings.problem: renderRA arms raNoticeTimer_ = clock() + 8 s and expires on clock() >= raNoticeTimer_, while guinotify.h:33-35 (and guiwait.cpp:97-98) state that this form breaks across the 32-bit clock wrap; popup and toast in the same class use the elapsed (clock() - start) form. A notice armed within 8 s of the wrap gets a wrapped deadline and is dropped after one frame. renderRA's only caller is drawRA, always with y=10, yadd=35 (gui.cpp:360).
findings.fix: Store the start tick and expire on (clock() - start) >= 8 s like popupStart_/toastStart_ (a separate armed flag replaces the 0 sentinel), and fold renderRA into drawRA.
findings.benefit: Removes a rare dropped-notice bug in RETROACHIEVEMENTS builds and one wrapper function; ~5 lines removed.
findings.evidence: Read guinotify.cpp:84-94 (toast, uint32 elapsed), 148 (popup, elapsed), 178-190 (RA, absolute). Grep drawRA/renderRA: gui.cpp:360 calls drawRA; renderRA only called at guinotify.cpp:197. The clock() width and wrap period are taken from the repo's own comment at guinotify.h:33-35, not verified against ps2sdk (INFERRED).

findings.title: vmcSavesDelete frees at most 64 file chains, leaking card space for bigger saves; its files[] buffer is not needed
findings.problem: vmcSavesDelete collects file chains into u32_t files[SAVE_FILES] and stops at 64 (1181-1182, 1193); files past the 64th, and sub-folders inside the save (only MC_FILE is taken, 1194), are never freed, so once the root entry is hidden (1197-1198) their clusters stay marked used with nothing naming them. The buffer exists to free chains after the entry is hidden, but vsFreeChain and vsSetFat (300-304, 406-415) only change the in-memory FAT until vsFlushFat (1205), so freeing inside the scan keeps the same on-disk order.
findings.fix: Call vsFreeChain(&v, e.cluster) inside the scan loop for every existing file with length > 0 (keep the length test: an empty file's cluster field is 0, vsWriteVmc line 585), and delete files[], nfiles, the 64 cap and the second loop. Sub-folders inside a save stay unsupported, as they already are for export.
findings.benefit: Deleting a save with more than 64 files no longer loses VMC space until a reformat; ~5 lines and a 256 B stack array removed (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read vmcsaves.cpp 1176-1208, 275-304 and 406-415: vsFreeChain edits only v->fat and fatDirty; the only disk write before vsFlushFat is the hidden root entry at 1198, and an error return before the flush discards in-memory changes in vsClose. vsLoadVmc refuses saves over 64 files (464-467), so such saves can be deleted but not exported. Caller: guigame.cpp:467 after a confirm box. How often real saves exceed 64 files is not verified (INFERRED rare), hence Med confidence.

findings.title: Native MMCE launch switches the card (Game ID) and writes the OSD history before the cheats prompt that can cancel the launch
findings.problem: The OPL-core leg sends the 0x8 Game ID switch (1410), waits the swap out and writes the OSD history record (1426) before sbLoadCheats. When per-game cheats are on and the .cht is missing or broken, sbCheatsMissingContinue asks, and a cancel returns to the menu (1543-1548). The card is then left on the game's per-game folder, or switching to it through its own history tracker, with a history entry for a game that never started. Nothing resets the card on that path (mmceReset serves non-game launches only), so later menu writes to that slot's mcN: go to the game's card (INFERRED).
findings.fix: Move the cheats load and its prompt (1540-1550, with the RA watch-list call above it if wanted) to just after `settings` is set at 1379, before the native Game ID block. The Neutrino leg already loads cheats before its own send. The two VMC fd closes in that bail then go away, because no fd exists yet.
findings.benefit: A cancelled launch leaves the card folder and OSD history untouched and skips a pointless swap wait of up to 180 s; 4 lines removed (INFERRED)
findings.evidence: Read MmceSource::launch 1292-1746: sbPrepare 1376, settings 1379, Game ID send + waitSwapDone/settleAfterSwitch 1410-1414, sysAddHistoryRecord + waitHistorySwitch 1426-1434, VMC fds opened 1462, cheats 1540-1550. Neutrino leg loads cheats at 1540 before its send at 1656, after every preflight bail (1629-1644). sbCheatsMissingContinue (supportbase.cpp:1667-1697) returns 0 on the cancel button and unprepares. mmceReset is described as the non-game-launch reset (mmcesupport.h:40-42); grep of mmceSendGameID callers shows every other source (e.g. httpsupport.cpp:842) sends right before deinit, after its bails. Inferred part: what the menu then writes to the switched mcN: surface. Two more post-send bails (Auto slot lost 1564-1581, ISO open failure 1685-1700) are hardware failures and stay.

findings.title: Tray-open check compares sceCdStatus() with an error code (SCECdErOPENS), so it never fires
findings.problem: sceCdStatus() returns the drive status register (bit 0 = tray open, value SCECdStatShellOpen; see the repo's own emulation in modules/iopcore/cdvdman/scmd.c:60-68,115-119), but both functions compare it with SCECdErOPENS, a member of the SCECdEr* error-code family returned by sceCdGetError. An open tray therefore never takes the documented 'return -1' exit. In sysGetDiscBootPath the open tray reads as NODISC and the code goes on to send a tray-close request (sysdisc.cpp:168-175) and re-detect for up to 2-4 s; in sysGetDiscID the NODISC test at system.cpp:506 returns -1 anyway.
findings.fix: Delete the two dead checks. They never fire today, and an open tray already ends in the NODISC handling in both functions. If an open tray should fail fast in sysGetDiscBootPath, test sceCdStatus() & SCECdStatShellOpen there instead.
findings.benefit: 4 lines removed (INFERRED); the code then does what it actually does, with no misleading guard. No ELF size change worth stating.
findings.evidence: grep -rn SCECdErOPENS over src/RiptOPL: only sysdisc.cpp:158 and system.cpp:498. grep sceCdStatus: modules/iopcore/cdvdman/scmd.c:115-119 returns cdvdman_stat.status, which scmd.c:68 sets to SCECdStatShellOpen on tray open (bit 0 test at :64,:79). SCECdEr* values elsewhere are error codes (e.g. test_udpfs_files_oplcore.py:235-237 SCECdErREAD 0x30, SCECdErTRMOPN 0x31). INFERRED: SCECdErOPENS is 0x11 in the ps2sdk header (not in this repo), which is not a reachable status value (tray-open bit plus seek bit). Callers do not distinguish -1 from -2: menusys.cpp:2365-2367 and discsupport.cpp:111-113,164-168 show one generic error.

findings.title: CNFGetKey leaves BOOT2 unterminated at 64 characters; GetStartupExecName's 64-byte buffer is then scanned past its end
findings.problem: CNFGetKey copies up to CNF_PATH_LEN_MAX (64) characters and writes '\0' only when it meets whitespace. A BOOT2 value of 64+ printable characters fills all of GetStartupExecName's char ps2disc_boot[CNF_PATH_LEN_MAX] (supportbase.cpp:116) with no terminator, and the ':' and ';' scans at supportbase.cpp:127-144 then read past it on the IO worker stack. The input is SYSTEM.CNF inside any user ISO read as iso:/SYSTEM.CNF;1 during the ISO scan (supportbase.cpp:450). The '\0' branch at ps2cnf.cpp:62-64 is unreachable under the loop condition.
findings.fix: Bound the copy loop to CNF_PATH_LEN_MAX - 1 characters and write the terminator once after the loop; delete the unreachable '\0' branch at lines 62-64.
findings.justification: Adds one terminator write after the loop: the only caller's buffer is exactly CNF_PATH_LEN_MAX bytes and the parser can fill it from ISO content, so this closes a stack over-read; deleting the dead branch makes the change net smaller.
findings.benefit: Closes a stack over-read on untrusted ISO content; ~2 lines net removed (3-line dead branch out, 1 line in) (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read ps2cnf.cpp:42-68 (loop i < CNF_PATH_LEN_MAX writes key[0..63], terminator only in the isspace branch) and :115 (caller only checks for -1). grep -rn ps2cnfGetBootFile over the repo: only production caller supportbase.cpp:120 with char ps2disc_boot[CNF_PATH_LEN_MAX] = "" at :116; GetStartupExecName called at supportbase.cpp:450 with iso:/SYSTEM.CNF;1. The host test tests/host/test_ps2cnf.cpp:25 uses a 65-byte buffer, so it cannot see this; .github/scripts/test_cnf_missing_equals.py:18 uses 64 but only tests a missing '='.

findings.title: Two Neutrino TOML preflights keep separate static 4 KB in/out buffer pairs (16.9 KB .bss) though they never run together
findings.problem: sysSyncNeutrinoUdpfsToml has static toml[4096] and updated[4116]; sysNeutrinoSmbPreflight has static toml[4096] and updated[4608]. That is 16,916 bytes of .bss held for the whole run. The two are only called one after the other (the udpfs sync from sysNeutrinoPreflight:836-837 for udpfs/udpfsbd/udpbd only; the SMB/NFS preflight only from ethsupport.cpp:1216), neither calls the other, and neither keeps data between calls, so one pair is enough.
findings.fix: Replace the four function-local statics with one file-scope pair (4096 in, 4096 + 512 out) used by both functions.
findings.benefit: 8,212 bytes .bss saved (MEASURED: nm gives 0x1000+0x1014 and 0x1000+0x1200 = 16,916 B; one 4096+4608 pair keeps 8,704). No code growth.
findings.evidence: evidence/RiptOPL/raw/riptopl-nm-size-sorted.full.txt lines 187 (SmbPreflight updated 0x1200), 206 (UdpfsToml updated 0x1014), 212 (UdpfsToml toml 0x1000), 214 (SmbPreflight toml 0x1000); riptopl-per-object.tsv:46 sysneutrino.o bss 17036. Callers via grep over src: sysSyncNeutrinoUdpfsToml only at sysneutrino.cpp:837; sysNeutrinoSmbPreflight only at ethsupport.cpp:1216, followed by sysNeutrinoPreflight(driver smb/nfs) at :1221, which skips the udpfs sync (sysneutrino.cpp:836). Both functions read the file fresh each call and keep no state in the buffers. The udpfs output needs at most 4094 + 15 bytes (sysneutrino.cpp:443), which fits in 4608.

findings.title: tarParseFile cold scan: an extra lseek RPC per member and +64-entry linear index growth
