findings.problem: For every member the scan does read(512), lseek64(fd, 0, SEEK_CUR) only to learn the offset it already knows (header end), and lseek64(paddedSize, SEEK_CUR). Each is a fileXio RPC on the art worker, and the scan contends with BGM I/O on the same channel. The index also grows by 64 entries per realloc. For N members that copies O(N^2) bytes when realloc moves the block (6000 members: about 18 MB copied) and leaves heap fragments.
findings.fix: Keep the file position in a local u64 (add 512 after each header, paddedSize after each member). Store it as dataOffset, and skip with one lseek64(pos, SEEK_SET). Delete the SEEK_CUR query. Double the capacity instead of adding 64.
findings.benefit: One fewer IOP RPC per member on each cold scan (N members = N RPCs) and realloc copying drops from ~18 MB to under 1 MB for 6000 members (INFERRED arithmetic: 4096 x 94 x 95 / 2 bytes vs < 2 x 384 KB)
findings.evidence: Read tar.cpp:256-365: per member read at :258, lseek64 SEEK_CUR at :293 (only used as dataOffset), lseek64 SEEK_CUR skip at :363 (and :288/:299 for skipped members); realloc with newCap = cap + 64 at :305-306. Runs on the art worker via tarFindPrefix -> tarLoadFromAnyDevice -> tarParseFile (artload.cpp:89) and, for THM, on every theme-load lookup (no sidecar, tar.cpp:63). The RPC cost per call is INFERRED; there was no hardware measurement.

findings.title: Ranet receive buffer rx_ is 2048 bytes but no read ever exceeds 992 + NUL; netTestLink keeps a second static rx[256]
findings.problem: ask() clamps every read to RA_RECV_MAX = 992 bytes (ranet.cpp:313-317, also for the mstack: path) and httpGet reads into rx_ at most 992 (ranet.cpp:1112), so at most 993 bytes of rx_ are ever written. netTestLink uses its own static rx[256] although it runs on the same thread and never overlaps a use of rx_.
findings.fix: Shrink rx_ to 1024 bytes (still 64-byte aligned) and let netTestLink use rx_ instead of its static rx[256].
findings.benefit: INFERRED: 2048 -> 1024 bytes for rx_ plus 256 bytes for netTestLink's buffer = 1,280 bytes of .bss, RA builds only.
findings.evidence: grep rx_ over the repo: every use is in ranet.cpp (576, 667, 835, 943, 947, 970, 982, 1012 via ask(); 1112 via tcpRecv capped at RA_RECV_MAX) plus the declaration at ranet.h:89. ask() sets asklen = min(outmax-1, RA_RECV_MAX) and askMstack receives that asklen. No test script mentions rx_. netTestLink's rx is only passed to pcTarget/ask (ranet.cpp:887, 907) and read at :931.

findings.title: Two separate static int sel[FM_MAX] buffers in guifilemgr.cpp
findings.problem: fmToClipboard and fmDeleteSelection each own a static 512-entry int selection buffer; the two never run at the same time (both are called from fmActions, one per dialog result), so one buffer is enough.
findings.fix: Use one file-scope selection buffer for both functions (or allocate it with the other File Manager buffers in guiShowFileManager).
findings.benefit: 2 KB .bss saved (INFERRED: 512 x 4 bytes); about 1 line
findings.evidence: Read guifilemgr.cpp:360-386 and 487-514; FM_MAX is 512 (line 50); callers are fmActions 598-607 only, sequential, no recursion.

findings.title: ThemeCatalog::reinit can leave themeId_ pointing at a removed or different theme (failed default load; 64-byte name copy)
findings.problem: When the active theme lives on the device being removed (SMB reconnect, UDPFS re-init) and thmLoad(NULL) returns -1 (MX4SIO art drain timeout at 1415, or OOM at 1361), themeId_ keeps the old index although the swap-remove at 1985-1997 just deleted that entry: the id now names another theme or lies past count_, so thmGetValue reads names_[count_+1] (NULL) or past the array, and picking the theme that moved into that slot is skipped as 'already loaded' (2034). Separately, activeName[64] truncates a theme name of 64+ chars, findGuiID misses, and themeId_ becomes 0 while the disk theme stays on screen.
findings.fix: Keep a pointer to the active entry's name instead of the 64-byte copy (only removed entries are freed; moved entries keep their name pointers), and when the active entry was removed set themeId_ to 0 whether or not thmLoad(NULL) succeeded, since the old index no longer exists.
findings.benefit: Fixes a wrong theme id (possible out-of-bounds read of names_) after a failed fallback load, and the id loss for long theme names; removes a 64-byte stack copy and its snprintf
findings.evidence: thmReinit callers: ethsupport.cpp:611 (reconnectSmb, IO worker) and udpfssupport.cpp:324 (UdpfsSource::init). thmLoad returns -1 at themes.cpp:1364 (malloc) and 1418 (cacheAbortMmceImageLoadsTimed(500) fails with curT set). names_ holds count_+2 entries with names_[count_+1]=NULL (themes.cpp:1888-1897); currentName returns names_[themeId_] unchecked (2022). thmGetValue readers: settingsio.cpp:2233 (guarded by thmSavedThemePending), guisettings.cpp:2749. setGuiValueLocked skips the load when themeId_ == themeID and reload == 0 (themes.cpp:2034). Theme names come from directory entries (readEntry, themes.cpp:1045-1047), not length-limited. Trigger needs an MX4SIO art read wedged during the reconnect, so it is rare.

findings.title: init() starts the pads twice at every boot: startPads() result at line 1686 is discarded and the wait loop calls it again
findings.problem: padStatus is initialised to 0 (1668) and the startPads() at 1686 ignores its return, so the while (!padStatus) loop always runs startPads() a second time even when the first call opened every port. PadManager::start() resets padCount_ and, for every port/slot, calls padPortOpen again without a close and re-runs initialize(): mode-table RPCs, padSetMainMode, press mode, actuator align, and up to six waitReady() polls of 25 x 1 ms each. All of that is repeated on the boot path before the config even loads.
findings.fix: Keep the result of the first call: make line 1686 assign padStatus = startPads() (and drop the separate = 0 initialisation at 1668), so the loop only retries when no port opened.
findings.benefit: One full pad bring-up (padPortOpen + initialize) per port saved on every boot; initialize can wait up to 6 x 25 ms per DualShock and ~25 ms per empty port, so roughly 50-300 ms of boot time (INFERRED from PAD_WAIT_POLLS=25, PAD_WAIT_POLL_US=1000, not measured)
findings.evidence: Read opl.cpp:1661-1709 (padStatus=0 at 1668, bare startPads() at 1686, loop 1701-1708 calls startPads() until non-zero). Read pad.cpp start() 1155-1200 (padCount_=0, startOne per port/slot), startOne 1136-1151 (padPortOpen then initialize then waitReady), initialize 188-297 (waitReady at 207/266/270/274/286/294), waitReady 171-186 with PAD_WAIT_POLLS=25 and PAD_WAIT_POLL_US=1000 (pad.cpp:111-112). grep padPortClose: only unloadOne (pad.cpp:1107), so the first session's ports are never closed before the reopen. The time saved is inferred from the poll constants; whether padman's second open is otherwise harmless was not verified on hardware (boot works today, so it does not fail).

findings.title: 12 gfx/ PNGs that no build embeds: Device_1..6, Device_all, no_Device, no_Rating, logo4..6
findings.problem: textures.cpp maps these textures to NULL or to a shared blob (Rating_0, logo3/2/1), and tools/assets.py PNG_ASSETS (46-57, plus the Korium additions at 163) does not list them, so the source PNGs are never bin2c'd. logo4/5/6 and no_Rating are byte-identical to logo3/2/1 and Rating_0 (cmp). No other file references the file names.
findings.fix: Delete the 12 PNG files from gfx/. Keep the table rows: their names are still theme lookup keys (misc/*.cfg use default=no_Rating).
findings.benefit: 29,792 bytes of tracked repo files removed (MEASURED: inventory/RiptOPL.tsv sizes); no ELF change
findings.evidence: Read tools/assets.py:46-60 and 159-180 (only PNG_ASSETS, Korium extras and ra_mark are embedded, sourced from gfx/<name>.png). Grep for Device_[1-6all].png, no_Device, logo4 over the whole repo: only textures.cpp. git grep no_Rating: only theme cfg default= keys and textures.cpp:243. cmp gfx/logo4.png logo3.png, logo5/logo2, logo6/logo1, no_Rating/Rating_0: identical. Sizes from inventory: 582+742+886+899+600+784+1016+676+1332+8569+7161+6545 = 29,792.

findings.title: AppSource::launch resets MMCE cards before checks that can still cancel the launch
findings.problem: mmceReset() runs at 1181, right after the Reboot-IOP answer. The path normalisation (1184-1187), the HDD partition and handoff-path checks (1265-1273) and the 256-byte argument-pool check (1286-1289) can then still return to the menu. resetCards loads the MMCE modules if they are not loaded and sends the 0x9 reset to every present MMCE card (mmcesupport.cpp:554-585). An over-long path or argv1 therefore leaves OPL in the menu with the card switched and mmceman resident. appLaunchElfPath does the same reset only after all its checks (1068-1072).
findings.fix: Move the mmceReset() call to just before host::app().deinit at line 1295, after the argBytes check. Keep a call in the OPLDIAG Ember block if that probe needs it.
findings.benefit: An aborted APPS launch no longer resets SD2PSX/MemCard PRO cards or loads mmceman; no line change (moved call).
findings.evidence: Read appsupport.cpp:1037-1075 and 1077-1312, mmcesupport.cpp:547-595. Grep mmceReset over the repo: mmcesupport.h:42, mmcesupport.cpp:592, appsupport.cpp:1072 and 1181, plus a stub in .github/scripts/test_app_launch_args.py:130 (does not pin the order).

findings.title: Every save with a Custom Settings Path rewrites config.path, including each game launch's CONFIG_LAST save
findings.problem: _saveConfig calls writeConfigPathRedirect after every successful explicit-path save, whatever lscstatus holds. Launch paths call saveConfig(CONFIG_LAST, 0) when Remember Last Played is on, and per-game resets call saveConfig(CONFIG_GAME, 0). Each of these truncates and rewrites config.path in the boot folder (often a memory card) and, on a network boot, the mc?:/OPL mirror too, although the path has not changed. configWriteChecked returns a positive value even when no set was dirty, so the rewrite happens even when nothing else was written.
findings.fix: Rewrite the redirect only when the save includes CONFIG_OPL, the set that holds custom_settings_path: add (lscstatus & CONFIG_OPL) to the condition at line 2420.
findings.justification: The condition removes one or two file rewrites (open with O_TRUNC, two writes, close) per game launch for Custom Settings Path users. The path can only change in a CONFIG_OPL save, so no state is lost.
findings.benefit: Saves 1 file rewrite per launch (2 on network boots: boot-folder copy plus mc mirror) for Custom Settings Path users, usually on a memory card (INFERRED)
findings.evidence: Read settingsio.cpp:331-385 (O_TRUNC open plus two write calls; mc mirror when gBootHomeDeferred), 2402-2429 (redirect written when customSettingsExplicit && lscret > 0, no lscstatus test), 2100-2121 (configWriteMulti counts unmodified sets as 1). grep saveConfig( callers: bdmlaunch.cpp:455,900, ethsupport.cpp:1226,1377, hddsupport.cpp:2391,2722, httpsupport.cpp:801, mmcesupport.cpp:1386, udpfssupport.cpp:1072 (CONFIG_LAST); guigame.cpp:2117, menusys.cpp:3258 (CONFIG_GAME); menusys.cpp:1021,2259 include CONFIG_OPL. settings.cpp:104 Remember Last Played setting.

findings.title: IGS halts the console forever when mc1 is missing or full, or after the 255th screenshot, instead of finishing the exit
findings.problem: The output path is hard-coded to mc1:. A failed fioOpen (no card in slot 2), any short fioWrite (card full: a 640x448x32 BMP is ~1.1 MB), and a 255th existing file all call DBGCOL_BLNK(..., true), which is BlinkColour with forever set (util.c:184-198), so the IGR thread never reaches IGR_Exit (padhook.c:659). The game is already shut down and the IOP reset, so the user is left on a blinking screen and must power-cycle; a truncated BMP stays on the card.
findings.fix: On an open or write failure (and at the 255 limit) close any open handle and return, passing false to the blink, so InGameScreenshot falls through to IGR_Exit like a normal exit.
findings.benefit: Removes a hang that needs a power cycle on realistic card conditions (empty slot 2, full card); no size change (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read igs_api.c 375-678 and InGameScreenshot 680-790; ee_core.h:91 maps DBGCOL_BLNK to BlinkColour(blinkCount, colour, forever); util.c:184-198 loops do{...}while(forever). Call path: IGR_CheckInputs sets IGR_COMBO_UP when EnableGSMOp (padhook.c:354-357) -> IGR_Thread shutdown branch (547-551) -> oplIGRShutdown(0), Reset_Iop, InGameScreenshot (646-648) -> IGR_Exit (659). Only compiled in the extras configurations (tools/build_configuration.py:37-40).

findings.title: Pad fault-discriminator runs (notReadyRun_/emptyRun_) are one counter updated once per pad, so an empty second port doubles them and logs false misses
findings.problem: readOne() advances the shared run counters per pad, not per poll. start() keeps an empty port in padData_ (initialize() returns 1 on every path), and a DISCONN port reads nothing, so each poll adds 1 to notReadyRun_. With one pad and one empty port, a k-poll miss on the real pad becomes a run of 2k: the debug HUD, DIAG.TXT and menuwatch (guioverlay.cpp:159, diagsave.cpp:33, menuwatch.cpp:192) report doubled maxima, maxNotReadyRun_ is never below 1, and a 2-poll miss writes 'pad: 4 polls in a row could not be read' into the 16 KB diag ring. With two pads, emptyRun_ interleaves the same way.
findings.fix: Decide the runs once per poll in read(): have readOne() report whether it attempted a native or ds34 read and whether any delivered, then after the loop count a not-ready poll when some pad attempted and none delivered, and an empty poll when one delivered and paddata_ is 0. Delete the per-pad block at 484-501.
findings.benefit: Correct fault counters and no false miss lines in DIAG.TXT on the diagnostic path the code was written to chase hardware faults with; net lines about 0 (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read pad.cpp:373-529 (padsRead is local per call, counters are members updated per call), 888-905 (read() loops readOne over padCount_), 1136-1200 (start() increments padCount_ whenever startOne succeeds; startOne fails only if padPortOpen fails), 188-297 (initialize returns 1 on all paths), opl.cpp:1696-1697 comment ('a port with nothing plugged in still counts'). Readers: grep padGetFaultCounters -> diagsave.cpp:33, guioverlay.cpp:159, menuwatch.cpp:192. diagLog is a RAM ring (diaglog.cpp:14-44).

findings.title: Static tables larger than needed: crctab[0x400] uses 256 entries; s_zeroBlock is a 512-byte table for one memcmp
findings.problem: USBA_crc32 declares crctab[0x400] (4096 bytes .bss) but only fills and indexes crctab[0..255] (index is byte ^ (crc>>24 & 0xFF)). It also rebuilds the table on every call. tar.cpp keeps a 512-byte all-zero .rodata block whose only use is memcmp in isZeroBlock.
findings.fix: Declare crctab[256]. Replace s_zeroBlock with a loop in isZeroBlock that checks the 64-byte-aligned header word by word, and delete the table.
findings.benefit: 3072 bytes .bss and 512 bytes ELF .rodata (MEASURED: nm riptopl-nm-size-sorted.full.txt shows _ZL6crctab 0x1000 and _ZL11s_zeroBlock 0x200)
findings.evidence: Read system.cpp:465-492: writes crctab[255 - table] for table 0..255 and reads crctab[byte ^ ((crc >> 24) & 0xFF)] with unsigned char byte, so the max index is 255. Read tar.cpp:73 and 87-90: s_zeroBlock is referenced only in isZeroBlock (grep s_zeroBlock: tar.cpp:73,89 only). Sizes from evidence/RiptOPL/raw/riptopl-nm-size-sorted.full.txt: 0060bb60 00001000 b _ZL6crctab; 005e0440 00000200 r _ZL11s_zeroBlock. Callers of USBA_crc32 (supportbase.cpp:1226,1473; ethsupport.cpp:1434) are not hot, so the per-call rebuild costs time but not memory.

findings.title: USBA_crc32 table crctab[0x400] is four times the 256 entries it uses
findings.problem: The table loop fills indices 0..255 and the lookup index is byte ^ (crc>>24 & 0xFF), at most 255, so entries 256..1023 of the static unsigned int crctab[0x400] are never touched.
findings.fix: Declare crctab[256] (upstream-derived code; behaviour unchanged).
findings.benefit: 768 x 4 = 3072 bytes of .bss saved (INFERRED from the declaration)
findings.evidence: Read system.cpp:465-492: writes crctab[255 - table] for table 0..255; reads crctab[byte ^ ((crc >> 24) & 0xFF)] with unsigned char byte. Grep crctab: no other use in the repo's src. Callers of USBA_crc32: supportbase.cpp:656,1226,1473 and ethsupport.cpp:1434.

findings.title: cheatConfigSaveSelections marks the game CFG modified even when the picks did not change, so every Select-mode launch rewrites it
findings.problem: The save first removes every $CheatSel000-249 key and then re-appends the enabled picks. removeKey sets modified_ when a key exists and append sets it again, so with any remembered pick the set is always dirty and CheatScreen::finish's configWrite rewrites the game's CFG on its device at each Select-mode launch, even when the user pressed START without changing anything. configWrite would otherwise skip a clean set (config.cpp:1511-1519).
findings.fix: Write the picks first with configSetStr (a no-op when the value is equal, config.cpp:371-377), then remove only the keys from index n upward; an unchanged pick list leaves the set clean and configWrite does nothing.
findings.benefit: One CFG file write saved per Select-mode launch with unchanged picks (game device, may be MMCE/USB/HDD); removeKey calls drop from 250 to 250-n. No size change (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read cheatconfig.cpp:62-111, guimodal.cpp:435-444 (finish: save + configWrite), config.cpp:363-386 (setStr marks modified only on change or append), :447-458 (removeKey marks modified only when the key is found), :1498-1519 (configWrite skips unmodified sets). Caller chain: sbLoadCheats -> sbCheatsSelect -> manageCheats (supportbase.cpp:1732-1739). Whether other launch code dirties the same set first was not traced.

findings.title: set_ipconfig indexes SmapLinkModeArgs with an unchecked eth_linkmode from conf_network.cfg
findings.problem: The link mode is read from conf_network.cfg with configGetInt and never range-checked (settingsio.cpp:1924), copied into the unsigned char g_ps2_ETHOpMode (system.cpp:1561), and set_ipconfig indexes the four-entry SmapLinkModeArgs with ETHOpMode - 1 for any non-zero value (util.c:96-100). A value of 5..255 (hand-edited or damaged file; -1 becomes 255) reads a pointer past the array and strncpy's 6 bytes from it: a garbage SMAP argument or an address/TLB exception at ee_core start. The menu's own switch treats such values as auto (netsupport.cpp:408-423).
findings.fix: In set_ipconfig, add the -no_auto arguments only when ETHOpMode is below ETH_OP_MODE_COUNT, as the menu does.
findings.justification: Adds one comparison: a config-file value currently reaches an array index unchecked; defaulting to auto matches what the menu already does with the same value.
findings.benefit: Closes an out-of-bounds read at game launch from a malformed network config; no net line change (INFERRED)
findings.evidence: Read util.c:71-102. grep -rn 'gETHOpMode|g_ps2_ETHOpMode' over src/: opl.cpp:1513 (default), settingsio.cpp:1924 (configGetInt, no clamp), :2285 (save), guisettings.cpp:792,884,985 (dialog), netsupport.cpp:408 (switch with default -> auto), system.cpp:1561 (copy into the core config). Enum ee_core/include/ee_core.h:44-52 has 5 values. coreconfig.h:46: unsigned char field.

findings.title: settingshell.h: mmceDialog_ reserves 256 UIItems (10 KB .bss) for a page of at most ~45 rows
findings.problem: SettingsShell holds two UIItem[SETTINGS_DIALOG_CAPACITY=256] arrays. mmceDialog_ is used only by guiShowMmceConfig (guisettings.cpp:377), which composes diaMmceConfig + diaMmceCommConfig + diaMmcePathConfig (dialogs.cpp:816-942, 43 source rows before skips). sizeof(struct UIItem) is 40 bytes (dia.h:72-121), so mmceDialog_ is 10,240 bytes of .bss of which ~8 KB is never used.
findings.fix: Size mmceDialog_ to 64 entries and let composeInto bound by the destination size (pass the capacity instead of using SETTINGS_DIALOG_CAPACITY at guisettings.cpp:2117 and 2125).
findings.justification: The capacity parameter is the only addition: without it composeInto would check a 64-entry buffer against 256 and could overflow. It costs one argument and saves ~7.7 KB of EE .bss.
findings.benefit: ~7.7 KB .bss: (256 - 64) x 40 B = 7,680 B. MEASURED total: gSettingsShell is 0x50bc = 20,668 B in evidence/RiptOPL/raw/riptopl-nm-size-sorted.full.txt:45; the 40 B UIItem size is INFERRED from dia.h.
findings.evidence: grep mmceDialog over src: settingshell.h:49,73 and guisettings.cpp:377 only. Counted rows in dialogs.cpp:816-850 (23), 854-875 (11), 926-942 (9). Layout of struct UIItem from dia.h:72-121: 16 B header + 20 B union (intvalue: 4 ints + pointer) + 1 B flag, padded to 40. nm: gSettingsShell B 0x50bc.

findings.title: utf8.h defines its 400-byte DFA table static in a header, so the ELF carries two copies
findings.problem: utf8d[] is a 'static const' array and utf8Decode a static function in the header; fntsys.cpp and textshape.cpp both include and use it, so each object gets its own table. nm shows two _ZL5utf8d symbols of 0x190 bytes. (POPSLoader carries the same upstream Hoehrmann table; that is cross-repo and not shareable.)
findings.fix: Make the table a single definition: declare it 'inline constexpr' (C++17, the GCC 15 default) or move the table and utf8Decode into one .cpp with a prototype in utf8.h.
findings.benefit: 400 B of .rodata (MEASURED: two 'r _ZL5utf8d' entries of 0x190 at 005dc7d0 and 005dceb8 in riptopl-nm-size-sorted.full.txt).
findings.evidence: Regex scan for utf8.h includes over src,include: only fntsys.cpp:12 and textshape.cpp:12; utf8Decode used at fntsys.cpp:766,828,898,1233 and textshape.cpp:21. nm lines 1757-1758. Upstream-derived code (Hoehrmann DFA, MIT).

findings.title: utf8d decoder table is static in utf8.h and linked twice (textshape.cpp and fntsys.cpp)
findings.problem: utf8.h defines the 400-byte DFA table as static const and utf8Decode as static, so each translation unit that includes it gets its own copy. The shipped ELF has two identical 400-byte _ZL5utf8d objects, one from each includer.
findings.fix: Give the table one definition: make it inline constexpr in the header (C++17 inline variable) and utf8Decode inline, or define both once in textshape.cpp and declare them in utf8.h.
findings.benefit: 400 bytes of .rodata removed. MEASURED: raw/riptopl-nm-size-sorted.full.txt lines 1757-1758, two _ZL5utf8d of 0x190 bytes.
findings.evidence: grep '#include "include/utf8.h"' over src/RiptOPL: only src/gfx/fntsys.cpp:12 and src/gfx/textshape.cpp:12. Read include/utf8.h 1-51 (static const uint8_t utf8d[] 21-36, static utf8Decode 38-49). evidence/RiptOPL/raw/riptopl-nm-size-sorted.full.txt:1757-1758: 005dc7d0 00000190 r _ZL5utf8d and 005dceb8 00000190 r _ZL5utf8d.

findings.title: vmcsaves holds 4.9 KB of .bss for the whole run: vsCopy's static vs_save_t and vsWritePsu's static pad
findings.problem: vsCopy's static vs_save_t s (1123; 3896 B, not the ~2.5 KB its comment says) and vsWritePsu's static pad[1024] (862) are used only during one copy but stay in .bss for the whole run; vmcsaves.o has 4924 B of .bss. Both run on GUI code paths whose thread stack is 128 KB.
findings.fix: Drop the two static keywords so both live on the stack during the copy (the memsets at 1127 and 881 already initialise them) and correct the size in the comment.
findings.benefit: 4920 B of RAM freed (MEASURED: riptopl-per-object.tsv vmcsaves.o bss 4924; nm sizes vsCopy::s 0xf38, vsWritePsu::pad 0x400); peak stack grows by 4.9 KB of 128 KB.
findings.evidence: evidence/RiptOPL/raw/riptopl-nm-size-sorted.full.txt: _ZZL6vsCopyiPKcS0_iS0_E1s size 0xf38 and _ZZL10vsWritePsuPK9vs_save_tPKcE3pad size 0x400; riptopl-per-object.tsv: vmcsaves.o bss 4924; riptopl-stack-heap.txt: main ELF _stack_size 0x20000. Callers: VMC Saves dialog (guigame.cpp:439-467) and File Manager paste (guifilemgr.cpp:448, 452, 559), INFERRED main thread. Deepest path: vsCopy (s) -> vsWriteVmc (about 2 KB of entries and first[]) or vsWritePsu (pad, two path buffers).

findings.title: A torn first save (favourites.bin.new without favourites.bin) or a zero-length store file blocks every later favourite/recent save
findings.problem: With the primary missing and an incomplete but recognised .new, favReadFile returns editable = missing && stagedMissing = 0 (420-421) and favPrepareSave returns ok = missing && recovery.missing = false (540), so addItem, removeByIdAndText and recentRecord refuse to save for good. The first-ever save writes .new while no primary exists (553-560), so a power cut or card pull there leaves exactly this state. A readable zero-length primary (for example made on a PC) is never editable either (231-234). Only deleting the files by hand recovers.
findings.fix: When the primary is missing, treat a recognised-but-incomplete .new as replaceable in favReadFile and favPrepareSave (it never held an authoritative list), and treat a readable zero-length file as an empty editable list.
findings.benefit: Removes a permanent 'save failed' state for favourites and recents; three condition edits, no added lines.
findings.evidence: Traced favReadFile 395-423: primary missing -> complete 0; staged torn OFAV -> favParseImage keeps recognized = 1 but complete = 0 (283-323), so stagedComplete = 0 and line 421 gives editable = 1 && 0. favPrepareSave 537-541 uses recovery.missing only. favParseImage 231-234 returns with editable 0 for size 0 while recognized stays 1; with no .new, line 421 again yields 0. addItem 1013-1016, removeByIdAndText 1060-1063, recentRecord 1493-1496 all return 0 when not editable. Trigger (power loss in the first-save window, or an externally created empty file) is rare.

findings.title: Art cache eviction frees a cover's pixels while the HIRES replay of the previous frame may still upload them
findings.problem: The LRU scan accepts any slot with lastUsed < guiFrameId, so a cover drawn in the previous frame (lastUsed == guiFrameId-1, typically the one that just scrolled off) is evicted and cacheClearItem frees texture.Mem in the middle of drawing the next frame. The repo itself states that in HIRES the DMA thread keeps replaying the previous frame, whose inline uploads reference those pixels, and guards theme and font frees with rmDiscardFrame for that reason; this per-frame eviction has no such guard, so the replay can read freed (and possibly already reused) memory.
findings.fix: Start the scan with rtime = guiFrameId - 1 so a slot drawn in the previous frame is never evicted; in the rare case every slot was drawn last frame the claim simply happens one frame later.
findings.benefit: Removes corrupted-cover flashes during scrolling in the 704-wide, 720p and 1080i HIRES modes (INFERRED from the repo's own HIRES model; not observed on hardware). No size change.
findings.evidence: Read texcache.cpp:388-407 (scan uses lastUsed < rtime, rtime = guiFrameId) and :467 (cacheClearItem(oldestEntry,1) on the GUI thread during cacheGetTextureEx, i.e. while the frame is being built). cacheClearItem :24-31 does rmUnloadTexture + free(Mem). Repo statements of the hazard: renderman.cpp:188-189 (HIRES replays the last frame; flip before referenced pixel buffers are freed), fntsys.cpp:120-123 (inline uploads reference pixels until the frame, under HIRES its replay, is retired), themes.cpp:1836-1839 (rmDiscardFrame before freeing the theme), saveicon.cpp:807 (retired model kept two frames for HIRES). grep rmDiscardFrame over src: only themes.cpp:1839, fntsys.cpp:138; grep cacheClearItem: texcache eviction path has no frame guard. gsKit HIRES internals are not in the repo, hence INFERRED.

findings.title: EthSupport::reconnectSmb clears the coalescing flags at its end, so a settings reconnect requested while it runs is dropped
findings.problem: requestReconnect (GUI thread, Network page OK) only sets reconnectRequested_ when reconnectQueued_ is 1 (692-696). reconnectQueued_ stays 1 for the whole reconnectSmb run on the IO worker (DHCP/link waits, logon, open-share poll of up to 90 s) and lines 628-629 then clear both flags, so a second OK pressed with corrected settings during that run never reconnects with them.
findings.fix: Move the two clears (628-629) to the top of reconnectSmb, before it reads any settings, so a request that arrives during the run queues a fresh reconnect.
findings.benefit: Fixes a lost settings apply (session stays on the old IP/share until another manual Reconnect); 0 lines, the two assignments move.
findings.evidence: Read ethsupport.cpp:601-709. Callers: grep ethRequestReconnect -> ethsupport.cpp:725 (init) and guisettings.cpp:1056 (Network page exit/OK, no wait on the worker). reconnectSmb runs via IO_CUSTOM_SIMPLEACTION (705); it calls loadModules/initSmb -> netApplyConfig (link/DHCP waitValidState up to ~30 s, netsupport.cpp:68-89) and smbConnect -> smbOpenShare (poll up to 900 x 100 ms, ethsupport.cpp:67-73). That the user can reopen and apply the Network page while the worker is blocked in those RPC waits is inferred from the non-blocking request path, not tested.

findings.title: File Manager label table allocates 160 bytes for each of 512 entries; folder rows never hold more than 47
findings.problem: fmLabel is malloc'd as FM_MAX x FM_ROW_TEXT = 512 x 160 = 80 KB while the File Manager is open. In a folder a label is only a card save title, clamped to FM_TITLE (48) at line 238, and is empty everywhere but a card root; only the handful of drive rows use the label text at all, and their row is clipped on screen long before 160 characters.
findings.fix: Give fmLabel its own row width of about 80 bytes (enough for the drive words and any title) instead of FM_ROW_TEXT.
findings.benefit: 40,960 B less heap while the File Manager is open INFERRED (512 x (160 - 80)); fewer FM_ERR_MEMORY failures on a fragmented heap
findings.evidence: Read guifilemgr.cpp:53,58,153-163 (drive labels: root + words), 225-239 (card title clamp to FM_TITLE), 256-260 (labels empty except mc root), 328-332 (row text, names already cut to %.60s), 619 (malloc). Drive count is bounded by MAX_BDM_DEVICES + 2 MMCE + 2 MC + pfs0 + udpfs + smb0 (lines 181-221). The on-screen clip width is INFERRED from the %.60s name limit, not measured.

findings.title: File Manager walks re-list big folders and probe every removed file twice on all devices
findings.problem: fmChildren re-runs fmList (opendir, readdir and one stat per entry) on a 4x larger array each time a folder fills it: a 2000-entry folder is read 4 times with 64+256+1024+2000 stats instead of 2000. fmRemove follows every successful remove/rmdir with fmExists (a failed open plus a failed opendir) and pauses 50 ms per retry on any device, though its comment names only the card. Both run on the GUI thread inside fmPaste/fmDeleteSelection (guifilemgr.cpp:428-514), which shows a static text screen meanwhile; fmCopyTo also walks the tree once more for the progress total.
findings.fix: Read a folder in one readdir pass in fmChildren, growing the array with realloc, instead of re-listing; in fmRemove do the fmExists check and the pause-retry only when fmIsMc(path), and take remove()/rmdir()'s result as is elsewhere.
findings.benefit: Deleting a 2000-file ART folder on USB: ~4000 fewer fileXio calls from fmRemove plus ~1300 fewer stats and 3 fewer readdir passes (counts READ from the code; time per call INFERRED ~1 ms, so seconds).
findings.evidence: Read filemgr.cpp 174-221 (fmList stats each entry via fmIsDir), 225-248 (cap 64, x4 per retry up to 65536, full fmList each time), 250-285 (fmTreeWalk), 435-449 (fmCopyTo walks fmTreeSize first), 468-477 (fmRemove: remove + fmExists, 4 tries with fmPause on any device), 479-498 (fmDeleteTree). Callers guifilemgr.cpp:428-485 and 487-514 run on the GUI thread (dialog handlers, guiRenderTextScreen progress). Per-call latency not measured.

findings.title: IO drains poll once per ~0.25 s delay(1) spin: launch/exit sees an empty queue up to 0.25 s late; lwnbdctl's 1000-tick bound is ~4 min
findings.problem: deinitEx, deinit and miniDeinit drain through IoQueue::blockOps, which re-checks hasPending() only after each delay(1), a 0x01000000-iteration NOP spin that opl.cpp:1269-1272 itself puts at about a quarter second. A queued request that ends just after a check is noticed up to ~0.25 s later, on a black Please Wait screen, on every launch or exit that finds the queue busy. The same tick unit makes LWNBD_IO_DRAIN_TICKS = 1000 a ~250 s bound, so a stuck request freezes NBD start for minutes instead of failing it.
findings.fix: In IoQueue::blockOps replace delay(1) with DelayThread(10000) (10 ms, yields the CPU) and restate the budgets in that unit: EXIT_IO_DRAIN_TICKS 100, LAUNCH_IO_DRAIN_TICKS 1000, and LWNBD_IO_DRAIN_TICKS at the intended bound. Update the unit comment at opl.cpp:1269-1275 to match.
findings.benefit: Up to ~0.24 s less black screen per launch/exit whenever IO is still queued (INFERRED: delay(1) = 16.8M x 4 NOPs ~ 0.25 s at 294 MHz, poll step becomes 10 ms); NBD preflight bound drops from ~250 s to the intended value; no change when the queue is empty
findings.evidence: Read opl.cpp:1257-1277 (budgets 4 and 40 ticks, comment that one tick is ~0.25 s), callers 1328, 1422, 1962. Read ioman.cpp:360-398 (while hasPending(): delay(1), count down timeoutTicks) and 467-476; hasPending() is head_ != NULL (include/ioqueue.h:31) and head_ is unlinked only after the handler returns (ioman.cpp:140-156), so completion is seen only at the next tick. Read util.cpp:941-950 (delay = count x 0x01000000 loops of 4 NOPs). grep ioBlockOpsTimed(1: opl.cpp x3, lwnbdctl.cpp:150 with LWNBD_IO_DRAIN_TICKS=1000 (lwnbdctl.cpp:78); menusys.cpp:248 passes 0 and is unaffected. autolaunch.cpp:204 also states delay() ticks are ~0.25 s. Tick length is arithmetic, not measured.

findings.title: On-screen keyboard moves the caret and backspaces one byte at a time, splitting multi-byte UTF-8 in an existing name
findings.problem: L1/R1 do caret-- / caret++ and both backspaces memmove out exactly one byte, while the view scroll already steps by UTF-8 characters (diaKeybNextChar/PrevChar). Renaming a game (menusys.cpp:306-316) or file whose name holds multi-byte UTF-8 leaves orphan lead/continuation bytes after one backspace, or inserts a key inside a sequence; confirming writes that invalid name through gsOf()->rename.
findings.fix: Use the existing helpers: caret = diaKeybPrevChar(text, caret) / diaKeybNextChar(text, caret, len) for L1/R1, and make both backspaces remove the bytes from diaKeybPrevChar(text, caret) to caret. ASCII text behaves exactly as now.
findings.benefit: Prevents renames that write broken UTF-8 into game/file names; no new code, four expressions change (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read diaeditors.cpp:298-307, 351-367, 395-403 (byte steps) and 112-126 (UTF-8-aware helpers used only for view at :225-227). Callers seeding existing names: menusys.cpp:306-309 (game rename via guiShowKeyboard), guifilemgr.cpp:522-523. INFERRED part: which devices return UTF-8 names; BDM FatFs is built with FF_LFN_UNICODE 0 / FF_CODE_PAGE 869 (modules/bdm/bdmfs_fatfs/fatfs/include/ffconf.h:87,136), so the case needs a source such as SMB/NFS/HDD returning UTF-8.

findings.title: PS1 save icons: colour-0 texels meant to be transparent are drawn as opaque black
findings.problem: saveIconFromPs1CardImage writes palette colour 0x0000 as texel 0 and sets bit 15 only on other colours, i.e. it encodes PS1 transparency in the A1 bit of a CT16 texture. The frames are drawn through rmDrawPixmap -> drawQuad, which enables alpha blending and the alpha test only for CT32 (or CT32-CLUT) textures; for CT16 it turns both off, so every transparent texel is written as black and the icon shows on a black square.
findings.fix: Decode the PS1 frames as CT32 (alpha 0 for colour 0, 0x80 otherwise) so drawQuad's existing CT32 path blends and alpha-tests them; the three frames grow from 1.5 KB to 3 KB. Update test_ps1_save_icons.py's expected texel values with it.
findings.benefit: PS1 icons render with their intended transparency instead of a black box; +1.5 KB peak for a shown PS1 icon (INFERRED: 3 frames x 256 texels x 2 extra bytes).
findings.evidence: Read saveicon.cpp:631-636 (color == 0 ? 0 : color | 0x8000), :1031-1036 (siPs1Tex PSM GS_PSM_CT16, Clut left NULL by the memset at :950), :1238-1239 (rmDrawPixmap(&siPs1Tex[frame]...)); renderman.cpp:513-517 drawPixmap -> drawQuad :445-451 (alpha on only for CT32 or CLUT CT32, else PrimAlphaEnable OFF and GS_ATEST_OFF). test_ps1_save_icons.py:158,181 confirms palette entry 0 = 0x0000 decodes to texel 0000. grep GS_PSM_CT16 over src: only saveicon.cpp and atlas.cpp, so no other CT16 texture relies on drawQuad's current behaviour. Visual result not observed on hardware.

findings.title: Unchecked eth_linkmode from conf_network.cfg makes ee_core index SmapLinkModeArgs[mode-1] out of bounds; ps2_ip can overrun g_ps2_ip[16]
findings.problem: settingsio.cpp:1924 reads eth_linkmode with configGetInt and no check; system.cpp:1561 truncates it into the u8 g_ps2_ETHOpMode. set_ipconfig (util.c:96-99, run at every game start from main.c:154) tests only != AUTO and then reads SmapLinkModeArgs[mode-1], a 4-entry local array, so eth_linkmode=5..255 (or -1) reads a stack word as a char* and strncpy copies 6 bytes from it: garbage SMAP args or an address error at game start. The menu treats these values as AUTO (netsupport.cpp:408-423). Second path: in UDPBD/UDPFS modes system.cpp:1580 sprintf's unchecked %d ps2_ip values (sscanf at settingsio.cpp:1950) into g_ps2_ip[16]; a field over 3 digits leaves it unterminated, strlen at util.c:85 then spans the netmask, and with a non-auto link mode g_ipconfig[64] overflows by up to ~15 bytes.
findings.fix: In util.c:96 also require g_ps2_ETHOpMode < ETH_OP_MODE_COUNT (the unused enum end at ee_core.h:51), so out-of-range values act as AUTO like the menu. At system.cpp:1580 print the four values as (u8) with %u, as line 1577 already does, or use snprintf with sizeof(config->g_ps2_ip).
findings.justification: Both changes stay on existing lines (one extra condition, one format change). They close an out-of-bounds read that can crash every launch and a .bss overrun, both caused by one bad config value.
findings.benefit: Removes an out-of-bounds stack read (wild-pointer strncpy) at ee_core init and a g_ipconfig overrun of up to ~15 bytes (INFERRED from 16+16+16+9+6 byte layout); 0 lines net
findings.evidence: Read util.c:71-102 (SmapLinkModeArgs[4] local, index g_ps2_ETHOpMode-1, guard only != ETH_OP_MODE_AUTO); main.c:154 calls set_ipconfig unconditionally; settingsio.cpp:1921-1956 (configGetInt eth_linkmode, sscanf %d ps2_ip, no range checks); system.cpp:1561 (u8 copy), 1577-1582 (%d sprintf into char[16] only for sysModeIsNetBlock); netsupport.cpp:408-423 default -> AUTO. grep ETH_OP_MODE_COUNT: only definitions at ee_core.h:51 and include/opl.h:115. GUI path (guisettings.cpp:985 diaGetInt) is an enum list, so the trigger is a hand-edited or corrupted conf_network.cfg. INFERRED: what the out-of-range stack word holds, hence crash vs garbage args.

findings.title: Xerabora mode: the Hardcore filter on a game's achievement list always shows an empty page
findings.problem: Square cycles achFilter 0..3 on any 'A' page (menusys.cpp:1239). In Xerabora mode achievementsXeraboraPage skips every entry with !a->hardcore when filter==3, but xeraEntryMember only fills hardcore for kind 'G'; for 'A' entries it stays 0 from the memset at achievements.cpp:371. So filter 3 (Hardcore) always lists nothing, with total 0.
findings.fix: In Xerabora mode let Square cycle only All/Earned/Locked (filter modulo 3 when gRAMode is RA_MODE_XERABORA), or drop the filter==3 clause for kind 'A' if the xeRAbora /game document turns out to carry a per-achievement hardcore field to parse instead.
findings.justification: One condition in the existing key handler removes a filter state that can never show data; it is smaller than parsing a field the document does not appear to provide.
findings.benefit: Fixes a UI state that always shows an empty list; about 1 line changed
findings.evidence: Read achievements.cpp:314-336 (hardcore set only under x->kind=='G'), 371 (memset), 397-417 (filter==3 && !a->hardcore -> continue), menusys.cpp:1238-1241 (Square on achKind=='A' cycles % 4). The test fixture .github/scripts/test_ra_xerabora_browser.py:40-54 models the /game document with no hardcore key per achievement; that the real xeRAbora document also lacks it is INFERRED from that fixture.

findings.title: ZombieZone_patches scans 768 KB past the end of 32 MB RAM
findings.problem: ZombieZone_patches searches from 0x001c0000 for 0x01f00000 bytes, i.e. up to 0x020c0000; every other scan in patches.c stops at or below 0x01FC0000. If the scePadEnd pattern is not found below 0x02000000 (a different build under one of the four serials at patches.c:105-108), find_pattern_with_mask reads 0x02000000, which no TLB entry maps (the cached RAM entries end at 0x01FFFFFF, tlb.c:84-92), and the TLB miss stops the boot instead of skipping the patch.
findings.fix: Change the size argument to 0x01e40000 (0x02000000 - 0x001c0000).
findings.benefit: Removes a TLB-miss hang path at boot for four titles when the pattern is absent; one constant, no size change (INFERRED)
findings.evidence: Read patches.c:392-415 (ZZ search 0x001c0000 + 0x01f00000) and the other find_pattern_with_mask calls (patches.c:193,227,473,501,780-785: end addresses 0x01F00000, 0x01F00000, 0x01FC0000, 0x01FC0000, <0x00A00000). util.c:117-121 reads buf[i+j] up to buf+bufsize. tlb.c:84-92 (same layout as the kernel default, per the note at ra.c:99-103, which also records that a TLB miss hangs the game). Only call is under file_eq_gameid (patches.c:963-965). INFERRED part: that a build of these serials without the pattern exists.

findings.title: config.path stores the slot-resolved massN: form, so the boot read loses the device type and can wait about 14 s
findings.problem: prepareCustomSettingsPath rewrites customSettingsTarget in place (usb:/CFG becomes massN:/CFG through bdmResolveBootDir), and that rewritten text is what writeConfigPathRedirect saves. At boot the untyped literal massN: goes to resolveLiteralMassSlot with the full budget. It loads USB, then MX4SIO, then iLink and ATA whatever the settings say, waits 3+3+8 s on the main thread when the device is absent, and accepts whichever device registered under that slot number, which depends on load order.
findings.fix: Pass gCustomSettingsPath (the user's own spelling) to writeConfigPathRedirect at line 2420 instead of the resolved customSettingsTarget. The boot read already runs prepareCustomSettingsPath on whatever it reads.
findings.benefit: With the settings device missing, the worst-case boot wait for a typed usb: path drops from about 14 s (3000+3000+8000 ms) to 3 s, with no unrequested MX4SIO/iLink/ATA loads (INFERRED from bdmboot.cpp budgets)
findings.evidence: Read settingsio.cpp:647-664 (prepareCustomSettingsPath -> bdmResolveBootDir, the full-budget resolver), 2367-2399 and 2419-2420 (writeConfigPathRedirect(customSettingsTarget) after the in-place rewrite), 964-969 (boot read). bdmboot.cpp:116-126 (rewriteBootDir writes massN:), 151-229 (literal slot: untyped tiers USB, SDC, iLink+ATA, no identity check), 295-299, 472-477 (resolve budgets 3000/10000/3000/8000 vs bootstrap 1500/5000/1500/3500 at 479-486). _loadConfig runs on the main thread from init() (opl.cpp:1661, 1719). That slot numbers follow registration order is INFERRED.

findings.title: elfldr linkfile keeps each -ffunction-sections input as its own output section: ~4 KB of section headers in the embedded elfldr_irx
findings.problem: elfldr is built with -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections (ps2.yaml:619) but the linker script only collects *(.text), *(.rodata), *(.data), *(.sbss), *(.bss), so every .text.<fn>, .rodata.<fn>.str1.8 and .bss.<var> input section becomes an orphan output section: size -A lists 73 sections for bin/elfldr.elf. The ELF is embedded whole as elfldr_irx (21,476 bytes, type D in the main ELF), but the parent only reads the ELF header, the program headers and PT_LOAD data (elfldr_noreset.cpp:220-237), so the section header table and .shstrtab are dead bytes held in EE RAM for the whole run.
findings.fix: In elfldr/linkfile collect the suffixed sections into their parents: *(.text .text.*), *(.rodata .rodata.*), *(.data .data.*), *(.sbss .sbss.*), *(.bss .bss.*). Keep the flags and --gc-sections; nothing else changes.
findings.benefit: INFERRED from MEASURED sizes: blob 21,476 B vs loadable span 16,900 B (0x84000..end of .data); ~75 headers x 40 B + ~1.4 KB of names shrink to ~10 headers, so ~3.9 KB less in the unpacked main ELF and in resident RAM; the packed file gains less.
findings.evidence: Read elfldr/linkfile:1-86 and ps2.yaml:615-624 (cflags -fdata-sections -ffunction-sections, ldflags --gc-sections). evidence/RiptOPL/raw/riptopl-size-A.txt:68-143 (size -A bin/elfldr.elf: .text 5616 at 540672 followed by .text.readAll ... .text.sceSifGetSreg, .rodata.*.str1.8, .data 4 at 557568, .bss.elfdata.0). raw/artifacts.tsv:18 and raw/riptopl-top80-symbols.txt:39: elfldr_irx 21476 D. Grep elfldr_irx over the repo: only elfldr_noreset.cpp:29-30,220,227,232 (ELF header, phdrs, PT_LOAD copy). Section-header count and name bytes are estimated from the size -A listing (INFERRED); the binary was not rebuilt.

findings.title: elfldr wipeUserMem calls GetMemorySize() in the loop condition: 507,904 kernel calls on every child-loader launch
findings.problem: The loop condition i < GetMemorySize() is re-evaluated every 64 bytes; GetMemorySize is an external libkernel call (a kernel syscall, INFERRED) the compiler cannot hoist, so a 32 MB console makes (0x2000000-0x100000)/64 = 507,904 calls, and a 128 MB DTL-T10000 four times that. It runs on the EE in main() before SifLoadElf (loader.c:420) on every Neutrino, POPSTARTER, Ember and app handoff. POPSLoader's child loader has the same loop; Launchstation's loader.c:216-217 already reads the size once.
findings.fix: Read GetMemorySize() once into a local before the loop and compare against it.
findings.benefit: INFERRED: removes ~508K syscall round trips per launch; at an assumed 100-200 cycles each on the 294.9 MHz EE that is roughly 0.15-0.35 s of black screen per handoff (more on 128 MB units).
findings.evidence: Read elfldr/loader.c:219-229 and :387-475 (wipeUserMem called at :420 on every path). Grep 'i < GetMemorySize()' over src/: RiptOPL elfldr/loader.c:222 and POPSLoader src/elf_loader/src/loader/src/loader.c:74 (read :66-81). Launchstation loader/loader.c:212-224 hoists end = GetMemorySize(). That GetMemorySize is a syscall and its per-call cost are not verifiable from the repos (SDK not read): INFERRED.

findings.title: vmc_groups.cpp: eight malformed title ids can never match a startup id
findings.problem: getGroupIdForTitleId does an exact strcmp (vmc_groups.cpp:1465) against the game's startup id (guigame.cpp:493,529), which has the dotted 11-char form SLUS_207.54. Entries SLUS_20754, SLUS_20824, SCES_50422, SLES_50422, SCES_51154, SLES_51154, SLES-5350 and SSCES_540.95 lack the dot, use a dash or have an extra letter, so these games never get their series VMC and silently fall back to a per-game card.
findings.fix: Correct the eight strings to the dotted form (SLUS_207.54, SLUS_208.24, SCES_504.22, SLES_504.22, SCES_511.54, SLES_511.54, SCES_540.95; SLES-5350 is most likely SLES_535.06, next to SCES_535.06 at line 496). None of the corrected ids is already in the table.
findings.benefit: Minor bug fixed: 8 titles get their shared group card. 0 lines, 0 bytes.
findings.evidence: Parsed all 97 arrays with a script: 8 ids fail the 11-char XXXX_NNN.NN shape, at lines 443,444,464,465,472,473,498,614. tests/host/test_vmc_groups.cpp:16-17,29 counts these as a KNOWN DATA ISSUE but does not assert. Grep for the dotted forms in vmc_groups.cpp: no matches. Caller format (dotted startup id from CONFIG_ITEM_STARTUP or gsOf(support)->startup) is INFERRED from guigame.cpp:521-529 and the dotted form of the other 1038 entries; the intended id for SLES-5350 is INFERRED.

findings.title: oplIGRShutdown writes poff uncached with SIF_RPC_M_NOWBDC and no cache flush
findings.problem: poffData is a 64-byte-aligned stack slot; its cache line can still be dirty in the write-back D-cache from earlier IGR-thread calls. The value is stored through UNCACHED_SEG and the call uses SIF_RPC_M_NOWBDC, so nothing writes back or invalidates that line; if it is evicted before the SIF DMA reads memory, the stale stack word replaces poff. CDVDMAN then powers the console off (poff != 0, cdvdman.c:289-295) on a normal IGR exit, or skips the power-off on the L3+R3 path (padhook.c:565,669). freeze_diag.c:185 and :214 call FlushCache(0) before the same kind of store for this reason.
findings.fix: Store poff with a normal write and drop SIF_RPC_M_NOWBDC so SifCallRpc writes the send buffer back itself (no extra code); or call FlushCache(0) before the uncached store as freeze_diag.c does.
findings.benefit: Removes a rare wrong-poff case on every IGR exit (unwanted power-off or missed power-off); no size change (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read cd_igr_rpc.c:1-26; callers padhook.c:565 (oplIGRShutdown(0)) and :669 (oplIGRShutdown(1)), freeze_diag.c:235. IOP side cdvdfsv.c:225-250 reads *(int *)buf as poff, cdvdman.c:279-299 powers off when non-zero. grep SIF_RPC_M_NOWBDC over *.c/*.cpp/*.h: freeze_diag.c:187 and :216 (both preceded by FlushCache(0) at :185/:214) and cd_igr_rpc.c:22 (no flush). INFERRED: the eviction timing between the store and the DMA was not observed on hardware.

findings.title: .cht parser: an indented comment line becomes a blank-named cheat, and lines over 255 chars are split with one byte dropped
findings.problem: For a line like '  // note', term_str cuts at '//' leaving '  ', trim_str returns -1 on an all-space string without clearing it, and strlen>0 makes it a cheat NAME: before a cheat's codes it renames the cheat to spaces; between codes it splits the cheat, and in Select mode the second half starts disabled. A line longer than 255 chars is capped, but buf advances by len+1 (256), so byte 255 is dropped and the tail is parsed as its own line (a long comment's tail becomes a cheat name).
findings.fix: In trim_str set s[0] = NUL before returning -1 for an all-space string. In parse_buf compute the advance from lfIdx (lfIdx + 1, or strlen when there is no LF) before capping len, so the rest of an over-long line is skipped.
findings.justification: One statement in trim_str and one changed expression; both fix wrong cheat names/splits from ordinary user-supplied .cht text (cht.tar packs are treated as untrusted input by the comment at 330-333). Names also key the remembered picks, so a wrong name restores the wrong cheat.
findings.benefit: Correct parsing of indented comments and long lines; no size change (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Traced parse_buf (cheatman.cpp:312-385) by hand: term_str :227-240 with is_cmt_str :205-208, trim_str :261-288 (early return at :269-270 leaves the string), is_cheat_code :167-182 returns 0 for '  ', name branch :346-351. Long line: lfIdx 300 -> len capped 255 (:334-335) -> buf += 256 (:381). Input reaches here from load_cheats/load_cheats_buf via sbLoadCheats (supportbase.cpp:1779,1811). PS2rd-derived code; upstream parity not checked.

findings.title: diagSave keeps a static 16 KB copy buffer in .bss for the whole run
findings.problem: static char copy[DIAG_SIZE] (16 KB) is reserved in every build although it is only used while DIAG.TXT is written: from the Drive Status 'save' action (drivestatus.cpp:161) and, with Debug on, before an MMCE launch (mmcesupport.cpp:1335,1436,1666).
findings.fix: malloc(DIAG_SIZE) at the start of diagSave, return 0 if it fails, free it after the write.
findings.justification: Adds one NULL check; returns 16 KB of EE RAM for the whole session for a rare debug save.
findings.benefit: 16 KB .bss removed (INFERRED: char copy[16 * 1024]); no ELF file size change.
findings.evidence: Read diagsave.cpp 1-55; DIAG_SIZE 16*1024 at line 17. Callers from grep diagSave over src: drivestatus.cpp:161, mmcesupport.cpp:1335/1436/1666 (via diagSaveBeforeLaunch). diagsave.cpp is in src/core, compiled into the main ELF (ps2.yaml:641 per brief). diaglog.cpp:46-71 diagCopy returns 0..size, so the write length is never negative.

findings.title: EthSource::update share picker: 64 KB ShareEntry_t sharelist[128] on the IO worker stack is a SIF DMA target with no cache maintenance
findings.problem: The share picker passes a stack array (128 x 512 B = 64 KB of the IO worker's 96 KB stack) as EE_addr; the shipped smbman_ra copies each entry into it with sceSifSetDma (smb_fio.c:1000, DMA_sendEE). Nothing writes back or invalidates the EE data cache for that range and the array is not 64-byte aligned, so a dirty or stale line from earlier deep stack use can override the DMA'd share names that are then read at 847-849.
findings.fix: Align the array to 64 bytes and write back/invalidate its range (SifWriteBackDCache, the pattern fileXioRead uses for its receive buffer) before the GETSHARELIST devctl. Optionally lower maxent (only the 31-char name is kept) to give back most of the 64 KB of worker stack.
findings.justification: Adds one cache-maintenance call and an alignment attribute: the IOP writes this buffer by DMA behind the EE cache, which is a correctness hole on real hardware; one line is the smallest way to make the read coherent.
findings.benefit: Removes a non-coherent DMA read on the share-picker path; with maxent 32 the frame drops from 64 KB to 16 KB of the 96 KB worker stack (INFERRED: sizeof(ShareEntry_t) = 512 per tests/smb2-live/inc-sdk/ps2smb.h:79-83).
findings.evidence: Read ethsupport.cpp:829-866; update() runs on the IO worker via menuDeferredUpdate (opl.cpp:855-871, handler registered opl.cpp:1691); worker stack 96 KB (ioman.cpp:42-44). ps2.yaml:146-154 + :652 show smbman_ra is the embedded smbman; its GETSHARELIST sends entries with DMA_sendEE -> sceSifSetDma (smb_fio.c:871-889, 999-1000). smb2man returns -ENOTSUP (smb2man.c:1708-1710). ShareEntry_t size taken from the in-repo SDK header copy. That fileXioDevctl does no cache op on pointers inside arg is INFERRED (ps2sdk source not in repo). git history: the stack array is inherited from upstream OPL (git show 31e9b1f4^:src/ethsupport.c line 472).

findings.title: HDD PS1 favourite launch and Ember settings save rebuild the whole VCD/Ember list on the GUI thread
findings.problem: When a PS1/Ember favourite is launched before this session built the HDD PS1 list (the HDD page never entered PS1/mixed view), launchVcd calls buildVcdGameList directly on the GUI thread with the IO worker blocked. That rebuild walks the APA table, mounts every __.POPS* and __.EMBER* partition, scans them, and runs cueGameSizeMB (opendir plus a stat per .bin) for every Ember game. No frame is drawn meanwhile, so the menu looks hung. menuSaveCueSettings at least prints a text screen first. launchVcd prints nothing.
findings.fix: Before the cold rebuild in launchVcd, render the wait text with host::ui().renderTextScreen(_l(_STR_PLEASE_WAIT)), as menusys.cpp:1004 already does for saveCueSettings. The larger fix is to run the rebuild through guiHandleDeferedIO on the IO worker.
findings.justification: Adds one line. Today the launch gives no feedback while a scan of several PFS mounts plus per-game directory walks runs on the render thread. A wait screen is the smallest change and uses an existing helper and string.
findings.benefit: Removes a silent UI hang of roughly 0.3-2 s on the first HDD PS1 favourite launch per session (INFERRED: mount and directory-scan costs scale with containers and Ember games; not measured).
findings.evidence: Read hddsupport.cpp 1530-1790 (buildVcdGameList: mounts and cueGameSizeMB per Ember folder), 2308-2345 (launchVcd cold path), 3356-3383 (saveCueSettings). Caller: favsupport.cpp:1290-1316 FavSource::launch -> launchVcd, reached from menu input on the GUI thread. Input dispatch runs after endFrame (gui.cpp:114-124, brief section 6), so publishVcdGameList's ui lock does not deadlock but no frames render. menusys.cpp:1004 renders _STR_SAVING_SETTINGS before saveCueSettings. cuesupport.cpp:963-988 shows the per-folder opendir plus stat walk. The duration is INFERRED, not measured.

findings.title: When a font's 4 atlases are full, cacheGlyph drops the glyph and FreeType re-renders it on every draw and measure
findings.problem: Nothing is evicted. Once all ATLAS_MAX (4) 256x256 atlases of a font are full, glyphAtlasPlace returns 0 and cacheGlyph returns NULL with the entry still invalid. The character is not drawn, the text closes up around it, and every later renderString or calcDimensions call runs FT_Load_Char + FT_Render_Glyph for it again and walks all four atlas trees. At 720p (native 720 lines, renderman.cpp:74) the 17 px font is ~25 px, so a CJK glyph cell is ~25x26 and an atlas holds ~90-100, ~400 per font. Japanese.yml alone has 490 distinct CJK characters.
findings.fix: On a placement failure, mark the entry valid with no allocation (as glyphAtlasPlace already does for empty bitmaps), so a full atlas costs nothing per frame. To make the characters show, raise ATLAS_MAX to 8: atlases are created lazily, so only a font that fills four pays 64 KB per extra atlas.
findings.justification: The problem is missing CJK characters, plus FreeType re-rasterising every missing glyph on the GUI thread each frame. Caching the failure is one assignment. Raising ATLAS_MAX is a constant change that allocates nothing for fonts that never need it, which makes it the simplest way to fit a CJK UI at 720p.
findings.benefit: Stops per-frame FreeType re-rendering of every glyph that does not fit (INFERRED: tens of microseconds each on the EE). With ATLAS_MAX 8, CJK UIs at 720p/576p keep all their characters (capacity arithmetic INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read fntsys.cpp:545-578 (returns 0 after ATLAS_MAX), 608-625 (isValid stays 0 on failure, so the next call loads again) and atlas.cpp:105-139 and 164-177 (guillotine split, width+1 x height+1 per glyph). updateAspectRatioLocked fntsys.cpp:654-674: char size 17 at 72*hs DPI, hs = native/480. renderman.cpp:74: 720p row 1280x720 (hs 1.5). The python count gives 490 distinct CJK characters in lng/fork/Japanese.yml, 645 in SChinese. Capacity: 256/25 x 256/26 = 10 x 9 = 90 per atlas (INFERRED; real glyph sizes depend on the language font).

findings.title: configWrite restores the snapshot only when the file is shorter than the OLD file, so a save cut short after it grew stays truncated
findings.problem: After a failed save the damage test is curLen < originalLen. When the new content is longer than the old file and the write stops part way (short write on a flaky or full device, the #184 case this machinery exists for), a file with originalLen <= curLen < new length is left as is: the tail settings are lost and the last line is cut mid-value, though a good snapshot is in RAM. The restore write's result is also unchecked (1681) while the log says restored.
findings.fix: Keep fileBuffer->totalQueued in a local before closeFileBuffer and restore when curLen differs from it (only on the path where the file was opened); leave the open-failure path without a restore as now.
findings.justification: Replaces one comparison and adds one local. The concrete problem is a truncated settings file left on disk after a failed save while the intact original is held in RAM; comparing with the length that was meant to land is the smallest correct damage test.
findings.benefit: Fixes a minor settings-loss case on failed saves to USB/HDD/MMCE/SMB; no size change (READ).
findings.evidence: Read config.cpp 1532-1570 (snapshot read of the old file, skipped on mc), 1578-1618 (single openFileBuffer with O_TRUNC, closeFileBuffer), 1639-1658 (read-back rescue only for non-pfs with intended captured), 1667-1691 (restore if curLen < originalLen). util.cpp 647-672: writeFileBuffer counts totalQueued, records writeError on short writes and continues; util.h:32 documents totalQueued as total bytes handed to writeFileBuffer.

findings.title: fntLoadDefault never sets a char size on the new default face (updateAspectRatioLocked runs while the font is still a local)
findings.problem: loadSlotLocked ends in updateAspectRatioLocked, which only calls FT_Set_Char_Size on fonts_[i]; loadDefault loads into the local newFont and copies it into fonts_[FNT_DEFAULT] afterwards, so the new default face has no size until some later fntUpdateAspectRatio or fntLoadFile. fntInit loads the built-in font this way: the __OPLDIAG autolaunch screen (opl.cpp:1944-1952) draws FNT_DEFAULT straight after fntInit, and the boot splash draws its version and status lines (guisplash.cpp:102-107) before _loadConfig reaches applyConfig's guiUpdateScreenScale. With no size, FreeType 2.14 loads glyphs unscaled and drops FT_LOAD_RENDER, so those glyphs are cached as valid but have no bitmap.
findings.fix: Move the updateAspectRatioLocked() call out of loadSlotLocked: call it in loadDefault after the memcpy into fonts_[FNT_DEFAULT], and in loadFile after a successful loadSlotLocked.
findings.justification: It moves an existing call rather than adding logic, at the cost of one extra line: the call has to run once the new font is in fonts_, otherwise the default face is never sized. This is the smallest correct fix.
findings.benefit: Text drawn with the default font between fntInit and the first guiUpdateScreenScale is drawn at the right size instead of blank (the FreeType no-size behaviour is INFERRED from the 2.14.1 SDK version; the missing FT_Set_Char_Size is READ). Net +1 line.
findings.evidence: Read fntsys.cpp:393-412 (loadSlotLocked -> updateAspectRatioLocked), 489-511 (newFont is a local, memcpy after), 648-677 (loop over fonts_ only). grep FT_Set_Char_Size|FT_Set_Pixel_Sizes|FT_Request_Size over the repo: only fntsys.cpp:674. grep fntUpdateAspectRatio: only gui.cpp:458 (Gui::updateScreenScale), called from settingsio.cpp:2523 (applyConfig), opl.cpp:358, guisettings.cpp. Boot order opl.cpp:1676-1719: lngInit (lang.cpp:454 fntInit), thmInit (internal theme, no fntLoadFile since themePath NULL, themes.cpp:1575-1576), splash at 1717-1718, then _loadConfig. OPLDIAG path opl.cpp:1944-1952 renders right after fntInit. FreeType version 2.14.1 from the installed SDK freetype.h; the NO_SCALE/RENDER behaviour of FT_Load_Glyph is from FreeType source knowledge, not read here.

findings.title: texLoadJpgMemory has no size limit before jpeg_start_decompress: a large progressive JPG allocates MBs of RAM on the art thread
findings.problem: The PNG path refuses images over 1024 px before libpng allocates rows (png_set_user_limits, 1035). The JPG path has no bound. Downscaling to 1/8 does not help a progressive JPEG: libjpeg keeps the whole coefficient image in RAM (about 3 bytes per pixel at 4:2:0, 6 at 4:4:4), and the linked memory manager has no backing store. A 2000x2000 progressive cover or background (common for web downloads) therefore takes about 12 MB of heap on the art worker, next to its staged file buffer, while the GUI thread allocates in parallel.
findings.fix: Right after jpeg_read_header, refuse a progressive image above a pixel bound (for example about one megapixel). Or set info.mem->max_memory_to_use once after jpeg_create_decompress so that libjpeg fails with an error instead of allocating.
findings.justification: One line closes an unbounded allocation driven by untrusted art files. The PNG side already has the same guard for the same reason (YAOPL 07c868d comment at 1033-1034).
findings.benefit: Caps the JPG decoder's transient heap use. INFERRED: progressive 2000x2000 4:2:0 = 93,750 blocks x 128 B = 12 MB; 3000x3000 = 27 MB fails outright after a long attempt.
findings.evidence: Read texLoadJpgMemory 1172-1265: jpeg_read_header (1196), scale_denom loop (1208-1211), jpeg_start_decompress (1212), no check of image_width/image_height or progressive_mode before it. texStageExternalFileIntoMemory caps only the compressed file size (8 MB, 160). Symbol table raw/riptopl-nm-size-sorted.full.txt: jpeg_mem_available 0x38 and jpeg_get_large 0x8 (IJG jmemnobs-style manager, no backing store; INFERRED), jinit_d_coef_controller present. Progressive whole-image coefficient buffer size is libjpeg behaviour (INFERRED, not read in this repo).

findings.title: Legacy app records leave argv1 uninitialised, and the argv1 that dedup donates to them is never passed at launch
findings.problem: addAppsLegacyList mallocs each node and never sets app.argv1 (696-721), yet appDedupList reads appsList[dup].argv1[0] of the legacy survivor (378), which is uninitialised heap. Even when the scanned duplicate's argv1 is copied in, config() for a legacy row never sets CONFIG_ITEM_ALTSTARTUP from argv1 (1323-1342; only the scanned branch does, 1354). An app listed in both conf_apps.cfg and a title.cfg with argv1= is shown as the legacy row and starts without its argument, contrary to the comment at 355-356.
findings.fix: Set app->app.argv1[0] = '\0' in addAppsLegacyList. In config()'s legacy branch, set CONFIG_ITEM_ALTSTARTUP from appsList[id].argv1 when it is non-empty. If donation is not wanted, delete lines 378-381 instead.
findings.justification: Adds 2-3 lines. They remove an uninitialised read and make the documented argv1 donation actually reach the launch. Otherwise the argument from title.cfg is lost whenever the app is also in conf_apps.cfg.
findings.benefit: Deterministic dedup; launch argument kept for apps present in both channels (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read appsupport.cpp:349-389, 662-773, 1314-1367, include/appsupport.h:21-32. Grep '\.argv1|->argv1|argv1\[' over the repo: written only at appsupport.cpp:379-380 (donation) and 762-765 (scanned); read at 378 and 1354; launch reads only CONFIG_ITEM_ALTSTARTUP (1203).

findings.title: A save request abandoned by the 30 s deferred-IO timeout still runs later with lscstatus 0
findings.problem: When guiHandleDeferedIO gives up after OPL_DEFERRED_IO_TIMEOUT_MS it only clears lscstatus. The queued IO_CUSTOM_SIMPLEACTION request stays in the queue, so _saveConfig still runs when the worker reaches it. With lscstatus 0 it runs the rest of the save path anyway: the BDM re-resolve and retry (bdmResolveBootDir with its full budget); on a bare boot, the whole trySaveAlternateDevice sweep including bdmHDDIsPresent(5000); and on an APA boot with a staged home it mounts pfs1:, writes nothing and commits the HDD home selector, which strands the next boot on a home without the settings.
findings.fix: Return at the top of _saveConfig when lscstatus is 0.
findings.justification: The one-line guard closes a path where a stale request blocks the single IO worker for seconds and can commit an APA home selection without its settings. The comment at 2604-2608 states that the timeout happens in practice.
findings.benefit: Avoids seconds of wasted IO-worker time and a possible wrong-home commit after a timed-out save (INFERRED)
findings.evidence: Read guiwait.cpp:79-113 (on timeout *flag_=0 and gLastDeferredTimedOut=1; nothing dequeues the request), ioman.cpp:179-185 (handler just calls the function), gui.h:194 (OPL_DEFERRED_IO_TIMEOUT_MS = 30000). settingsio.cpp:2215-2463: no lscstatus==0 guard; 2306-2316 staged APA path commits through commitSelectedHddOplHome; 2435-2445 BDM retry; 2452-2454 trySaveAlternateDevice; 2003-2026 bdmHDDIsPresent(5000); 2140-2203 saveSelectedHddOplHome writes only requested sets. hddsupport.cpp:1234-1242, 1301-1324 selector state. That a stale request meets a pending selection is INFERRED.

findings.title: BgmPlayer::quiesce() signals and wakes semaphore/thread IDs it does not own when the player is not live
findings.problem: deinitEx()/deinit() call bgmQuiesce() on every launch and exit, and quiesce() does SignalSema(inSema_), SignalSema(outSema_), WakeupThread(threadId_) without checking live_. With BGM never started these IDs are 0; with BGM enabled but no usable bgm.ogg, start() created the objects and teardown() deleted them (759-764, 720-726), leaving stale IDs the kernel can hand to later CreateSema/CreateThread calls. A launch then signals or wakes another subsystem's object.
findings.fix: Return early from quiesce() when live_ is 0.
findings.justification: Two lines. The player must only touch kernel objects it created; the guard closes the stale-ID signal on the common BGM-on-without-music and BGM-off paths. stop() needs no change because all its callers already gate it on isBgmPlaying() or the running flags.
findings.benefit: Removes a spurious SignalSema x2 and WakeupThread on unowned IDs during every launch/exit teardown; consequence depends on ID reuse (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read bgm.cpp:645-734,741-764,820-881 and bgmplayer.h:35-40 (IDs default 0, live_ cleared only in teardown). grep bgmQuiesce: opl.cpp:1325 (deinitEx) and 1419 (deinit), both unconditional. grep bgmStop callers: selfupdate.cpp:423, guisettings.cpp:2741, sound.cpp:50, all guarded. INFERRED part: that the EE kernel reuses freed semaphore/thread IDs and that a reused one is live at launch.

findings.title: PADEMU poll issues ds34bt/ds34usb get_status SIF RPCs every frame for port 1 (and every multitap slot), which the menu never enables
findings.problem: readOne() runs for every opened pad on the GUI thread each frame (Gui::pollPads, gui.cpp:311) and calls ds34bt_get_status and ds34usb_get_status, each a synchronous SifCallRpc. padCount_ includes empty ports, so a normal console makes 4 RPCs per frame with no DS3/DS4 attached. system.cpp:431 loads both drivers with pad mask 1 and the IOP modules set enabled = (enable >> pad) & 1, so port 1 can never be RUNNING: its two RPCs per frame are always wasted. A multitap repeats port 0's calls once per slot.
findings.fix: Run the PADEMU block in readOne() and the loop body in pademuStopAll() only for pad->port == 0 && pad->slot == 0, the one pad system.cpp enables (note next to ds3pads that the two must change together).
findings.justification: The added condition removes half of the idle-case per-frame SIF RPC traffic from the GUI thread; the code itself documents synchronous SIF RPCs on the GUI thread stalling the menu under IOP load (sfx.cpp:264-267). One comparison is the smallest change that does it.
findings.benefit: 2 of 4 synchronous SIF RPCs per frame removed in the common case = about 120 RPC/s at 60 Hz off the GUI thread; more with a multitap (INFERRED from the call counts above, cost per RPC not measured).
findings.evidence: Read pad.cpp:446-483 and 664-679; libds34bt.c:72-83 and libds34usb.c:61-72 (get_status = SifCallRpc when inited); system.cpp:430-446 (ds3pads = 1, both IRX loaded and inited whenever SYS_LOAD_USB_MODULES, which reset() at opl.cpp:1214 always passes); ds34usb.c:940-959 and ds34bt.c:1675-1685 (enabled bit per pad from argv[1][0]); ds34bt.c:1559-1569 (RUNNING comes from the per-pad status). initialize() returns 1 on every path (pad.cpp:209,235,248,256,296) so start() counts empty ports. INFERRED: the IOP loader passes the 4-byte arg as argv[1] (same mechanism and comment 'only one pad enabled' as upstream OPL).

findings.title: httpclient's single RPC client, static buffers and one IOP stream are used by the IO-worker catalog fetch and the GUI-thread launch probe at once
findings.problem: httpclient.cpp has one SifRpcClient, one RpcTxBuffer/RpcRxBuffer and one streamBuffer, and the IOP keeps one live stream (httpclient.h:22-24). HttpSource::update fetches games.csv on the IO worker (httpsupport.cpp:596, via IO_MENU_UPDATE_DEFFERED), while HttpSource::launch runs httpProbeImage on the GUI thread (httpsupport.cpp:794) without blocking IO. menuitems.cpp:174-175 notes that source lists may refresh during the launch hold. A launch pressed while a refresh is in flight (start-up, or a view toggle that marks HTTP dirty) lets the two sessions overwrite each other's RPC arguments and stream. The probe then fails with the range error, or the refresh fails or keeps stale rows.
findings.fix: Serialize the probe against the worker the way HddSource does (hddsupport.cpp:2319-2333): ioBlockOps(1) before httpProbeImage in HttpSource::launch and ioBlockOps(0) right after it, including on its failure return.
findings.justification: Adds two calls. The race is between the only two users of a single-session RPC client and IOP stream. Blocking the IO queue around the probe reuses an existing pattern and is smaller than locking every Http* call and the Begin/Read/Close sessions in httpsupport.cpp.
findings.benefit: Removes an intermittent HTTP launch failure or corrupted refresh when launching during a catalog refresh; +2 lines (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read httpclient.cpp:1-161 (file-scope SifRpcClient, RpcTxBuffer, RpcRxBuffer; function-static streamBuffer; no lock) and modules/network/common/httpclient.h:22-24 (only one stream live). Callers via grep: httpsupport.cpp:266-357 (openRequest/fetchCatalog), :437 (httpTestServer), :596 (update), :681-692 (httpProbeRead), :794 (launch). update runs on the IO worker: opl.cpp:1691 registers menuDeferredUpdate for IO_MENU_UPDATE_DEFFERED. Launch path menuitems.cpp:140-192 has no ioBlockOps. HTTP refresh triggers: httpsupport.cpp:567 (init), :577 consumeDirty(HTTP_MODE). The exact corruption on overlap is INFERRED, not reproduced.

findings.title: vsIo seeks and transfers each 512-byte page separately even on images without ECC, doubling the I/O calls of every card-image access on the GUI thread
findings.problem: vsIo issues one lseek plus one read or write per page, ppc times per cluster. Without the ECC spare (raw == pageLen, the only kind that can be written, 238-241) a cluster's pages are contiguous, so one lseek and one transfer of csize bytes does the same. Every directory entry (vsEnt 316-329), FAT cluster (vsOpen 265, vsFlushFat 281) and data cluster (vsReadChain 366, vsWriteVmc 553 and 589) goes through it, synchronously from the VMC Saves dialog loop (guigame.cpp:435-474) on the GUI thread, which shows nothing while a copy runs.
findings.fix: In vsIo, when v->ecc is 0, do one lseek to abs * csize and one read or write of csize bytes; keep the per-page loop only for ECC images.
findings.justification: Adds one branch: it halves the lseek/read/write calls (each a fileXio RPC on the PS2, INFERRED) for standard 2-page clusters, which is the main cost of copying a large save while the UI is frozen; it adds no state.
findings.benefit: Calls per 1 KB cluster 4 -> 2: an 8 MB save export drops from ~32 K to ~16 K calls (INFERRED: 8192 clusters x 2 pages x 2 calls); listing and FAT loads halve too.
findings.evidence: Read vmcsaves.cpp 173-184, 198-273, 316-329, 358-374, 494-629: page p of cluster abs is at offset (abs*ppc+p)*raw, contiguous when raw == pageLen; ECC images are refused for writing at 238-241. Callers: guigame.cpp:377, 422, 439-467 call vmcSaves* inside the diaExecuteDialog loop at 435 (GUI thread). That each newlib call is one fileXio RPC, and its cost, is INFERRED, not measured.

findings.title: favWriteFile rewrites favourites.bin/recents.bin even when the new image is byte-identical (every relaunch of the last game, no-match removals)
findings.problem: One save on the GUI thread costs: the caller's favReadFile read, favPrepareSave's second read and parse of the same primary (528-545), a .new write plus read-back, a primary write plus read-back, and a .new delete (547-570). recentRecord (1486-1521), run before every launch by itemRecordRecent (menuitems.cpp:88-101) when Favourites, All Games or Last-played sort is on, always writes, even when the launched game is already first and the result is byte-identical; removeByIdAndText also writes when no record matched (1065-1076).
findings.fix: Pass the new image to favPrepareSave; when the complete primary it already loads is byte-identical (same size, memcmp equal), return success without writing. This covers the replay and no-match cases in one place.
findings.justification: Saves memory-card writes and launch delay on the commonest launch (replaying the last game) and on no-op removals; the check reuses the primary image favPrepareSave already reads, about 3 lines.
findings.benefit: Per skipped save: 2 card file writes, 2 read-backs and a .new create/delete avoided (INFERRED from 547-570); ~+3 lines.
findings.evidence: Read favPrepareSave 528-545 (favLoadImage + favParseImage of the primary), favWriteFile 547-570 (favWriteWhole + favImageMatches for .new and primary, then remove). recentRecord 1491-1516: out[0] is the new record, later records skip only matches, then favWriteFile unconditionally; identical bytes when recs[0] is the same game with the same id/icon/text ids. removeByIdAndText 1065-1074 calls favWriteFile even with survivors == count. Callers: menuitems.cpp:88-101 (launch path), 459-468 (R3); favsupport.cpp:442-449 comment confirms the GUI thread runs this off R3.

findings.title: Boot splash waits for the sample count read from a theme's sound/boot.adp header, unchecked: a non-ADPCM file holds the splash for hours
findings.problem: SoundEffects::load() sets duration_ms from the u32 at bytes 12-15 of a theme's boot.adp before, and regardless of, audsrv_load_adpcm, with no magic or range check. BootSplash::run() waits duration minus the fade before fading out, and that comparison is the loop's only exit. A WAV renamed to boot.adp has 'fmt ' there (544,501,094), giving 12,346,964 ms: the menu sits on the splash for about 3.4 hours at every boot while Boot Sound is on, until the user knows to hold START.
findings.fix: In load(), keep the header value only when audsrv_load_adpcm succeeded (else 0), and clamp duration_ms to a small bound such as 10 s, as THEME_HOLD_MAX_S already does for the theme hold.
findings.justification: The clamp is one comparison and closes a boot-time hang reachable from a user-supplied theme file; the success check reuses the existing return value.
findings.benefit: Removes an hours-long boot splash hang from a bad theme sound file (arithmetic: 544501094 / 44100 * 1000 = 12.3M ms); about 3 lines added.
findings.evidence: Read sfx.cpp:87-252 (theme sound dir used when present; SFX_BOOT read when bootSnd=1), guisplash.cpp:137-236 (fadeDelayMs clamped only below 0; line 142 comment: the comparison is the only exit; splash never polls pads), opl.cpp:1740-1748 and 1816-1827 (sfxInit(1) queued after _loadConfig). soundeffects.h:36-44 names boot.adp. INFERRED: the saved theme is active when deferredAudioInit runs (true for a card theme), and audsrv rejects or mis-plays a non-ADPCM file; neither changes the wait, which uses only the header.

findings.title: Cancel on a focused int/bool/enum row restores the value the page opened with, discarding an earlier confirmed edit of the same row
findings.problem: diaHandleInput's Cancel calls diaResetValue, which sets current = def; def is the value diaSetInt stored when the page opened (diaitems.cpp:105-106) and edits never update it. Sequence: set an IP octet 192 -> 10 and confirm, focus it again, press Up once, press Cancel: the row shows 192, not 10. Same for enums. Inherited Open PS2 Loader behaviour.
findings.fix: When Confirm gives a row focus (dia.cpp:1298-1301) remember cur->intvalue.current in a local, and on Cancel restore that value for UI_INT/UI_BOOL/UI_ENUM instead of def; def stays the page-open value diaHasChanges needs.
