findings.justification: Adds one local and one assignment: def cannot be reused because diaHasChanges (diaitems.cpp:59-80) depends on it meaning the page-open value, so the pre-edit value has to be kept somewhere; this is the smallest place.
findings.benefit: Cancel undoes only the current edit; about 3 lines added (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read dia.cpp:839-855 (diaResetValue uses def), :863-868 (Cancel path), :1298-1301 (focus taken), :919-934 (Up/Down change current only); diaitems.cpp:97-111 (diaSetInt sets def and current) and :55-80 (diaHasChanges compares to def, comment says Cancel restores def).

findings.title: Module storage end never checked against 0xD0000; RA work area is bounded only at 1 MB while IGR cheats use the 0xD0000 rule
findings.problem: The linkfile reserves 0x97000-0xD0000 (228 KB) for modules and says 0xD0000+ is used by some games. The IGR cheats code respects that, but nothing checks the modules from sendIrxKernelRAM or the RA work area placed after them, and raWorkBytes caps its card packet at 0x100000. In an RA edition, an SMB2 game with VMC, BT pad emulation, MMCEIGR and telemetry already needs ~220 KB of IRX, and RA_EE_WORK_BYTES (about 13 KB plus 4 bytes per watch) then ends above 0xD0000. A game that writes that range overwrites the RA buffers or the module images ee_core reloads on an in-game IOP reset.
findings.fix: Use one rule: cap the RA work area at 0xD0000 like the cheats. Use 0xD0000 as the low-memory limit in raWorkBytes, and in sysLaunchLoaderElf drop the reservation (telemetry off for that launch, logged) when modules plus list would end above it.
findings.justification: Adds one comparison, the same one the cheats block makes ten lines later. The alternative is RAM the linkfile documents as game-used holding live buffers and IRX images.
findings.benefit: Prevents in-game corruption for RA launches whose storage ends past 0xD0000 (INFERRED: IRX sizes from evidence/RiptOPL/raw/irx-modules.tsv sum to ~219.6 KB; room to 0xD0000 is 233,472 B)
findings.evidence: ee_core/linkfile:19-20; iosupport.h:108 OPL_MOD_STORAGE 0x97000; system.cpp:1450-1462 cheats use top 0xD0000 (or IGROVL_BASE); system.cpp:1443-1447 RA area appended unbounded; host.cpp:140 limit 0x00100000; ra_snap.h:79 RA_EE_WORK_BYTES = RA_SNAP_TOTAL + count*4 + nodes*20; ra_watch.h:49 9 parts of ~1.4 KB. Sum from irx-modules.tsv: udnl 5889, IOPRP ~64075 (IOPRP_img 248 + smb2_cdvdman 55605 + cdvdfsv 7309 + eesync 913, INFERRED), imgdrv 1257, resetspu 1241, usbd 21333, sio2man 5241, smap_ingame 7841, SMSTCPIP 45101, smbinit 10049, raudp 12161, mmceigr 1385, smb_mcemu 11309, mmcedrv 11329, bt_pademu 21373 = 219,584. No game that breaks was identified.

findings.title: AppSource::rename can drop the app's config: legacy branch removes the key via a pointer into the freed node and before validating newName
findings.problem: Legacy branch: configRemoveKey(configApps, cur->key) frees cur at config.cpp:464 and the loop keeps comparing later nodes against that key, a read after free on every legacy rename. Then configSetStr(newName) fails when the name is empty or contains '=' (configKeyValidate, config.cpp:221-227; '=' is on the on-screen keyboard), and configWrite saves conf_apps.cfg without the app, so it disappears. Scanned branch: the configRead result is ignored, so after a failed read configWrite rewrites title.cfg with only title=, which loses boot= and argv1=. The app then drops out of the list because appScanCallback needs boot.
findings.fix: Legacy branch: return early when newName is empty or contains '='. Copy cur->key into a local buffer and pass that copy to configRemoveKey. Scanned branch: call configSetStr/configWrite only when configRead succeeded.
findings.justification: Adds about 4 lines. They close a use-after-free and two ways a rename silently deletes the user's app entry or title.cfg, and they are the smallest checks that do so.
findings.benefit: No freed-memory read per legacy rename; no lost conf_apps.cfg entry or title.cfg keys on rename (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read appsupport.cpp:936-969, config.cpp:221-227 (empty or '=' key rejected), 363-386 (setStr returns 0 on invalid key), 447-477 (removeKey frees the match and keeps looping with key), 1419-1434 (configRead returns 0 on failure). Caller menusys.cpp:302-319 passes keyboard text (max CONFIG_KEY_NAME_LEN=48). diaeditors.cpp:149 keyboard row contains '='. Grep 'configRemoveKey(.*->key)' over src: only appsupport.cpp:950.

findings.title: VMC Saves actions and Load from disc block the UI thread for seconds with no wait screen
findings.problem: Export, Export as PSU, Import and Delete in guiGameShowVMCSaves call vmcSaves* directly on the menu thread; these read and write the card image one 512-byte page per lseek+read/write (vmcsaves.cpp:173-184), so a large save takes seconds. Load from disc calls sysGetDiscID, which waits for disc detection, sceCdDiskReady and a standby spin-up (system.cpp:498-535). Neither draws anything first, so the dialog's last frame stays frozen until the call returns.
findings.fix: Call guiRenderTextScreen(_l(_STR_PLEASE_WAIT)) right before each blocking call, as fmUnpackPsu already does (guifilemgr.cpp:558).
findings.justification: Four one-line calls to an existing helper turn a frozen screen of several seconds into a visible wait message; moving the work to the IO thread would be far more code.
findings.benefit: No frozen frame during multi-second card-image or disc I/O; durations INFERRED from page-at-a-time image I/O and CD spin-up, not measured
findings.evidence: guiGameShowVMCSaves (guigame.cpp:413-475) is reached from guiGameShowVMCConfig:635, from guiGameShowVMCMenu, called by menusys.cpp:3229 (menu thread). guiGameShowCompatConfig is called by menusys.cpp:3219. No guiRenderTextScreen or other draw between diaExecuteDialog's return and the vmcSaves*/sysGetDiscID calls (read 435-474, 1810-1830). vmcsaves.cpp:173-184 page loop read; system.cpp:494-545 read. Freeze length INFERRED.

findings.title: RA unlock pulse forces PMODE to circuit 1 only and leaves it there
findings.problem: For 60 frames the pulse writes PMODE with EN1=1, EN2=0, SLBG=1, and on the last frame writes RA_OVL_PMODE(0xFF), relying on the game rewriting PMODE on its next flip (ra_pulse.c:112-115). A game that shows its picture through read circuit 2 only shows circuit 1 during the pulse, and one that writes PMODE only at start-up stays on circuit 1 afterwards. The card path (ra_overlay.c:185-210) already treats circuit 2 as a normal case and reads the tracked PMODE.
findings.fix: When the GS tracker is on (GSM, cards or In-Game Menu, main.c:127-152), save GSMSourceGSRegs.pmode when the pulse starts and write that value back on the last frame instead of RA_OVL_PMODE(0xFF); skip the pulse's PMODE writes when the saved value has EN1 clear. Keep the current behaviour when nothing was tracked.
findings.justification: Adds one saved word and two conditions; without them an unlock can leave a circuit-2 game, or one that sets PMODE once, on the wrong display circuit.
findings.benefit: Avoids a wrong or black display after an unlock notice in RA builds for such games (INFERRED, not tested on hardware)
findings.evidence: Read ra_pulse.c fully; RA_PulseOnVblank is the default notice (ra_overlay.c:377-380: used whenever raClientMode is 0, cards are compiled out or no card buffer). GSMSourceGSRegs (gsm_engine.S:56-57, igs_api.h:126) records PMODE/DISPFB/DISPLAY; ra_overlay.c:185-210 and igrmenu.c:584 read it. main.c:142-152 enables the tracker for cards or In-Game Menu. INFERRED part: how many games use circuit 2 only or write PMODE once; no hardware test.

findings.title: VMC Saves lists and File Manager selection arrays hold about 30 KB of .bss for the whole run
findings.problem: vmcSavesCard[64], vmcSavesFolder[64] (166-byte vmc_save_t each), vmcSavesFolderLabels and the two item arrays are file-scope statics used only while guiGameShowVMCSaves runs, and fmToClipboard and fmDeleteSelection each keep their own static int sel[512] although both only run inside guiShowFileManager. Together they pin 30,792 bytes of EE RAM from boot to exit for two rarely opened modal dialogs.
findings.fix: Allocate the VMC Saves arrays at the top of guiGameShowVMCSaves and free them on return. In the File Manager, drop both static sel arrays and allocate one selection buffer with the other FM buffers in guiShowFileManager (or put sel on the 128 KB main stack).
findings.justification: The fix adds one malloc/free pair per dialog. It returns 30 KB of permanently reserved RAM, and the File Manager already allocates its larger buffers this way (guifilemgr.cpp:618-621), so no new pattern is introduced.

findings.title: rabadge refresh stats two files per list row on every rebuild, including an smb0: share probe, on the single I/O worker
findings.problem: For each row, watchListExists() stats <prefix>RA/<serial>.wl and, when that is missing, smb0:RA/<serial>.wl. A rebuild of an N-game USB list therefore costs up to 2N fileXio round trips, and N of them go over the network when an SMB share is mounted, even when neither RA directory exists. This runs inside updateMenuFromGameList on the I/O worker that also serves cover art (opl.cpp:745-747), so every list rebuild delays art by that many round trips.
findings.fix: In refresh(), stat the two directories (<prefix>RA and smb0:RA) once before the loop and skip the per-row probe for a side whose directory is missing; keep the per-row stats only where the directory exists (favourites keep the current path).
findings.justification: Adds about 6 lines. The concrete problem is up to 2N stat round trips per list rebuild on the shared I/O thread; one directory stat per side removes all of them for devices never checked and for setups without smb0:RA, which is the simplest change that keeps the loader's lookup order.
findings.benefit: INFERRED: a 500-game USB list with no RA folders goes from up to 1,000 stat RPCs (500 over SMB if mounted) to 2 per rebuild; at roughly 1-3 ms per SMB stat that is about 0.5-1.5 s less I/O-thread time per rebuild (timing not measured).
findings.evidence: Read rabadge.cpp:118-199. Call path: menu update -> updateMenuFromGameList (opl.cpp:690) -> raBadgeRefresh (opl.cpp:747), run only when needsUpdate is true (opl.cpp:870-871) on the I/O worker (comment opl.cpp:745-746). Same worker serves cover art (opl.cpp:964-972, 1032-1038 describe the contention). Per-row stat at :127 and smb0: fallback at :132-136 for every row without a local list. Timing per stat is INFERRED, not measured.

findings.title: PS2 logo and ZSO-on-HDD reads issue one fileXio devctl per 512-byte sector
findings.problem: CheckPS2Logo's HDD branch reads the 24 KB logo area with 48 hddReadSectors(lba + k, 1, ...) calls, and zso.c ReadHDDSectors reads every 2048-byte ISO sector as four single-sector calls. hddReadSectors takes a sector count (hdd.cpp:101-112) and rahash.cpp already reads 16 sectors (8 KB) per call to amortise the EE/IOP round trip. Runs on the launch path of HDD games (hddsupport.cpp:2790-2799).
findings.fix: Read in chunks of up to 16 HDD sectors per hddReadSectors call, as rahash.cpp does: 3 calls for the logo instead of 48, one call per ISO sector in ReadHDDSectors instead of four.
findings.benefit: 48 -> 3 fileXio RPCs for the HDD logo check and 4x fewer for menu-side ZSO-on-HDD reads; a few tens of ms per HDD launch (INFERRED, not measured); ~4 lines shorter.
findings.evidence: Read util.cpp:799-806, zso.c:14-23, hdd.cpp:101-112 (fileXioDevctl HDIOC_READSECTOR with nsectors*512 output), modules/hdd/apa/src/hdd_fio.c:1176-1179 (blkIoDmaTransfer of the requested count). rahash.cpp:340-344,376 uses HDL_READ_SECTORS=4 ISO sectors (16 HDD sectors, 8 KB) per call. Callers: hddsupport.cpp:2790 (CheckPS2Logo), :2796-2799 (ZSO probe). The per-call size limit of fileXio devctl was not verified in this repo, so 8 KB (proven by rahash) is the chunk proposed.

findings.title: Screenshot() asks DMA channel 1 for 8192 qwords when the frame is under 128 KB, then divides by slices == 0
findings.problem: slices = qwords >> 13 is 0 for any frame below 131072 bytes (for example 256x240 PSMCT16 = 122880 B, or the 64x64 minimum that the range checks at 193-197 accept). The do-while still runs once with QWC = 8192 + 0, so the channel waits for more data than the BITBLT sends and would write up to 128 KB past the buffer, and line 304 then evaluates 255 * i / slices with slices 0 (GCC MIPS traps on integer division by zero by default).
findings.fix: Loop over the remaining qword count, sending min(remaining, 8192) per pass, and drop the slices/remainder arithmetic and the fade division with it.
findings.benefit: Fixes a hang with interrupts disabled (DI at 683) on small frames; the loop gets ~4 lines shorter (INFERRED: over-long VIF1 read never completing is hardware behaviour not tested here).
findings.evidence: Read igs_api.c 168-329 and 680-738: width = FBW*64, image_size = width*height*pixel_size, qwords = image_size >> 4, slices = qwords >> 13, remainder only added when slices > 0 (279-280, 289). With slices 0 the single pass sets QWC 8192 at 289 and waits at 300-301 before reaching the division at 304. eecore cflags in ps2.yaml:604-613 do not pass -mno-check-zero-division. Small frames on PS2 are rare, hence rank 1.

findings.title: ps2cnf CNFGetKey: unreachable EOF branch, and no terminator for a 64-character BOOT2 path
findings.problem: The loop condition already stops at '\0', so the '*line == '\0'' branch at 62-64 can never run (its own comment admits it duplicates the earlier check). When the token fills all CNF_PATH_LEN_MAX (64) bytes the loop exits without writing a terminator, and GetStartupExecName then scans its 64-byte ps2disc_boot for ':' or '\0' past the end. Only a malformed SYSTEM.CNF with a 64+ char BOOT2 value triggers it.
findings.fix: Loop to CNF_PATH_LEN_MAX - 1, delete the unreachable branch, and always write the terminator after the loop.
findings.benefit: 3 lines removed and an out-of-bounds read on a malformed disc closed (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read ps2cnf.cpp:42-68 and the only caller supportbase.cpp:114-130 (grep ps2cnfGetBootFile: supportbase.cpp:120 only); ps2disc_boot is char[CNF_PATH_LEN_MAX] = "" (zero-filled), so only the 64-byte case lacks a NUL.

findings.title: saveIconDraw keeps a redundant per-vertex colour array siCol
findings.problem: Each frame siShade fills siCol in model order and the sort pass copies it into siDrawCol. The model is a plain (non-indexed) triangle list, so every vertex is copied exactly once and the shade could be computed straight into siDrawCol[dst]. siCol is an extra 8-byte-per-vertex buffer held, like the other work buffers, until saveIconReset (only called when the setting is switched off, guisettings.cpp:1795).
findings.fix: Delete siCol: compute siShade for src directly into siDrawCol[dst] in the sorted copy loop and drop its malloc, free and NULL checks.
findings.benefit: Up to 48,000 bytes less heap held (INFERRED: SAVEICON_MAX_VERTS 6000 x sizeof(u64)); one array and one store/load per vertex per frame removed; ~3 lines.
findings.evidence: Read saveicon.cpp:810-813 (buffer declarations), :1136-1175 (siFreeBuffers/siEnsureBuffers: siCol malloc'd at :1165), :1265-1284 (siCol filled per vertex), :1300-1311 (siDrawCol[dst] = siCol[src], each src used once since a = siOrder[i]*3 covers each triangle once). grep -n siCol saveicon.cpp: only 812, 1144, 1148, 1165, 1169, 1282, 1309. saveIconReset callers: guisettings.cpp:1795 only.

findings.title: retrogemGetDiscImageGameID retries a .VCD at offset 0 (raw and cooked) after the 1 MiB-offset read fails; both retries cannot match
findings.problem: For isVcd, when the 0x100000-offset layout finds no serial (no SYSTEM.CNF, as on PSX.EXE titles, a non-serial BOOT, or a read error), the function goes on to reopen the file twice and probe offset 0 as raw and as cooked. Offset 0 of a POPStarter VCD is its 1 MiB header, not disc sector 0, so neither probe can reach the disc PVD. The cooked probe reads up to 16 sectors. On the IO worker, resolveRowId repeats a failed resolve up to 4 times per row (VCD_ID_MAX_RETRIES 3, vcdsupport.cpp:264). The launch path repeats it again on the main thread.
findings.fix: Delete the offset-0 fallbacks for VCDs: make retrogemGetVcdGameID return retrogemTryImageLayout(path, PS1_VCD_IMAGE_OFFSET, PS1_IMAGE_RAW_2352, ...) directly, and drop the isVcd parameter from retrogemGetDiscImageGameID.
findings.benefit: Per failed VCD resolve: 2 fopen/fclose and up to 17 sector reads (1 raw + 16 cooked x 2048 B) avoided, times up to 4 attempts per row per session plus 1 at launch (INFERRED from the code, not measured). About 2 lines removed.
findings.evidence: Read retrogem.cpp:177-232 (read-sector/PVD scan: raw layout fails on the first sector whose mode byte is not 1/2; cooked scans LBA 16-31), 390-407, 558-604. Callers via grep retrogem: vcdsupport.cpp:449 (resolveRowId, IO worker per its comment at 411-412; retry logic 467-470, VCD_ID_MAX_RETRIES=3 at 264), vcdsupport.cpp:3034 (vcdPrepareRetroGemBarcode, called from the launch legs before deinit: bdmlaunch.cpp:247, ethsupport.cpp:1041, mmcesupport.cpp:1283, hddsupport.cpp:2294, udpfssupport.cpp:823), and retrogem.cpp:589-590 (.VCD extension). Every isVcd caller passes a .VCD path. The claim that the 1 MiB VCD header never holds an ISO9660 PVD at offset 16x2352 or 16x2048 is INFERRED from the POPStarter VCD layout that PS1_VCD_IMAGE_OFFSET encodes. The header contents were not inspected.

findings.title: Boot runs PadManager::start() twice: init() discards the first startPads() result and its retry loop always calls it again
findings.problem: opl.cpp:1686 calls startPads() and ignores the result; padStatus is still 0 (opl.cpp:1668), so the loop at 1701 calls startPads() again at once. start() has no guard against re-entry: it re-issues padPortOpen on ports that are already open and runs initialize() again for every pad, which resends padSetMainMode(LOCK), padEnterPressMode and padSetActAlign with up to seven 25 ms bounded waits per DualShock, on the main thread before the first menu frame.

findings.title: apply_capcom_protection_patch passes the opcode value to SyncDCache; the flush is not needed

The flush is also unnecessary: smem_write comes from ps2sdk libkernel smem.o (pulled in by patches.o, evidence/RiptOPL/raw/eecore-archive-members.txt:20) and copies with CPU stores through the IOP memory window, so the source never has to be written back to RAM.

INFERRED part: ps2sdk smem_write being a CPU copy through 0xBC000000 and SyncDCache's handling of start > end are SDK internals not in this repo.

findings.title: VMC Saves re-reads both the card image and the SAVES folder after every button, even a declined delete

findings.title: guiAlignSubMenuHints measures a missing glyph as 20+2 px but guiDrawIconAndText draws it as 0 px
findings.problem: For a NULL glyph texture (a use_default=0 theme without circle.png/cross.png, the case the comment at :68-69 names) the measure uses w = 20 and subtracts rmWideScale(20)+2, while the drawer uses w = 0 and does not advance x. Right-aligned hint rows (dia.cpp:795, guioverlay.cpp:78, guisettings.cpp:3155) then end about 22 px short of their margin per missing glyph and centred rows (guisettings.cpp:3126, themeelems.cpp:2338) sit about 11 px off.
findings.fix: Use 0 width and skip the +2 gap for a NULL texture in guiAlignSubMenuHints, matching guiDrawIconAndText.
findings.benefit: Hint rows line up when a theme lacks a glyph; no size change
findings.evidence: uidraw.cpp:70 'w = iconTex ? ... : 20' then :73 'x -= rmWideScale(w) + 2'; uidraw.cpp:15-29 starts with w = 0 and only advances x by rmWideScale(w) + 2 when iconTex && iconTex->Mem. thmGetTexture returns NULL whenever Mem is NULL (themes.cpp:938-951). Callers pairing the two: dia.cpp:795/815-820, guioverlay.cpp:78-83, guisettings.cpp:3126-3132 and 3155-3160, gui.cpp:413-414, themeelems.cpp:2338-2344.

findings.title: netTestLink uses an absolute clock() deadline and an overflowing millisecond product, unlike the wrap-safe form used elsewhere in the file
findings.problem: deadline = t0 + 3 * CLOCKS_PER_SEC and the test clock() < deadline break when the 32-bit microsecond clock wraps (about every 71.6 min): if t0 is within 3 s of the wrap the loop never runs and the link test reports no answer. ms = (clock() - t0) * 1000 / CLOCKS_PER_SEC overflows once the elapsed time passes 4.29 s, which a last ask() started near the deadline can reach. The same file and its test say clock() is a 32-bit microsecond counter and use the elapsed form for httpGet.
findings.fix: Loop while (clock_t)(clock() - t0) < 3000 * (CLOCKS_PER_SEC / 1000), as httpGet does, and compute ms as (clock() - t0) / (CLOCKS_PER_SEC / 1000).
findings.benefit: Removes a false 'no answer' in the link test around each clock wrap and a wrong round-trip figure; no size change (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read ranet.cpp:851-936. Clock width stated by the repo: ranet.cpp:1064-1065, nettime.cpp:72, ratls_ps2.cpp:167-168, and .github/scripts/test_ra_xerabora_browser.py:464-468 ('clock() is a 32-bit microsecond counter on the EE ... an absolute deadline breaks at the wrap'). ask() can take up to RA_TRY 12 x 10 polls x RA_POLL_MS 25 ms = 3 s per call (ranet.cpp:113-114, 322-348), so elapsed can exceed 4.29 s. Caller: supportbase.cpp:3152.

findings.title: sysDeleteFolder leaks its file list when a subfolder delete fails, and sprintf's to an unchecked malloc
findings.problem: The collected DirentToDelete list (nodes and filenames) is freed only inside the result >= 0 branch, so when a recursive sysDeleteFolder of a subfolder fails (r < 0 at 879-880) every node of the parent's list is leaked. The path buffer at 873 is used by sprintf without a NULL check. Reached from AppSource::deleteGame (appsupport.cpp:930) when the user deletes an app folder.
findings.fix: Always walk and free the list; only skip the unlink calls when result < 0. Check the malloc at 873 before the sprintf.
findings.justification: The NULL check stops a NULL write on allocation failure; the leak fix only moves the existing free loop.
findings.benefit: A few bytes per file leaked per failed app delete, plus one NULL-pointer write path removed; tiny.
findings.evidence: Read util.cpp:857-936. grep -rn sysDeleteFolder over the repo: definition util.cpp:857, recursion :878, prototype util.h:63, only external caller appsupport.cpp:930 (deleteGame for non-legacy apps).

findings.title: sysLaunchLoaderElf sprintf's unvalidated int ps2_ip[] with %d into char g_ps2_ip[16]
findings.problem: For UDPBD/UDPFS launches, line 1580 formats int ps2_ip[4] with %d into g_ps2_ip[16]. The values come from sscanf("%d") of conf_network.cfg or IPCONFIG.DAT with no range check, so an octet over 255 or a negative one ("192.168.100.1000") writes past the field. The worst case is 47 chars + NUL, which stays inside ip+netmask+gateway, and the next two sprintfs rewrite those. ee_core is still left with an unterminated IP that runs into the netmask string.
findings.fix: Use snprintf(config->g_ps2_ip, sizeof(config->g_ps2_ip), ...) with (u8) casts and %u, as line 1577 already formats the DHCP address.
findings.benefit: Closes a small out-of-field write from config-file input (READ; effect limited to a wrong in-game IP)
findings.evidence: coreconfig.h:43-45: char g_ps2_ip[16], g_ps2_netmask[16], g_ps2_gateway[16] in that order. opl.cpp:162 int ps2_ip[4]. Writers: settingsio.cpp:1950 and config.cpp:752 (sscanf %d, no clamp), guisettings.cpp:979 (dialog int). system.cpp:1579-1580 runs when sysModeIsNetBlock(mode_str) (BDM_UDP_MODE, BDM_UFS_MODE, UDPFS_MODE).

findings.title: texStageExternalFileIntoMemory reads up to 8 MB before refusing a file whose size it already knows is too big
findings.problem: When lseek reports a size over TEX_STAGE_MAX_SIZE, or malloc(size) fails, the fast path falls through to the chunked loop. The loop then reads about 8 MB in 32 KB reads and grows its buffer to 8 MB by realloc (4 MB + 8 MB live at once) before it refuses with ERR_BAD_FILE. The size probe had already given the answer. This is reachable for any oversized art or theme PNG on mass/pfs/smb (texLoadAll staged arm, texLoadJpgFile).
findings.fix: When the size probe succeeded, do not enter the loop: return ERR_BAD_FILE for size > TEX_STAGE_MAX_SIZE and ERR_FILE_IO when malloc(size) fails. Keep the loop for MMCE (shortReadIsEof), where lseek is not available.
findings.benefit: Avoids an 8 MB read (about 8 s on USB 1.1, INFERRED) and a 12 MB realloc peak for an oversized file; rare trigger.
findings.evidence: Read textures.cpp 623-731: fast path 639-659 (size > cap -> else-if seeks back and falls to the loop; malloc NULL -> falls to the loop), loop 668-721 grows by doubling from 64 KB and refuses only when capacity >= TEX_STAGE_MAX_SIZE (684-689). Callers: texLoadAll 966 (mass/mmce) and texLoadJpgFile 1281 (all devices).

findings.title: thmLoadResource takes a psm parameter it never uses
findings.problem: The body (1063-1073) never reads psm; all 11 call sites pass GS_PSM_CT32.
findings.fix: Delete the psm parameter and the GS_PSM_CT32 argument at every call site.
findings.benefit: No line change; one register argument less per call (INFERRED, a few bytes).
findings.evidence: thmLoadResource is static; grep -n thmLoadResource themes.cpp: definition 1061 and calls 1261, 1703, 1717, 1721, 1733, 1745, 1749, 1750, 1797, 1801, 1811; no match in .github/scripts or tests.

findings.title: utf8.h: the 400-byte static utf8d table is linked twice (fntsys.cpp and textshape.cpp)
findings.problem: utf8.h defines utf8d as a static const array and utf8Decode as a static function, so each including translation unit gets its own copy. The shipped ELF holds two 400-byte _ZL5utf8d objects.
findings.fix: Define the table and utf8Decode once (for example in fntsys.cpp) and leave only a prototype in utf8.h, or make both inline (inline constexpr table) so the linker keeps one copy.
findings.benefit: 400 B .rodata. MEASURED: two _ZL5utf8d entries of size 0x190 in evidence/RiptOPL/raw/riptopl-nm-size-sorted.full.txt:1757-1758.
findings.evidence: grep 'include.*utf8.h|utf8Decode' over src/RiptOPL (c,cpp,h,py): included only by src/gfx/fntsys.cpp:12 and src/gfx/textshape.cpp:12, both compiled into the main ELF (ps2.yaml src/gfx glob per brief). nm shows 005dc7d0 and 005dceb8, each 00000190 r _ZL5utf8d.

findings.title: AttributeImage (built-in theme) and BdmIndex look up the internal texture id by name every frame
findings.problem: On the built-in theme, drawAttributeImage calls thmAttributeTexId every frame (snprintf for 'value/asset' values, then texLookupInternalTexId, a linear strcmp over the ~129 internal texture names) although the value only changes when currentConfigId changes. The built-in info page has 7 AttributeImage elements, so the GUI thread repeats up to 7 snprintf plus about 900 strcmp per frame for an unchanged result; drawBDMIndex does one snprintf plus the same scan per frame on the main page.
findings.fix: In drawAttributeImage resolve the texId once inside the existing currentConfigId != config->uid() block and keep it in the element (currentCacheId is unused on the built-in branch), then draw from the stored id. Leave drawBDMIndex as it is unless the same edit is made there for free.
findings.justification: No new state is needed for AttributeImage: the uid-gated refresh block already exists and currentCacheId is idle on that branch, so the per-frame work is removed by moving one call.
findings.benefit: About 7 x 129 strcmp + up to 7 snprintf per frame removed on the built-in info page, roughly 50 us per frame at 294 MHz (INFERRED: ~15 cycles per mismatching strcmp).
findings.evidence: Read drawAttributeImage 1517-1577: config uid gate 1525-1533, per-frame thmGetTexture(thmAttributeTexId()) at 1536 on the built-in path; thmAttributeTexId 1506-1515; textures.cpp:349-362 linear strcmp over TEXTURES_COUNT; include/textures.h enum has ~129 entries (counted with awk). misc/conf_theme_OPL.cfg:238-286 has 7 AttributeImage attributes (#Media, #Format, Vmode, Aspect, Scan, Players, Rating). drawBDMIndex 1917-1925 snprintf + lookup per frame. Timing is an estimate, not measured.

findings.title: BdmSource::config retries mkdir of <home>/CFG on every row settle once the folder exists
findings.problem: On a read-only UDPBD/UDPFS page, config() remembers the CFG folder in madeCfgDir only when mkdir returns 0. From the second boot on the folder already exists, mkdir fails, nothing is latched, and the mkdir is issued again on every config() call. _menuLoadConfigAsync calls config() each time the cursor settles on a row (menusys.cpp 587-606), so each settle costs one extra mkdir RPC on the settings home, usually the memory card.
findings.fix: Also latch madeCfgDir when mkdir fails because the folder already exists (errno EEXIST), so the one-mkdir-per-folder intent in the comment holds across boots.
findings.benefit: One fileXio mkdir RPC (memory card or USB) less per row settle on read-only network pages (INFERRED; EEXIST mapping of the mc/mass drivers not verified)
findings.evidence: Read bdmsupport.cpp 2042-2073: madeCfgDir is written only inside 'if (mkdir(dir, 0777) == 0)'. Grep '->config(' over src/: menusys.cpp 571 (_menuLoadConfig), 606 (_menuLoadConfigAsync, browse-time settle), 659 (#Size), guigame.cpp 258, cfgtitle.cpp 227, favsupport.cpp 1287. MODE_FLAG_READ_ONLY is set only for UDPBD-type slots (bdmdevices.cpp 299-303, 398-402). INFERRED: mkdir on an existing folder returns -1 on the PS2 newlib port for mc and mass.

findings.title: EE_RESET_SUFFIX_BYTES is 7 but ResetIopSpecial writes 8 bytes after the payload (latent one-byte stack overflow of command[])
findings.problem: ResetIopSpecial accepts arglen up to sizeof(command) - 7, then writes the NUL at command[arglen] and _strcpy's "host0:" with its terminator (util.c:24-27 copies strlen+1) to command[arglen+1..arglen+7], so arglen = sizeof(command)-7 writes command[sizeof(command)], one past the stack array. eeResetPayloadLength repeats the same 7 for commandCapacity, and the test pins it ((19,80,16) == 9 means 9+8 = 17 bytes into 16). Not reachable today: the only caller passes packetCapacity = sizeof(SifCmdResetData_t.arg), which caps the payload at 70 for an 80-byte arg (INFERRED SDK size), below the 73 the guard allows.
findings.fix: Set EE_RESET_SUFFIX_BYTES to 8 and fix its comment (NUL, "host0:" and its NUL). Change the test's (19,80,16) case to expect -1 and (20,80,16) stays -1.
findings.benefit: Corrects a latent off-by-one in the reset-command bound; no size change (INFERRED)
findings.evidence: Read reset_arg_bounds.h:1-21, iopmgr.c:74-96 (char command[RESET_ARG_MAX + 1]; guard arglen > sizeof(command) - EE_RESET_SUFFIX_BYTES; command[arglen]=0; _strcpy(&command[arglen+1], "host0:")), util.c:24-27 (_strcpy copies the terminator), iopmgr.c:436-439 (only caller with args). grep eeResetPayloadLength/EE_RESET_*: iopmgr.c and test_reset_arg_bounds.py only. Unreachability INFERRED from RESET_ARG_MAX 79 and arg[RESET_ARG_MAX + 1] as stubbed in test_reset_failure_lifecycle.py:31-32; the real SDK header was not read.

findings.title: Launch Disc waits use absolute clock()+budget deadlines that break at the 32-bit clock wrap
findings.problem: sysDiscSettle and the NODISC re-detect compute deadline = clock() + budget and loop while clock() < deadline. The repo itself says clock() is a 32-bit microsecond counter (ratls_ps2.cpp:167, nettime.cpp:72) and that only the elapsed form (clock() - start) survives the wrap (guiwait.cpp:97-98). If Launch Disc is chosen in the last 1-4 s before a wrap (every ~71.6 min), the deadline overflows, every wait ends at once, and a disc that is still identifying or spun down is reported as 'disc launch error'.
findings.fix: Keep a start tick and compare elapsed time, as guiwait.cpp:99-103 does: (clock() - start) < budgetTicks for the three tests. Same line count.
findings.benefit: Removes a rare spurious Launch Disc failure (about 4 s in every 71.6 min of uptime, about 0.1% of launches; INFERRED). No size change.
findings.evidence: Read sysdisc.cpp:132-145 and 168-207. Repo statements on clock(): ratls_ps2.cpp:167-172 and nettime.cpp:72-75 ('32-bit microsecond counter ... compare elapsed time, which survives the wrap'), guiwait.cpp:97-103 ('unlike an absolute clock()+limit deadline'). Every other timed wait found by grep 'clock() - ' (guinotify.cpp:89,148, guisettings.cpp:1388, menusys.cpp:2755, ranet.cpp:1110) uses the elapsed form. INFERRED: clock_t width and CLOCKS_PER_SEC come from those comments; the ps2sdk header is not in this repo. Reachable: menusys.cpp:2365 (GUI thread) and discsupport.cpp:50 call sysGetDiscBootPath.

findings.title: Share picker in EthSource::update treats ERROR_ETH_LINK_FAIL/DHCP_FAIL as listable and replaces the link error with a share-list error
findings.problem: With no share name set, update() only skips the GETSHARELIST devctl when gNetworkStartup < ERROR_ETH_SMB_OPENSHARE (303). ERROR_ETH_LINK_FAIL (310) and ERROR_ETH_DHCP_FAIL (311), set by netApplyConfig on a pulled cable or failed DHCP (netsupport.cpp:119-143), pass the gate, the devctl fails on the unconnected driver and 864-865 overwrite the status and message with ERROR_ETH_SMB_LISTSHARES.
findings.fix: Also return early when gNetworkStartup is above ERROR_ETH_SMB_LISTGAMES (the link/DHCP codes), so only the open-share and list errors retry the listing.
findings.benefit: Correct error message and no pointless SMB RPC after a link or DHCP failure on the share-picker page; one condition changed, 0 lines.
findings.evidence: Enum values read at iosupport.h:41-60 (CONN 300 .. LISTGAMES 305, LINK_FAIL 310, DHCP_FAIL 311). grep ERROR_ETH_LINK_FAIL/DHCP_FAIL: set only in netsupport.cpp:119-143. initSmb (ethsupport.cpp:370-377) returns after that failure with smbman still loaded, and the deferred update then reaches 832. smbman_ra smb_GetShareList (smb_fio.c:959-981) fails without a session. That setError replaces the earlier message is inferred from host.cpp:86 (setErrorMessageWithCode), not traced further.

findings.title: Theme reloads can run out of font slots: new theme's fonts load before the old theme's are released (15 slots, up to 16 fonts per theme)
findings.problem: fntLoadFile takes the first free slot of 1..15 (slot 0 is the default font) and the language fallback font holds one. thmLoad loads all the new theme's fonts (up to THM_MAX_FONTS = 16) while the old theme still holds its own, and releases those only at publish. A theme with 8 or more font files, or two consecutive themes whose fonts add up to more than 14, gets FNT_ERROR for the rest: those keys silently fall back to fonts[0] after a view switch, Widescreen or language reload, and each such TTF is still read whole from the device and then freed.
findings.fix: Lower THM_MAX_FONTS to 7 so old + new + fallback always fit the 15 slots, or, if themes really use more fonts, raise FNT_MAX_COUNT to 2 * THM_MAX_FONTS + 2.
findings.benefit: Font choice no longer changes across reloads for font-heavy themes and no wasted TTF reads; lowering the constant also shrinks theme_t by 36 bytes (9 ints)
findings.evidence: FNT_MAX_COUNT = 16 (fontsystem.h:21); FontSystem::loadFile scans i = 1..FNT_MAX_COUNT-1 for !isValid and frees the buffer when none is free (fntsys.cpp:472-484); loadFallback uses loadFile (fntsys.cpp:451) and is called from lang.cpp:438. thmLoadFonts loops fntID < THM_MAX_FONTS = 16 (themes.h:9) and calls fntLoadFile per key (themes.cpp:1159); the old theme's fonts are released by thmFree(curT) at themes.cpp:1843 after the new ones are loaded (1576). No theme cfg in the repo uses font5 or higher (grep '^font([5-9]|1[0-5])='), so the trigger is limited to third-party themes with many fonts.

findings.title: appLookupByStartup scans the whole list linearly after every hash-table miss
findings.problem: The hash table holds every app with a non-empty startup, so a completed probe sequence that misses proves no row matches; the linear loop at 578-581 is only needed when the table could not be allocated, yet it runs on every miss (art worker path via image()).
findings.fix: Run the linear scan only when appArtLookupTable is NULL (make it the else branch).
findings.benefit: Removes an O(n) strcmp pass per art miss; ~0 lines
findings.evidence: Read appBuildArtLookup 520-558 (only empty startups skipped) and appLookupByStartup 560-584. An empty-startup row has artMode -1 (appSetArtSource 475-478), so image() returns -1 either way for value "".

findings.title: disc_key.h defines sysReadDiscKey as static inline with static RPC buffers, so two translation units each get their own copy
findings.problem: The header is included and called in system.cpp and sysdisc.cpp, so the function body and its 64-byte request and 64-byte response buffers (both 64-byte aligned statics) are emitted twice in the main ELF.
findings.fix: Make sysReadDiscKey an ordinary function defined once (for example in sysdisc.cpp) and leave only its prototype and the libcdvd externs in disc_key.h.
findings.benefit: 128 B .bss (2 x 64-byte static arrays, INFERRED) plus one copy of a ~20-line function (~100-150 B .text, INFERRED); no lines removed.
findings.evidence: git grep disc_key.h: src/platform/sysdisc.cpp:7, src/platform/system.cpp:7 (and the host test test_disc_key_semaphore.py:14, which compiles the header and would need the definition too). git grep -w sysReadDiscKey: system.cpp:527, sysdisc.cpp:230. INFERRED part: that the compiler does not merge the two copies (no LTO in ps2.yaml).

findings.title: freeze_diag.c shutdown_cd copies only .server, so the shutdown argument is DMAed to IOP address 0
findings.problem: shutdown_with_deadline fills the second client with shutdown_cd.server = igr_cd.server only. ps2sdk SifCallRpc sends the argument to cd->buf (the server buffer address that SifBindRpc stores in the client), which stays NULL here, so the 4-byte argument goes to IOP address 0 and cbrpc_shutdown (cdvdfsv.c:244) reads whatever its buffer last held. It works today only because the preceding FREEZE_DIAG_RPC_FNO call left 0 in that buffer; the IOP is rebooted right after.
findings.fix: Copy the whole bound client (shutdown_cd = igr_cd) instead of only the server pointer, so buf and cbuf come along.
findings.benefit: The shutdown argument reaches the server and no stray SIF write lands at IOP address 0; INGAMEDIAG builds only; no size change (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read freeze_diag.c:156-246 (igr_cd bound at :164, shutdown_cd never bound, only .server copied at :213, call at :216 with &shutdown_arg). cdvdfsv.c:173 registers shutdown_rpcbuf for 0x80000598; :232-238 the fno 2 path returns without touching buf; :241-248 fno 1 reads *(int *)buf. INFERRED: ps2sdk SifCallRpc passes cd->buf as the send destination (SDK source is not in the repo). Built only in the ingamediag configuration (tools/build_configuration.py:57-78).

findings.title: Select on an image-opened achievements page skips achievementsForget, so the cached library and HTTPS 'unreachable' latch are reused
findings.problem: achievements.cpp says Select (achievementsForget) retries the online lookup and refetches, but the Select handler for a card page whose target is still 'image' (any non-READY state, e.g. ACH_NOT_PLAYED after an HTTPS failure) only calls achievementsRequestImage. loadXerabora then re-hashes the ISO, skips HTTPS because xeraHttpsUnreachable is still set, and xeraFetch returns the cached library because xeraStale is 0, so the 'Select refreshes this page' prompt can never change the result in that session.
findings.fix: Call achievementsForget() before achievementsRequestImage/achievementsRequestVcd in the image branch of the Select handler (menusys.cpp:1225-1229).
findings.justification: One added call makes the image-page refresh do what the on-screen prompt and the achievements.cpp comment promise; no new state.
findings.benefit: Refresh on a NOT_PLAYED/UNSUPPORTED card page actually refetches (RA editions, Xerabora mode); +1 line.
findings.evidence: Read menusys.cpp:1072-1090 (menuOpenAchievements sets achTarget 'image'), :1128-1129 (target replaced by gameId only in READY with gameId>0), :1224-1233 (image branch has no achievementsForget; the other branch does). achievements.cpp:519-527 latches xeraHttpsUnreachable, :425-426 cache hit, :612-616 library fallback, :618-623 NOT_PLAYED with gameId 0. lng/tmpl/_base.yml:1944-1945 CAD_BACK_REFRESH text. The host test .github/scripts/test_ra_xerabora_browser.py:268 models Select as achievementsForget before the image request.

findings.title: TarEntryCfg/TarEntryCht declare filename[20] but the parser writes 24 bytes; names loaded from the sidecar are never re-terminated
findings.problem: nameMax = entrySize - sizeof(TarEntryBase) - 1. For the CFG/CHT entries that is 40 - 16 - 1 = 23 (sizeof is 40 because of the u64 member, INFERRED alignment), so strncpy writes 23 chars and a NUL at [23] into a filename[20]. tar.h:41-49 documents and fixes exactly this for TarEntryArt but not here, and the CHT kind is live (supportbase.cpp:1761). Separately, tarReadCache rejects a corrupt rawSize but never terminates names, so a damaged *_cache.bin makes tarFind's strcasecmp/strrchr read past the entry, and past the heap block for the last one.
findings.fix: Declare filename[24] in TarEntryCfg and TarEntryCht (sizeof stays 40). In the existing validation loop of tarReadCache also set the name byte at nameMax to 0.
findings.justification: The added line in tarReadCache sits in the loop that already rejects corrupt rawSize from the same untrusted sidecar. It is the smallest way to bound the string scans that follow.
findings.benefit: Removes an out-of-declared-bounds write on every CHT/CFG entry and an OOB read on a corrupt sidecar (READ; practical impact small)
findings.evidence: tar.h:31-36 TarEntryBase {u64, u32, u32} = 16 bytes; tar.h:53-63 filename[20]; tar.cpp:59-63 entrySize = sizeof(TarEntryCfg/Cht); tar.cpp:254 nameMax; :358-359 strncpy + fname[nameMax] = 0. tarReadCache tar.cpp:144-176 reads entries raw and checks only rawSize. Name scans: tar.cpp:492-497, 524-527, 548-552, 568-570. CHT live: supportbase.cpp:1761-1777. The sizeof of 40 assumes 8-byte u64 alignment (INFERRED for the EE ABI, matching the host test).

findings.title: askPc keeps broadcasting every RAG1 chunk request in Xerabora discovery mode and accepts each chunk from any responder
findings.problem: Without a companion IP, pcTarget leaves `to` as 255.255.255.255 and askPc never narrows it after RAQ1 answers, so all chunk requests are broadcast and ask() accepts each reply from whichever host answers first (the source filter applies only to unicast). With two xeRAbora PCs on the LAN holding different versions of a set, chunks of the same index and length from different PCs can be stitched into one list that passes the length checks.
findings.fix: After raqAsk returns 0, if `to` is the broadcast address set to.sin_addr.s_addr = replyIP_ so the chunk requests go to, and are only accepted from, the PC that confirmed the game.
findings.justification: Adds one line; it closes the mixed-source list case and stops broadcasting up to 23 chunk requests per check, and it is the smallest change that ties the transfer to one peer.
findings.benefit: Chunked watch list comes from one verified PC; fewer broadcast datagrams (INFERRED). No size change.
findings.evidence: Read ranet.cpp:309-352 (source check only when to is not INADDR_BROADCAST), 515-523 (Xerabora without hostIsExplicit returns 0 with broadcast target), 548-766 (to is not modified between raqAsk at :585 and the chunk loop at :658-693; rememberPeer uses the last replyIP_ at :710). Chunk acceptance checks only index and expected length (:673, :685). The two-PC scenario is a reasoned case, not observed.

findings.title: Cut then Paste of a .psu onto a memory card unpacks it but leaves the .psu in place and drops it from the clipboard
findings.problem: In fmPaste the .psu-onto-card branch runs vmcSavesPsuToFolder whether the clipboard is Copy or Cut. With Cut, a successful unpack counts as done, so the entry is removed from the clipboard (line 479), but the source .psu is never deleted, which contradicts HINT_FM_CUT ('Paste here moves them'). The user sees a move that was really a copy.
findings.fix: When fmClipCut is set, delete the source .psu after a successful unpack (one fmDelete call); otherwise leave the entry on the clipboard.
findings.justification: The single added call makes Cut behave as its hint promises; the alternative of documenting the exception would add more text than code.
findings.benefit: Correct Cut semantics for .psu onto a memory card; no data loss today, only an unexpected leftover file
findings.evidence: Read guifilemgr.cpp:428-485: branch at 449 has no fmClipCut test and calls only vmcSavesPsuToFolder; keep logic 469-479 keeps only failed entries. lng/tmpl/_base.yml:2331-2333 HINT_FM_CUT text. vmcSavesPsuToFolder (vmcsaves.cpp:1171-1174) is a vsCopy from the .psu to a folder and never removes the source.

findings.title: hddDvrScan publishes its full 128-entry candidate array (44 KB) whatever the ISO count
findings.problem: Each DVR scan callocs HDD_DVR_MAX_ISOS records and, when any directory was readable, publishes that allocation as the live list even when count is 0 or a handful. The memory stays held until the next scan or teardown.
findings.fix: Before hddDvrPublish, shrink candidate to count with realloc, or free it and publish NULL when count is 0.
findings.justification: Adds one or two lines. It returns about 44 KB of EE heap for the life of the session on a DESR with the DVR view enabled, where the list is usually empty or short.
findings.benefit: Up to 45,056 bytes of EE RAM returned (INFERRED: sizeof(hdd_dvr_iso_t) = 128 + 224 = 352 bytes x 128). Applies only to DESR hardware with gEnableDVR.
findings.evidence: Read hddsupport.cpp 64-76 (hdd_dvr_iso_t = hdl_game_info_t + char path[224]), 128-137 (publish keeps the pointer), 217-274 (calloc of 128 entries, published as-is when available > 0). hdl_game_info_t is 128 bytes (include/hddsupport.h:19-32 with APA_IDMAX 32). The scan runs on every HDD update (hddsupport.cpp:1884), gated by gEnableDVR and the SPD DVR capability bit (82-86, 94-101).

findings.title: ImageCache::requestFinished decrements activeRequests_ without protection against the GUI thread's increment
findings.problem: activeRequests_ is the guard that stops cacheDestroyCache freeing content[] under an in-flight request. The art thread (priority 72) does a plain volatile read-modify-write decrement with interrupts enabled; the vsync interrupt wakes the GUI thread (priority 31), which preempts it and may run activeRequests_++ for the same cache before the decrement is stored. The increment is then lost, the counter under-counts for the rest of the cache's life, and a later theme switch can free content[] while a request still points into it.
findings.fix: Do the decrement inside a DIntr()/EIntr() bracket in requestFinished (or inside gArtQ.release's existing bracket); the GUI-side increment cannot be preempted by the lower-priority art thread and needs nothing.
findings.justification: Two lines close a lost-update race on the only guard against the theme-switch use-after-free that texcache.h:125-133 describes; the code already uses the same DIntr bracket for its queue counters.
findings.benefit: Removes a rare race that defeats the use-after-free guard (INFERRED window: about two instructions per completed request against a 60 Hz interrupt). No size change.
findings.evidence: Read texcache.h:101-107,125-134; texcache.cpp:520 (GUI thread increments directly; requestQueued has no caller: grep -rn requestQueued src include gives only texcache.h:101). grep requestFinished: artload.cpp:370 (artFreeChain) and :386 (artReleaseRequest), both outside the DIntr sections per artload.cpp:342-348. Priorities: ART_THREAD_PRIORITY = 72 (artload.cpp:31,840), GUI 31 (brief, opl.cpp:2064). renderman.cpp:195-209 wakes the GUI thread from the vsync interrupt. The compiled instruction window is INFERRED.

findings.title: Overscan read from the settings file is never clamped; >= 1000 makes displayWidth_ 0 and unScaleX divides by zero
findings.problem: The dialog limits Overscan to 0..100 (dialogs.cpp:1087), but settingsLoad and screenPosLoad copy overscan and overscan_N from the cfg file unchecked, and setOverscan uses the value as is. With overscan >= 1000 (a hand-edited or damaged settings_riptopl.cfg) displayXOff_ reaches half the width, displayWidth_ becomes 0 or negative, and every text measurement through rmUnScaleX divides by it (a divide-by-zero trap on GCC MIPS builds, INFERRED) on every boot until the file is fixed.
findings.fix: Clamp overscan to 0..100 at the top of Renderer::setOverscan.
findings.justification: One clamp at the single consumer covers both cfg keys and the dialog; it turns an unrecoverable boot fault from a bad cfg value into the nearest valid setting.
findings.benefit: Removes a boot-time crash/garbage layout from an out-of-range cfg value (INFERRED). Trigger needs a hand-edited file, so rated low.
findings.evidence: grep -rn gOverscan src include: settings.cpp:88 (intSetting load), :263/:273 (per-mode store/recall), guisettings.cpp:2582-2585,2733 (dialog), renderman.cpp:360 (setMode -> setOverscan). screenPosLoad settings.cpp:294-305 loads overscan_N unchecked. renderman.cpp:800-803: displayXOff_ = (W-baseW)/2 + baseW*overscan/2000, displayWidth_ = W - 2*displayXOff_; :784-787 divides by displayWidth_. rmUnScaleX callers: fntsys.cpp:806,960,977, dia.cpp:81,139 and others. GCC MIPS -mcheck-zero-division default is INFERRED.

findings.title: cuePrepareLaunch skips the 256-byte argv pool check for a folder launch, so an over-long Ember argv is refused only after deinit
findings.problem: The pool check (2*strlen(emberElf)+strlen(argument)+3 > 256) runs only after a discs.txt manifest; with no manifest line 313 returns 1 first. Over SMB the ELF path is up to 52 chars (smb0: + 31-char ETH prefix + EMBER/ember.elf), NFS 56, so a folder name of 150-160 chars (allowed by the scan cap ISO_GAME_NAME_MAX, cuesupport.cpp:502) exceeds the pool; sysLoadELFKeepIOP then refuses after host::app().deinit has already torn the menu down.
findings.fix: Apply the existing pool check on the no-manifest path too (run it before returning 1 at line 313), so the message is shown while the GUI is still live.
findings.justification: The check already exists; it only has to cover the second return path. The concrete problem is a refused handoff after teardown, which leaves the user with no menu.
findings.benefit: Turns a post-teardown launch failure into an on-screen message for long names on network prefixes; about 2 lines moved/added.
findings.evidence: Read cuesupport.cpp:300-344 and the callers' order: ethsupport.cpp:1071 (cuePrepareLaunch) then 1094-1095 (deinit UNMOUNT_EXCEPTION, sysLaunchEmber); same order in bdmlaunch.cpp:88/117, hddsupport.cpp:2211/2230, mmcesupport.cpp:1219/1239, udpfssupport.cpp:850/866. sysLaunchEmber passes argv {emberElf, folder} (system.cpp:1278-1302); pool = strlen(filename)+1 + each argv+1 (elfldr_noreset.cpp:190-205) = 2L+F+3. Lengths: EMBER_FOLDER_DEFAULT/EMBER_ELF_NAME (cuesupport.h:113-114), gETHPrefix[32] (opl.h:501), prefix built at ethsupport.cpp:380-383. What the menu does after a refused handoff post-deinit is inferred, not traced.

findings.title: lngGetFilePath(0) reads languages[-1]; the language popup calls it with the current id, which can be 0
findings.problem: Notifications::check only ever sets showLang_ (never clears it), and show() re-reads lngGetGuiValue() every frame for 5 s and passes it to lngGetFilePath, which indexes languages[langID - 1] with no check. Pick a language in Settings (popup armed), then switch back to English within the 5 s: guiLangID is 0, lngGetFilePath reads the word before the heap array as a char * and snprintf %s dereferences it (garbage text or an EE exception).
findings.fix: Return NULL from lngGetFilePath for langID < 1 and skip the language line in show() when it is NULL (as the theme line already does via thmGetFilePath at guinotify.cpp:29).
findings.justification: Two-line guard; the concrete problem is an out-of-bounds pointer read reachable from the Settings language switch.
findings.benefit: Removes a rare menu crash path; no size change.
findings.evidence: Read lang.cpp 481-526 (lngSetGuiValue sets guiLangID = 0 for English), 550-556 (no bound). guinotify.cpp 21-38 (check sets showLang_ only when id != 0, never resets it), 96-108 and 134-140 (show re-reads lngGetGuiValue per frame), 148 (5 s window). opl.cpp:357-360 calls guiCheckNotifications(0, langChanged) after a language change; settingsio.cpp:2521 is the Settings path. grep lngGetFilePath: only guinotify.cpp:135 calls it.

findings.title: cacheGlyph runs one or two FreeType cmap lookups for every non-ASCII character on every draw and measure once a fallback font is loaded
findings.problem: The fallback test (two FT_Get_Char_Index calls) runs before the glyph-cache lookup, so a cached glyph still pays it on every renderString and calcDimensions call. fntRenderStringFit measures a string several times a frame. This runs on the GUI thread whenever the optional font_CJK/font_Japanese file was found (lngInitFallbackFont), for every character >= 0x80: every CJK glyph of a CJK UI font, and twice for every CJK game title character drawn from the fallback.
findings.fix: In cacheGlyph, return the active font's own valid entry first, then the fallback font's valid entry for the same codepoint. A fallback entry only becomes valid through this redirect, and every font load flushes all caches. Only on a miss in both, run the two cmap lookups as now.
findings.justification: It adds one extra cache probe (~3 lines) to remove up to two cmap binary searches per character per pass on the GUI thread. It is the smallest change that makes cached glyphs free.
findings.benefit: Removes ~1-2 FT_Get_Char_Index binary searches per drawn or measured CJK character per frame (INFERRED ~0.5-1 us each, so ~0.5-2 ms per frame on a CJK game list). Applies only when the fallback font exists.
findings.evidence: Read fntsys.cpp:581-638: fallback condition at 586-591 is evaluated before glyphPageOk / isValid at 598-610. fallbackFontId_ is set only by loadFallback (fntsys.cpp:442-459), called only from lngInitFallbackFont (lang.cpp:424-441), which opl.cpp:1741 calls at boot. The fallback slot id is never returned to callers, so its entries become valid only via this redirect. Every loadFile/loadDefault flushes all fonts (fntsys.cpp:409, 669-675). The per-lookup cost is INFERRED, not measured.

findings.title: games.bin records are trusted unvalidated; strcpy at launch copies a possibly unterminated startup into filename[32]
findings.problem: hddLoadGameListCache derives the record count from the file size, ignoring any remainder, and publishes the raw bytes as hdl_game_info_t without terminating partition_name, name or startup. The native launch then does strcpy(filename[32], game->startup). A truncated, corrupted or foreign-layout games.bin can carry an unterminated startup. The copy then runs through the following flag, LBA and size bytes and can write past the 32-byte stack buffer.
findings.fix: Use snprintf(filename, sizeof(filename), "%s", game->startup) at 2787. In hddLoadGameListCache, reject a file whose size is not a whole number of records, and force a NUL at the end of the three string fields of each loaded record.
findings.justification: Adds about 4 lines. games.bin is a file on the user's disk that is read back as raw structs and reaches an unbounded strcpy. The size check and three terminators close that path at the one place the file enters the program.
findings.benefit: Closes a stack overflow reachable from a corrupt cache file. Applies only with the opt-in cache enabled (INFERRED: overflow needs at least 32 non-zero bytes from offset 98 of a record).
findings.evidence: Read hddsupport.cpp 3097-3144 (no remainder check, no termination) and 2572-2833 (filename[32], strcpy at 2787). include/hddsupport.h:19-32: startup[13] sits at offset 98 of a 128-byte record, followed by flags, layer_break, start_sector and total_size_in_kb. Writers terminate the strings (platform/hdd.cpp:131-136), so a valid file is safe. INFERRED: how likely a corrupt file is (for example a write-back PFS mount losing power mid-write).

findings.title: Unchecked malloc/calloc in theme element init (initMutableText, initImageTexture, initMutableImage, initBasic, initItemsList and others)
findings.problem: These allocations are written through immediately with no NULL check, so an allocation failure during a theme (re)load is a NULL write and a crash rather than a disabled element. The same file does check in initGameCountText (509-519), thmParseDeviceList (79-81) and thmWallpaperLoad (1766-1768), and coverflow.cpp:360 / grid.cpp:674 test initMutableImage's result for NULL, which it can never return because it dereferences the malloc result first.
findings.fix: Return NULL on allocation failure from initImageTexture, initImageInternalTexture (their callers already treat NULL as no texture) and initMutableImage (Coverflow/Grid already handle NULL; add the same early return in initStaticImage, initGameImage, initAttributeImage and initBackground). Leave initBasic/initItemsList as they are unless addGUIElem is changed too.
findings.justification: A theme reload happens mid-session (view switch, settings change) while art caches hold the heap; a NULL write there takes the menu down. Only a few early returns are added, and they make the existing NULL guards in coverflow.cpp and grid.cpp reachable.
findings.benefit: Crash becomes a disabled element under OOM at theme load; about 10 lines added. Failure of these small allocations is unlikely (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read every cited allocation: 211 malloc then field writes 212-217; 226 malloc then memcpy 227; 275 calloc then snprintf 277/279; 703 calloc then write 704; 723 malloc then memcpy 724; 767/774 same; 810 malloc then writes 811-826; 1608 malloc then writes 1610-1622; 2123 malloc then itemsListFit write at 2131. Callers: themes.cpp:687-801 (addGUIElem) deref elem after initBasic; coverflow.cpp:356-360 and grid.cpp:671-674 check the initMutableImage result.
